children.title: Fine-Grained Iteration
children.top_down_role: Iteration organized around smaller propagation work units.

knowledge_statements.title: Fine-Grained Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-propagator scheduling reacts immediately to each effective store reduction through a sound invalidation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a store \(D^0\) from a finite store lattice, a finite family \(F\) of contracting, monotone, solution-preserving propagators, and a sound update operator \(U\). Initialize \(D=D^0\) and a queue \(Q\) containing every member of \(F\). While \(Q\ne\varnothing\), remove one \(f\in Q\), save \(D_{\mathrm{old}}=D\), and set \(D=f(D_{\mathrm{old}})\). Report failure if a domain in \(D\) is empty. If \(D\ne D_{\mathrm{old}}\), enqueue every propagator in \(U(f,D_{\mathrm{old}},D)\); otherwise enqueue nothing. The update operator is sound when every propagator that can fail to be at fixpoint after the change, including \(f\) when necessary, is either already queued or returned by \(U\). Stop when \(Q=\varnothing\) and output \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Execute one queued propagator at a time and, after every effective reduction, queue all propagators whose stability may have been invalidated, including the selected propagator when necessary.
assumptions_latex: The store lattice and propagator family \(F\) are finite.
Every propagator in \(F\) is contracting, monotone, and solution-preserving.
The update operator \(U\) soundly covers every possible stability invalidation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates; on termination without failure, \(f(D)=D\) for every \(f\in F\).

notation.meaning: Sound set of propagators to enqueue after f changes the store.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound fine-grained chaotic iteration requires complete invalidation scheduling

children.title: Granularity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Scheduling overhead, redundancy, plus responsiveness across iteration granularities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure Equivalence Does Not Imply Runtime Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on conclusions obtainable from schedule-independent closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: D_g^*=D_{g'}^*\ \centernot\Rightarrow\ T_g(I)\le T_{g'}(I).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two fair granularities can compute the same closure yet reverse their runtime ordering across instances because one incurs more redundant executions and the other more scheduling events.
assumptions_latex: The schedules are fair and apply the same contracting monotone propagators.
Execution and scheduling operations may have different positive costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists\text{ an instance-independent runtime ordering implied solely by closure equivalence.}
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Equivalence Does Not Imply Runtime Dominance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational accounting for propagation granularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: T=\sum_{e\in E}c(e)+C_{\mathrm{schedule}}+C_{\mathrm{invalidate}}. Coarser work units may reduce scheduling costs while increasing redundant propagator executions; finer work units may do the converse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Granularity trades redundant propagation against queueing, invalidation, and dependency-maintenance costs.
assumptions_latex: Runtime is attributable to propagator executions and scheduling operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Propagation cost is not generally monotone in work-unit granularity.}
knowledge_statements.title: Granularity Cost Decomposition
Granularity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates fixpoint equivalence from schedule-dependent propagation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be finite contracting, monotone propagators on a finite store lattice. Any fair coarse-, fine-, or hybrid-grained iteration beginning at the same store \(D^0\) reaches the greatest common fixpoint below \(D^0\), independent of execution granularity. Operational costs need not be ordered: coarse sweeps may execute already stable propagators, whereas fine scheduling incurs queue and dependency-maintenance overhead and may execute a propagator repeatedly after small changes. Therefore granularity preserves the closure under fairness but can change the numbers and costs of propagator invocations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair granularities compute the same closure, but batching, redundant executions, queue overhead, and incremental responsiveness produce instance-dependent runtime tradeoffs.
assumptions_latex: Propagators are contracting and monotone on a finite lattice.
Every propagator invalidated by a store change is eventually executed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The final common fixpoint is schedule-independent, while propagation work is generally schedule-dependent.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fair chaotic iterations share a closure but incur schedule-dependent work
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The schedule-independent closure and schedule-dependent work distinction fits Granularity Tradeoffs under fair iteration, but an authoritative fixpoint-iteration citation is absent.

children.title: Hybrid-Granularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Iteration structures combining multiple work-unit granularities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Omitted Block Invalidation Causes Premature Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete necessity of sound inter-block invalidation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the store be D\subseteq\{0,1,2\}. Define g(D)=D\setminus\{1\} and f(D)=D\setminus\{2\} if 1\notin D, otherwise f(D)=D. From D^0=\{0,1,2\}, executing f and then g yields \{0,2\}. If f is not requeued, the worklist can empty although f(\{0,2\})=\{0\}\ne\{0,2\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block may become unstable after another block changes the store; omitting that dependency can make an empty worklist falsely signal closure.
assumptions_latex: Blocks containing f and g are scheduled separately.
The invalidation rule omits the dependency from g's deletion to f.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q=\varnothing\ \centernot\Rightarrow\ \forall h\in F,\ h(D)=D\text{ without sound invalidation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Omitted Block Invalidation Causes Premature Termination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block representation and limiting granularities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hybrid regime consists of a partition \mathcal B=\{B_1,\ldots,B_s\} of F, an intra-block iteration rule, and an inter-block invalidation rule. Singleton blocks recover fine-grained scheduling; one block recovers coarse-grained iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid scheduling partitions propagators into blocks and coordinates local closure with inter-block invalidation.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal B is a disjoint exhaustive partition of F.

notation.meaning: Scheduled partition of the propagator family.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Regimes as Propagator Partitions
Hybrid-Granularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines block-local fixpoint computation with event-driven scheduling between propagator blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition a finite propagator family \(F\) into nonempty blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_s\). Initialize the store \(D=D^0\) and a worklist \(Q\) containing every block. Repeatedly remove a block \(B_j\), save \(D_{\mathrm{old}}=D\), and fairly apply members of \(B_j\) until \(f(D)=D\) for every \(f\in B_j\). Report failure if a domain becomes empty. If \(D\ne D_{\mathrm{old}}\), enqueue every block containing a propagator whose stability may have been invalidated by the change. Otherwise enqueue nothing. If the block-invalidation rule is sound, output \(D\) when \(Q\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schedule blocks by store changes, compute a common fixpoint within each selected block, and requeue every block whose propagators may have become unstable.
assumptions_latex: The store lattice and propagator family \(F\) are finite.
Every propagator is contracting, monotone, and solution-preserving.
Execution within each selected block reaches a common fixpoint for that block.
The block-invalidation rule soundly schedules every block whose stability may be invalidated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates; termination without failure yields \(f(D)=D\) for every \(f\in F\).

notation.meaning: A nonempty block of propagators handled at coarse granularity.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hybrid iteration requires block-local stability or retained unfinished work

children.title: Worklist Iteration
children.top_down_role: Propagation scheduling organized through explicit pending-work collections.

knowledge_statements.title: Worklist Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic chaotic iteration maintains explicit pending work until a common fixpoint is certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite store \(D^0\) and contracting, monotone propagators \(F\), initialize \(D=D^0\) and worklist \(W=F\). While \(W\ne\varnothing\), remove \(f\in W\), set \(D'=f(D)\), and stop with failure if \(D'\) contains an empty domain. When \(D'\ne D\), set \(D=D'\) and add to \(W\) every propagator that may cease to be at fixpoint after this change. When \(W=\varnothing\), output \(D\). A sound update rule makes absence from \(W\) imply stability at the current store.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain pending propagators explicitly, readding affected work after changes and terminating when no possibly unstable propagator remains.
assumptions_latex: The store lattice is finite.
The update rule schedules every propagator whose stability may be invalidated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates and outputs a common fixpoint or detects an empty domain.

notation.meaning: Set or queue of pending propagators.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard worklist formulation of finite chaotic iteration
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is a suitable generic worklist formulation with a sound invalidation rule, but it lacks an authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Event-Directed Iteration
children.top_down_role: Propagation scheduling activated by relevant information-state events.

knowledge_statements.title: Event-Directed Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain events select propagators registered as potentially affected by those event classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite family of contracting, monotone, solution-preserving propagators on a finite store lattice, let \(E\) be a set of domain-event types, and let \(M:E\to2^F\) map each event type to propagators that may become unstable when it occurs. Initialize \(D=D^0\) and a queue \(Q\) containing every member of \(F\). Repeatedly remove \(f\in Q\), set \(D_{\mathrm{old}}=D\), compute \(D_{\mathrm{new}}=f(D_{\mathrm{old}})\), and derive \(\Delta(D_{\mathrm{old}},D_{\mathrm{new}})\). Report failure if a domain in \(D_{\mathrm{new}}\) is empty. Otherwise set \(D=D_{\mathrm{new}}\) and enqueue \[\bigcup_{e\in\Delta(D_{\mathrm{old}},D_{bnew}})}M(e).\] Stop when \(Q\) is empty. If \(M\) covers every propagator invalidation caused by each event, an empty queue certifies a common fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserve the old and new stores while classifying a domain change, then awaken every propagator registered for an event that occurred.
assumptions_latex: The store lattice and propagator family \(F\) are finite.
Every propagator is contracting, monotone, and solution-preserving.
The event map \(M\) covers every propagator invalidation caused by each event type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates; on termination without failure, \(f(D)=D\) for every \(f\in F\).

notation.meaning: Events generated by the transition from the old store to the new store.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: event-directed worklist iteration must derive events from distinct pre-change and post-change stores

children.title: Event-to-Work Mapping
children.top_down_role: Associations between state changes and eligible propagation work.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition-quantified characterization of the pointwise least semantically sound event-to-work map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each event type \(e\), let \(T_e\) be its represented transition class and define \[\mu_{\min}(e)=\{p\in P:\exists(D,D')\in T_e,\ p(D)=D\ \text{and}\ p(D')\ne D'\}.\] For propagators not already pending, an event map \(\mu:E\to2^P\) sound for every represented transition must satisfy \(\mu_{\min}(e)\subseteq\mu(e)\) for every \(e\). Conversely, these inclusions ensure that every established fixpoint which some represented transition can invalidate is subscribed. Thus \(\mu_{\min}\) is the unique pointwise least sound map under this event abstraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An event type's least sound subscription contains exactly the propagators whose established fixpoint can be invalidated by some transition represented by that type.
assumptions_latex: Each event type \(e\) denotes a specified transition class \(T_e\).
A propagator already pending need not be added again.
Soundness requires every invalidated established fixpoint to remain or become pending.

notation.meaning: transitions represented by event type e

knowledge_statements.title: Least Sound Event Subscription

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite set of domain-change event types and \(P\) is a finite set of propagators.
Each emitted event soundly describes the domain transition that produced it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W^{+}=W\cup\bigcup_{e\in S}\mu(e)\) contains every propagator subscribed to an event in \(S\).

notation.meaning: events emitted by the latest transition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic subscription map for an event-driven propagation worklist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An event-to-work mapping is a function \(\mu:E\to 2^P\). When a domain transition emits the event set \(S\subseteq E\), the scheduler updates its worklist by \[W^{+}=W\cup\bigcup_{e\in S}\mu(e).\] Soundness requires that whenever a propagator \(p\in P\) can cease to be at a fixpoint solely because of a transition emitting \(e\), one has \(p\in\mu(e)\). The mapping may conservatively include additional propagators; these inclusions cause redundant work but do not invalidate propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mapping assigns each domain-change event all propagators that might require reconsideration; conservative extra assignments are sound but may create redundant work.
knowledge_statements.title: Event-to-Work Mapping

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and conservative-subscription condition fit the Event-to-Work Mapping leaf, and the mathematical notation is internally coherent. However, the record has no citation or inspectable locator supporting the event semantics, worklist update, or soundness condition.

children.title: Redundant-Wakeup Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Scheduling regimes in which event activation produces avoidable work.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-domain example in which omitting a relevant wakeup permits premature termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_x=D_y=\{0,1\}\). Define \(p\) to remove \(1\) from \(D_x\) when \(D_y=\{0\}\), and otherwise to do nothing. Let \(q\) enforce the unary restriction \(D_y\subseteq\{0\}\). Initially \(p(D)=D\). After executing \(q\), the store is \(D'=(\{0,1\},\{0\})\), and \(p(D')=(\{0\},\{0\})\subsetneq D'\). If the change made by \(q\) does not awaken \(p\), the worklist may become empty at \(D'\), although \(D'\) is not a common fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A domain event can invalidate a previously established propagator fixpoint; omitting that wakeup can make an empty worklist unsound.
assumptions_latex: The model includes the unary restriction on \(y\) enforced by \(q\).
The scheduler has removed \(p\) from pending work after observing its initial fixpoint.
The transition reducing \(D_y\) is permitted to omit \(p\) from pending work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: It is possible that \(W=\varnothing\) while \(p(D')\ne D'\).

notation.meaning: propagator producing the relevant domain event

knowledge_statements.title: Missed-Wakeup Nonfixpoint Example

assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a contracting propagator and \(D'\subseteq D\) is a domain transition.
Immediately before the transition, \(p(D)=D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Skipping the wakeup is semantically safe exactly when \(p(D')=D'\); otherwise it may miss required pruning.

notation.meaning: domains before and after an event
set of propagators awakened by event e

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semantic boundary between harmless and unsound omitted wakeups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a transition \(D'\subseteq D\) emitting \(e\), omitting \(p\) from \(\mu(e)\) is redundant for that transition exactly when \(p(D')=D'\). If instead \(p(D')\subsetneq D'\), the transition has invalidated the previous fixpoint of \(p\); omitting its wakeup can terminate propagation at a noncommon fixpoint. Thus syntactic event filtering is sound only when every skipped transition lies inside this semantic redundancy boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A wakeup is redundant precisely when the affected propagator remains at a fixpoint; skipping it outside that boundary can leave removable values.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Wakeup Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the exact equivalence is stated for one transition while membership in the event subscription map is normally determined for an event type across all transitions represented by that type. An authoritative source is required to determine the intended quantification and validate the claimed exact boundary.

On \(L=2^{\{a,b\}}\), ordered by inclusion, define \(f(X)=X\setminus\{a\}\) and \[g(X)= egin{cases}X,&a\in X,\X\setminus\{b\},&a
otin X.\end{cases}\] Both maps are monotone, contracting, and idempotent. For \(X=\{a,b\}\), \(g(X)=X\), whereas \(f(X)=\{b\}\) and \(g(f(X))=\varnothing
e f(X)\). Moreover, \(f\circ g
e g\circ f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a relation such as commutativity, running one propagator can invalidate another propagator that was previously at a fixpoint.
assumptions_latex: Stores are ordered by inclusion on the finite powerset lattice.
The scheduler suppresses \(g\)'s wakeup solely because \(g(X)=X\) before \(f\) runs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Monotonicity, contraction, and idempotence alone do not justify suppressing \(g\) after \(f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Noncommuting Wakeup-Suppression Counterexample

assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a finite poset and every operator in \(F\) is monotone, contracting, and idempotent.
The iteration applies operators fairly except for wakeups justified by commutativity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(g(x)=x\) and \(f\circ g=g\circ f\), then \(g(f(x))=f(x)\), so \(g\) need not be reawakened after applying \(f\).

notation.meaning: current store in the propagation order

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wakeup suppression for commuting idempotent propagation operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g\in F\). If \(g(x)=x\) and \(f\circ g=g\circ f\), then \[g(f(x))=f(g(x))=f(x).\] Hence applying \(f\) cannot invalidate the established fixpoint of \(g\), and a scheduler may omit \(g\) from the wakeups caused solely by that application. Repeating this rule while fairly scheduling every operator whose fixpoint may actually be invalidated preserves termination and the common fixpoint reached by ordinary fair iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A commuting propagator already at a fixpoint remains fixed after its partner runs, so its corresponding wakeup can be suppressed.
knowledge_statements.title: Commutativity-Aware Iteration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The commutativity calculation is coherent and the principle content kind fits the topic. The broader claim that repeated wakeup suppression preserves termination and the common fixed point requires an inspectable fixed-point iteration source specifying the fairness and operator assumptions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case cost under naive support scanning for every directed revision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\) be the number of variables, \(e\) the number of binary constraints, and \(d=\max_i|D_i^0|\). With \(O(d^2)\) work per directed revision, a complete sweep costs \(O(ed^2)\). Every changing sweep deletes at least one of at most \(nd\) values, and at most one final unchanged sweep is needed. Thus AC-1 takes \(O(ed^2(nd+1))=O(end^3)\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Naive AC-1 has quadratic domain work per arc per sweep and at most one changing sweep per deleted value, giving O(e n d cubed) worst-case time.
assumptions_latex: There are \(O(e)\) directed arcs.
A directed revision scans at most \(d\) candidates for each of at most \(d\) values.
No residual support cache is retained between sweeps.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Sweep Complexity of AC-1

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixpoint characterization of exhaustive full-sweep revision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite binary CSP, repeatedly applying every directed-arc revision until a complete sweep changes nothing terminates. If no domain becomes empty, the returned domains \(D^*\) form the greatest componentwise subdomain of the input domains that is arc-consistent. The result is independent of the order of revisions within the complete sweeps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-1 terminates at the unique greatest arc-consistent closure below the input domains, independently of within-sweep arc order.
assumptions_latex: All domains are finite.
Revision deletes exactly the values lacking support on its directed arc.
Every directed arc is revised in every completed sweep.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D^*=\operatorname{ACClosure}(D^0),\qquad D^*\text{ is independent of within-sweep ordering}.
knowledge_statements.title: AC-1 Closure Correctness

assumptions_latex: The input is a finite binary CSP with current domains \(D_i\).
Every directed constraint arc is examined by the revision operation during each sweep.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a detected empty domain or domains unchanged by revision on every directed arc.

notation.meaning: binary constraint between variables i and j
directed revision of domain i against domain j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical full-sweep formulation of the AC-1 family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the domains to the input domains. Repeatedly perform a complete sweep over every directed constraint arc \((i,j)\), replacing \(D_i\) by \[\{a\in D_i:\exists b\in D_j\text{ with }(a,b)\in C_{ij}\}.\] Stop immediately if some domain becomes empty. Otherwise stop after the first complete sweep that deletes no value, and return the resulting domains. Because every nonterminal sweep deletes at least one value, the procedure terminates on finite domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-1 repeatedly revises every directed arc in full sweeps until a sweep deletes nothing or some domain becomes empty.
knowledge_statements.title: AC-1 Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The full-sweep algorithm is a plausible AC-1 formulation and algorithm is the correct content kind, but no historical or authoritative source with a specific algorithm or section locator is supplied.

assumptions_latex: The binary CSP has finite domains and its variables are given a fixed total order.
Every deletion activates all earlier-stage arcs whose support may have been destroyed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After the last stage, every directed constraint arc is stable under revision, unless an empty domain was detected.

notation.meaning: current active set of directed arcs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered, staged characterization of the foundational AC-2 family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an ordering \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). Process the variables in order, seeding a work set \(Q\) with the directed arcs introduced by the current stage. Remove an arc \((i,j)\) from \(Q\), revise \(D_i\) against \(D_j\), and, whenever \(D_i\) shrinks, insert every already admitted arc whose support can depend on \(D_i\). Continue until the stage work set is empty, then admit the next variable. Stop on an empty domain; otherwise output the domains after all stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-2 organizes revision in ordered stages and revisits earlier arcs only when a deletion may have destroyed their supports.
knowledge_statements.title: AC-2 Family

The exact historical AC-2 variant cannot be validated or reconstructed reliably without a specific authoritative source.

children.title: Arc Revision
children.top_down_role: The value-filtering responsibility of an AC-3 arc revision.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Revision Idempotence Fails After Supporting-Domain Shrinkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary on fixed-supporting-domain idempotence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_i=\{a\}\), \(D_j=\{b,c\}\), and let \((a,b)\in C_{ij}\) be the only supporting pair. Revision initially retains \(a\), but after \(b\) is removed from \(D_j\), another revision deletes \(a\). Thus fixed-domain idempotence does not justify skipping revision after the supporting domain shrinks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Revision is idempotent only while the supporting domain is fixed; deleting the last support can make another revision necessary.
assumptions_latex: The supporting domain may shrink between revision calls.
knowledge_statements.title: Revision Idempotence Fails After Supporting-Domain Shrinkage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction, monotonicity, and fixed-supporting-domain idempotence of directed binary revision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For domains \(A\) and \(B\), define \(\rho_{ij}(A,B)=\{a\in A:\exists b\in B,\ (a,b)\in C_{ij}\}\). Then \(\rho_{ij}(A,B)\subseteq A\); if \(A\subseteq A'\) and \(B\subseteq B'\), then \(\rho_{ij}(A,B)\subseteq\rho_{ij}(A',B')\); and, for fixed \(B\), \(\rho_{ij}(\rho_{ij}(A,B),B)=\rho_{ij}(A,B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directed revision is contracting, monotone in both domain arguments, and idempotent while the supporting domain is unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The binary relation \(C_{ij}\) is fixed.
The supporting domain is unchanged between the two applications in the idempotence statement.
review_flags: Idempotence is conditional on the supporting domain remaining unchanged.

assumptions_latex: \(C_{ij}\subseteq D_i\times D_j\) is a binary constraint on finite current domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The revised domain is \(D_i'=\{a\in D_i:\exists b\in D_j,\ (a,b)\in C_{ij}\}\).

binary relation constraining i and j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed binary-constraint revision used by AC-3.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the directed arc \((i,j)\), inspect each \(a\in D_i\). Delete \(a\) exactly when no \(b\in D_j\) satisfies \((a,b)\in C_{ij}\). Equivalently, revision replaces \(D_i\) by \[D_i'=\{a\in D_i:\exists b\in D_j\text{ such that }(a,b)\in C_{ij}\}.\] It reports a change precisely when \(D_i'\subsetneq D_i\); it reports failure when \(D_i'=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arc revision removes exactly those values in the tail domain having no compatible value in the head domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Arc Revision

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The revision operation is precise, consistent with the leaf, and appropriately classified as an algorithm. It nevertheless lacks any cited source and specific locator supporting the directed-arc convention and revision specification.

children.title: Support Search
children.top_down_role: Discovery of supporting values during binary arc filtering.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-value cost of exhaustive support search over an explicitly enumerable neighboring domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(a\in D_i\), let \(m=|D_j|\). A sequential uncached search performs at most \(m\) tests of \((a,b)\in C_{ij}\). It therefore takes \(O(m\tau)\) time when each test costs \(O(\tau)\). It performs \(\Theta(m)\) tests when no support exists or the first support occurs last, and takes \(\Theta(m\tau)\) in those cases when each test costs \(\Theta(\tau)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncached support search uses one constraint test per examined candidate and has linear worst-case cost in the supporting domain size.
assumptions_latex: \(D_j\) is explicitly enumerable.
Each membership test in \(C_{ij}\) costs \(O(\tau)\); the matching time bound assumes \(\Theta(\tau)\) per test.
No index or cached support skips candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{search}}(a)=O(|D_j|\tau),\quad T_{\mathrm{search}}(a)=\Theta(|D_j|\tau)\text{ in the stated worst cases under uniform }\Theta(\tau)\text{ tests}.

notation.meaning: reference cost of one binary-constraint membership test

knowledge_statements.title: Uncached Support-Search Cost

assumptions_latex: \(a\in D_i\) and \(C_{ij}\subseteq D_i\times D_j\) is represented by a membership test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search succeeds with a support \(b\in D_j\) satisfying \((a,b)\in C_{ij}\), or certifies that no current support exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncached support search inside one directed arc revision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(a\in D_i\), enumerate candidates \(b\in D_j\) until finding one with \((a,b)\in C_{ij}\). Return the first such \(b\) as a current support. If every \(b\in D_j\) fails the constraint test, return failure; this failure is the certificate used by arc revision to delete \(a\). Without stored residual supports, a later revision begins this search again from the prescribed start of \(D_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support search scans the neighboring domain for a compatible value and reports failure only after all current candidates have been rejected.
knowledge_statements.title: Support Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uncached linear search is a coherent algorithm for this leaf. No inspectable source supports the scan convention, failure semantics, or claim that later revisions restart from the prescribed beginning of the neighboring domain.

children.title: Revision–Support Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependence of revision behavior on support-search organization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency condition governing when a directed arc can become newly inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_{ij}(a)=\{b\in D_j:(a,b)\in C_{ij}\}\). For every remaining \(a\in D_i\), if \(C_{ij}\) and \(D_j\) are unchanged, then \(S_{ij}(a)\) is unchanged. Hence revision of \((i,j)\) can become necessary only after \(D_j\) shrinks. A deletion from \(D_i\) instead may invalidate supports on directed arcs \((k,i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed arc can lose support only when its supporting endpoint shrinks; deleting from the revised endpoint may instead activate arcs supported by that endpoint.
assumptions_latex: \(C_{ij}\) remains fixed during propagation.
Domains change only by deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_j'=D_j\Longrightarrow S_{ij}'(a)=S_{ij}(a),\qquad D_j'\subsetneq D_j\Longrightarrow S_{ij}'(a)\text{ may become empty}.

notation.meaning: current supports in the domain of variable j for value a of variable i
directed arc revising the domain of i against the domain of j

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Revision Reactivation Condition

assumptions_latex: \(D_i\) and \(D_j\) are finite current domains linked by \(C_{ij}\).
Arc revision uses support-search failure as its deletion test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A value \(a\in D_i\) is deleted exactly when its support search in \(D_j\) fails; any deletion from \(D_j\) may invalidate searches for \(D_i\).

notation.meaning: support set of value a in the current domain of j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical coupling between support failure, value deletion, and renewed revision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(a\in D_i\), define \(S_{ij}(a)=\{b\in D_j:(a,b)\in C_{ij}\}\). Directed revision retains \(a\) exactly when \(S_{ij}(a)\neq\varnothing\), and deletes it exactly when the corresponding support search returns failure. Consequently, shrinking \(D_j\) can change a previously nonempty support set into the empty set and must reactivate revision of every relevant incoming arc \((i,j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Revision deletes a value exactly when support search fails, while deletions in a supporting domain can make previously successful searches fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Revision–Support Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-set property correctly expresses the local revision-support relationship and fits the property container. The scheduling consequence about reactivating every relevant incoming arc requires an authoritative AC-3 source with a specific locator.

children.title: Repeated-Search Costs
children.top_down_role: Cost exposure caused by rediscovering supports across revisions.

assumptions_latex: There are \(e\) directed arcs and every domain initially has at most \(d\) values.
Revision performs uncached linear support searches.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A revision costs \(O(d^2)\), and repeated revisions of one directed arc can cost \(O(d^3)\) over a closure computation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primitive repeated-search cost underlying the classical AC-3 bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under unit-cost membership tests for \(C_{ij}\), one revision examines at most \(d\) tail values and at most \(d\) candidate supports per tail value, hence costs \(O(d^2)\). A directed arc can be reactivated after successive deletions in its head domain, at most \(d\) times under the standard charging argument. With no residual-support memory, its accumulated support-search work is therefore \(O(d^3)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncached revision costs quadratic time per call and can accumulate cubic work on one arc through repeated support searches.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Search Costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the leaf and the per-call quadratic estimate is standard under the stated unit-cost model. The asserted per-directed-arc reactivation charge and accumulated cubic bound depend on the precise AC-3 worklist and arc-counting conventions, for which no source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Omitting an Affected Incoming Arc Can Return a Non-Arc-Consistent State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of requeueing every incoming arc whose supporting domain has shrunk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let equality constrain \(X_i\) with both \(X_j\) and \(X_k\), with \(D_i=D_k=\{0,1\}\) and \(D_j=\{0\}\). If \((k,i)\) is processed before \((i,j)\), it initially deletes nothing. Revision of \((i,j)\) then reduces \(D_i\) to \(\{0\}\). If \((k,i)\) is not requeued, the algorithm may terminate with unsupported value \(1\in D_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failing to requeue an incoming arc after its supporting domain shrinks can leave an unsupported value and terminate short of arc consistency.
assumptions_latex: The worklist may process \((k,i)\) before \((i,j)\).
Affected incoming arcs are not otherwise guaranteed another processing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Omitting an affected }(k,i)\text{ can make empty-queue termination non-arc-consistent}.
knowledge_statements.title: Omitting an Affected Incoming Arc Can Return a Non-Arc-Consistent State

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Why the Just-Revised Reverse Arc Need Not Be Requeued
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural justification for excluding the source neighbor in the standard AC-3 requeue rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose revision of \((i,j)\) deletes \(a\in D_i\) only when no \(b\in D_j\) satisfies \((a,b)\in C_{ij}\), with \(C_{ji}=C_{ij}^{-1}\). No deleted \(a\) supported any value of \(D_j\); therefore its deletion cannot newly invalidate \((j,i)\), and only \((k,i)\) for \(k\in N(i)\setminus\{j\}\) need be requeued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Values deleted while revising i against j supported no value of j, so their deletion cannot invalidate the reverse arc.
assumptions_latex: Revision deletes exactly the values of \(D_i\) having no support in \(D_j\).

notation.meaning: binary relation between variables i and j

knowledge_statements.title: Why the Just-Revised Reverse Arc Need Not Be Requeued

assumptions_latex: The input is a finite binary CSP with one directed arc for each revision direction.
Duplicate worklist entries are either suppressed or treated without affecting fairness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination returns failure on an empty domain or a domain family stable under every directed revision.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard directed-arc worklist organization for AC-3.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(Q\) with every directed constraint arc. Repeatedly remove \((i,j)\) and revise \(D_i\) against \(D_j\). If \(D_i\) becomes empty, return failure. If \(D_i\) shrinks, insert into \(Q\) every arc \((k,i)\) with \(k\in N(i)\setminus\{j\}\), since supports in \(D_i\) may have disappeared. When \(Q\) is empty, return the current domains. The choice of the next arc may be arbitrary provided pending arcs are eventually processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-3 keeps directed arcs in a worklist and requeues incoming neighboring arcs whenever revision shrinks their supporting domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Arc Worklist Organization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The directed-arc worklist algorithm fits the topic and is internally coherent under the usual binary-constraint conventions. A specific authoritative AC-3 algorithm locator is required to support the initialization, reverse-neighbor exclusion, duplicate handling, and termination claim.

children.title: AC-3 Closure
children.top_down_role: The propagation closure produced by the AC-3 family.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonempty AC-3 Closure Is Not a Satisfiability Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility limitation of binary arc-consistency closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Boolean variables \(x,y,z\) with pairwise disequality on the triangle, every directed arc already has support, so AC-3 terminates with every domain equal to \(\{0,1\}\). The network is nevertheless unsatisfiable. Thus an empty AC-3 closure is a sound inconsistency certificate, but a nonempty closure is not generally a satisfiability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-3 leaves the unsatisfiable Boolean disequality triangle unchanged, so nonempty closure does not prove feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The binary constraint graph is the three-cycle.
Every initial domain is \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonempty AC-3 Closure Is Not a Satisfiability Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness, Order Independence, and Idempotence of AC-3 Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural consequences of fair iteration to the common revision fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under finite domains and fair scheduling of the standard contracting monotone revision operators, the AC-3 closure below a fixed initial store is unique. Every fair processing order reaches that closure, and reapplying AC-3 performs no further deletion: \(F_{AC3}(F_{AC3}(D))=F_{AC3}(D)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair processing order changes intermediate work but not the final AC-3 closure, which is idempotent.
assumptions_latex: Domains are finite.
The revision semantics and rescheduling convention are fixed.
Every arc affected by a deletion is eventually reconsidered.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness, Order Independence, and Idempotence of AC-3 Closure

assumptions_latex: All domains are finite and revision is applied fairly until the worklist is empty.
The initial domains define the upper bound of the domain-reduction order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AC-3 returns the greatest common fixed point of all directed revision operators below the initial domains, or detects that this fixed point has an empty domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain greatest-fixpoint characterization of AC-3 closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_{ij}\) range over all directed revision operators and let \(D^0\) be the initial domain family. Fair AC-3 iteration terminates at a family \(D^*\preceq D^0\) satisfying \(R_{ij}(D^*)=D^*\) for every directed arc. Moreover, for every common fixed point \(F\preceq D^0\), one has \(F\preceq D^*\). Thus \(D^*\) is the greatest arc-consistent subdomain family obtainable without deleting a supported value; an empty component certifies inconsistency of this closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair AC-3 computes the greatest arc-consistent domain reduction below the initial domains, or discovers an empty domain.
knowledge_statements.title: AC-3 Closure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A theorem is appropriate for the closure characterization, but the greatest-common-fixed-point claim depends on the exact domain order, monotonicity of every revision operator, and fairness theorem. Those requirements are not fully sourced, and no inspectable fixed-point characterization is cited.

children.title: AC-3 Time Complexity
children.top_down_role: Runtime bounds across AC-3 algorithm variants.

assumptions_latex: The binary CSP has \(e\) directed arcs and maximum initial domain size \(d\).
Constraint compatibility tests and queue operations take constant time, and support searches are uncached.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The classical AC-3 closure computation uses \(O(ed^3)\) time in the worst case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical uncached-support worst-case bound with directed-arc counting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A call to directed revision performs at most \(O(d^2)\) compatibility tests. Each directed arc can be charged at most \(O(d)\) effective reactivations, because each relevant reactivation is associated with deletion of a value from its head domain. Summing over \(e\) directed arcs gives \[T(e,d)=O(ed^3).\] This is the classical AC-3 bound for naive support search; residual-support or specialized constraint representations can improve it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With naive support search, AC-3 spends quadratic time per revision, revises each directed arc at most linearly many times, and uses cubic domain-factor time overall.
knowledge_statements.title: AC-3 Time Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind exactly fits the leaf, and the stated classical naive-support bound is plausible. Its derivation depends on whether e counts directed arcs, the precise reactivation rule, and the charging argument; no authoritative source or specific complexity locator is provided.

children.title: AC-3 Space Complexity
children.top_down_role: Storage requirements across AC-3 algorithm variants.

knowledge_statements.title: AC-3 Space Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-space bound for queue-based AC-3 on a finite binary constraint network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\) be the number of variables, \(e\) the number of binary constraints, and \(d=\max_i|D_i|\). Represent the propagation queue as a set of directed arcs, so it contains at most \(2e\) entries. Excluding storage of the input constraint relations, AC-3 stores the current domains and the queue; hence its auxiliary space is \[O(nd+e).\] If the mutable domains are counted as part of the input state rather than auxiliary workspace, the additional workspace is \(O(e)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-3 stores current domains and at most two directed arcs per binary constraint, using O(nd+e) space, or O(e) workspace when domains are excluded.
assumptions_latex: \(n<\infty\), \(e<\infty\), and every domain has size at most \(d\).
Queue membership and each directed-arc entry occupy constant space.
The representation of binary relations is excluded from auxiliary space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{AC3}}=O(nd+e)\), with additional workspace \(O(e)\) when domain storage is excluded.
review_flags: Exact AC-3 space convention requires an authoritative constraint-programming source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the terminal container, and the stated convention is plausible, but no cited source or inspectable locator supports either the O(nd+e) auxiliary-space bound or the alternative O(e) workspace convention. The unrelated local inventory cannot establish this claim.

children.title: Complexity-Sensitive Variants
children.top_down_role: AC-3 family members distinguished by complexity-relevant organization.

knowledge_statements.title: Complexity-Sensitive Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Design principle separating closure correctness from scheduling and support-search costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider any AC-3 variant that repeatedly applies a sound revision operator and, after deleting values from \(D_j\), eventually schedules every neighboring arc \((i,j)\) whose validity may have changed. Queue discipline, duplicate suppression, residues, and specialized support search may alter time and space consumption, but not the terminal domains: upon quiescence the algorithm computes the greatest arc-consistent subdomains contained in the initial domains. Complexity must therefore be stated separately for revision calls, compatibility tests, and stored support information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound, fair AC-3 variants share the same arc-consistency closure; scheduling, cached supports, and specialized revision change only their resource profile.
assumptions_latex: All domains and the set of directed arcs are finite.
Each revision deletes exactly values lacking support in the current neighboring domain.
Every arc made potentially inconsistent is eventually processed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All such variants terminate at the same greatest arc-consistent domain reduction, although their time and space bounds may differ.

notation.meaning: directed constraint arc from variable i toward variable j

review_flags: Closure invariance and precise fairness hypotheses need a supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role is suitable for a variants container, but the closure-invariance assertion depends on exact soundness, fairness, and rescheduling hypotheses. No source or locator supports those hypotheses or the greatest-closure conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: AC-3.1 Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: AC-3 refinement exploiting information obtained while revising both directions of a binary constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite binary constraint network and initialize a queue with all directed arcs. When processing \((i,j)\), scan \(D_j\) for a support of each relevant \(a\in D_i\), deleting \(a\) if none exists. During these scans, retain admissible information useful for the reverse arc \((j,i)\), so reverse revision avoids compatibility tests already resolved by the same constraint traversal. After any deletion from \(D_i\), enqueue every affected arc \((k,i)\) with \(k\ne j\). Stop when the queue is empty or some domain is empty; output the resulting domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-3.1 refines AC-3 by reusing information gathered while checking one arc to reduce redundant work on its reverse arc.
assumptions_latex: The network is finite and all constraints are binary.
A compatibility test decides whether \((a,b)\) satisfies the relevant binary relation.
Queue processing is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is failure if some domain becomes empty; otherwise it is the arc-consistency closure of the input domains.
review_flags: The exact AC-3.1 data structures and reverse-arc reuse rule require primary-source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role for this family container, but the description of retaining information for reverse revision is too dependent on the canonical AC-3.1 formulation to validate without a primary source. No citation or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: AC-3rm Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residue-based AC-3 refinement retaining the most recently found support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every directed arc \((i,j)\) and value \(a\in D_i\), maintain a residue \(r_{ij}(a)\), initially undefined. On revision, keep \(a\) immediately if \(r_{ij}(a)\in D_j\) and \((a,r_{ij}(a))\in R_{ij}\); otherwise search \(D_j\) for a support \(b\). Set \(r_{ij}(a):=b\) when found and delete \(a\) otherwise. Propagate every deletion by scheduling affected incoming arcs. Terminate on an empty domain or an empty queue and return the resulting domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-3rm stores a residue for each value-arc pair and searches again only when that remembered support is no longer valid.
assumptions_latex: The binary constraint network and its domains are finite.
Residues are hints only and are validated against the current domain before reuse.
Every affected incoming arc is eventually revised.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates with failure or with the same arc-consistency closure as ordinary AC-3.

notation.meaning: remembered support of value a across arc (i,j)

review_flags: The canonical AC-3rm initialization and complexity claims require a primary source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the container, but the record may describe a generic residue-enhanced AC-3 scheme rather than the exact canonical AC-3rm family. A primary source is needed to confirm the residue indexing, validation rule, scheduling behavior, and closure claim.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional storage bound for a generic table containing one remembered support per directed-arc and initial tail-value pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If there are \(e\) directed arcs, every initial tail domain has size at most \(d\), and one constant-size residue \(r_{ij}(a)\) is stored for each directed-arc and initial-value pair, then the residue table occupies \(O(ed)\) space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One constant-size remembered support per directed-arc and initial tail-value pair uses O(ed) storage.
assumptions_latex: There are \(e\) directed arcs.
Each initial tail domain has cardinality at most \(d\).
Each residue entry or undefined marker occupies constant space.

notation.meaning: remembered support for value a on directed arc (i,j)

review_flags: The bound is correct conditionally, but the packet does not establish that this is the canonical AC-3rm representation rather than a generic residue scheme.
knowledge_statements.title: Residue-Table Storage Bound

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf should own canonical AC-3rm mechanics, correctness invariants, named variants, and family-specific resource bounds. The proposed residue claims are mathematically plausible but deferred because their canonical home may instead be generic support caching; AC-3.1 and ordinary AC-3 behavior were excluded.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stale Residues Are Not Current Support Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic correctness boundary for reuse of remembered binary supports after domain shrinkage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A remembered value \(r_{ij}(a)=b\) is a current support only if \(b\in D_j\) and \((a,b)\in R_{ij}\). If domain membership is not revalidated, a deleted last support may be reused and an unsupported value \(a\) may be retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A remembered support must still belong to the current neighboring domain; unchecked stale residues can make filtering unsound.
assumptions_latex: Domains may shrink after a residue is recorded.
Residues are not automatically invalidated when referenced values are deleted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{ij}(a)=b\not\Rightarrow b\in D_j;\quad b\notin D_j\text{ makes residue-only acceptance unsound}.
review_flags: This is a sound generic residue boundary, but canonical AC-3rm may use a different residue convention or invalidation discipline.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale Residues Are Not Current Support Certificates

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf should own canonical AC-3rm mechanics, correctness invariants, named variants, and family-specific resource bounds. The proposed residue claims are mathematically plausible but deferred because their canonical home may instead be generic support caching; AC-3.1 and ordinary AC-3 behavior were excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: AC-4 Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precomputed-support arc-consistency algorithm for extensional binary constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each directed constraint \(R_{ij}\), value \(a\in D_i\), and compatible \(b\in D_j\), record that \(a\) depends on \(b\), and initialize \(c_{ij}(a)=|\{b\in D_j:(a,b)\in R_{ij}\}|\). Enqueue and delete every \(a\) with some counter \(c_{ij}(a)=0\). Whenever a queued value \(b\in D_j\) is deleted, decrement exactly the counters of values recorded as supported by \(b\); newly zero counters trigger corresponding deletions. Stop when the deletion queue is empty or a domain is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-4 precomputes all supports, counts them, and propagates each value deletion by decrementing precisely the counters that depended on that value.
assumptions_latex: All domains are finite and constraints are binary extensional relations.
Each support pair is enumerated during initialization.
Each value deletion is processed at most once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns failure or the arc-consistency closure; with \(e\) constraints and maximum domain size \(d\), its standard worst-case time and support storage are \(O(ed^2)\).

notation.meaning: number of current supports for a in the domain of j

review_flags: AC-4 correctness and complexity require an authoritative algorithm source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is appropriate for the AC-4 family leaf, and the support-counter presentation is plausible. However, no source supports the exact initialization and deletion protocol or the combined O(ed^2) time and support-storage claims.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for decremental support-counter maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(c_{ij}(a)\) is initialized to \(|\{b\in D_j^0:(a,b)\in R_{ij}\}|\). Under elementary domain deletions and a fixed relation \(R_{ij}\), the invariant \[c_{ij}(a)=|\{b\in D_j:(a,b)\in R_{ij}\}|\] is preserved for every possible deletion sequence if and only if deleting a compatible value \(b\) causes exactly one decrement of \(c_{ij}(a)\), while deleting an incompatible value causes none. A missed decrement can leave a positive count after the last support disappears; an unwarranted or duplicate decrement can produce zero while a support remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact one-for-one accounting of deleted supports is required for a support counter to remain exact; missed and extra decrements cause opposite zero-test errors.
assumptions_latex: \(c_{ij}(a)\) is initialized from \(D_j^0\).
Domains change only through elementary value deletions.
\(R_{ij}\) remains fixed during maintenance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The test \(c_{ij}(a)=0\) is sound and complete for absence of support exactly under the stated update discipline.

notation.meaning: maintained support count for value a

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Update Boundary for Support Counters
Support-Counter Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant underlying counter-based propagation for binary arc consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every directed arc \((i,j)\) and surviving value \(a\in D_i\), maintain \[c_{ij}(a)=|\{b\in D_j:(a,b)\in R_{ij}\}|.\] If each deletion of \(b\in D_j\) decrements \(c_{ij}(a)\) once for every recorded pair \((a,b)\in R_{ij}\), then the equality remains invariant under monotone domain deletion. Consequently, \(c_{ij}(a)=0\) is a directly checkable certificate that \(a\) has no support across \((i,j)\) and must be deleted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support counter equals the number of currently surviving supports; reaching zero certifies that its value is arc-inconsistent.
assumptions_latex: Counters are initialized from the initial domains.
Domains only shrink during propagation.
Every deleted support causes exactly one decrement of each dependent counter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_{ij}(a)=0\) if and only if \(a\) has no current support in \(D_j\) under \(R_{ij}\).

notation.meaning: current support count for a across arc (i,j)

review_flags: No supplied locator supports the support-counter invariant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is an appropriate role for the maintenance invariant. The formula and zero-counter implication are internally coherent, but there is no cited evidence or inspectable locator for the invariant and its exact-decrement assumptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deletion-Event Bound for the Generic Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional representation-independent bound on queue events and handler notifications in monotone support-update propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_i^0=|D_i^0|\). In any monotone deletion framework that suppresses duplicate deletion events, at most \(\sum_i d_i^0\) distinct deletions are enqueued. If deletion of a value of \(x_j\) is delivered once to every affected directed handler, the number of notifications is at most \(\sum_j d_j^0\deg(j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under monotone deletion and duplicate suppression, each initial domain literal generates at most one deletion event and one notification per affected handler.
assumptions_latex: Domains are finite and change only by deletion.
Duplicate deletion events are suppressed.
Every affected handler is notified once per actual deletion.

notation.meaning: initial domain size of variable i
number of directed update handlers affected by deletion from variable j

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion-Event Bound for the Generic Framework
Generic Support-Update Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract AC-5 interface separating propagation control from constraint-specific support updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input finite domains and binary constraints. For each directed arc \((i,j)\), invoke a constraint-specific initialization routine that returns unsupported values of \(D_i\) and initializes support state. Place all returned deletions in a queue. When \(b\in D_j\) is deleted, invoke an update routine for every incident arc; it modifies that arc's support state and returns exactly those \(a\in D_i\) that have consequently lost their last support. Delete and enqueue each newly returned value. Stop at an empty domain or an empty queue, and output failure or the remaining domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-5 uses constraint-specific initialization and deletion-update routines inside a generic queue-based propagation loop.
assumptions_latex: Initialization identifies exactly the initially unsupported values.
Each update reports exactly the values losing their final current support.
Domains are finite and deletions are processed fairly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generic loop terminates and computes the arc-consistency closure independently of the internal support representation.
review_flags: The canonical AC-5 routine signatures and invariants require primary-source verification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the generic-framework container, but the stated initialization and update interfaces must be checked against the canonical AC-5 framework. No primary source or locator is provided, so the exact algorithm and closure claim remain unreliable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity Transfer for an AC-5 Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric runtime inherited from the initialization and deletion handlers of one constraint-specific instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a specialized instance incurs total initialization cost \(T_{\mathrm{init}}\), and let \(T_q\) be the total specialized-handler cost caused by deletion event \(q\). If each actual deletion is delivered once to every affected handler and queue operations take constant amortized time, then with \(M\) handler notifications the total time is \(O(T_{\mathrm{init}}+\sum_qT_q+M)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The runtime of a specialized AC-5 instance is its initialization and deletion-handler cost plus linear event-management overhead.
assumptions_latex: Domains are finite and shrink monotonically.
Each affected handler receives each actual deletion once.
Queue operations and duplicate-deletion checks take constant amortized time.

knowledge_statements.title: Complexity Transfer for an AC-5 Specialization
Constraint-Specialized AC-5 Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient interface conditions for a constraint-specific AC-5 instantiation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A binary constraint class admits a correct AC-5 instance when it supplies, for each directed constraint \(R_{ij}\): an initialization routine returning exactly \(\{a\in D_i:\nexists b\in D_j,\ (a,b)\in R_{ij}\}\), and an incremental routine that, after deletion of \(b\in D_j\), returns exactly the still-present values of \(D_i\) whose final support has thereby disappeared. Both routines may use any constraint-specific representation, provided their maintained state is consistent with the current domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A specialized AC-5 instance is valid when its initialization and deletion handlers report exactly the values that lack current support.
assumptions_latex: The constraint-specific state is initialized consistently with the input domains.
All domain changes are monotone deletions.
Each deletion event is delivered once to every affected handler.

The exact-reporting conditions are plausible, but their identification as the formal AC-5 specialization interface and the resulting closure conclusion require a direct source with a specific locator.

children.title: AC-6 Family
children.top_down_role: Incremental-support filtering variants derived from AC-6.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds induced by monotone successor searches and one dependency entry per directed arc-value pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(e\) binary constraints and maximum initial domain size \(d\), there are \(O(ed)\) directed arc-value pairs. Because each pair scans at most \(d\) support candidates in fixed order, AC-6 performs \(O(ed^2)\) compatibility tests. Storing one chosen support and one inverse dependency entry per pair requires \(O(ed)\) auxiliary space, excluding domains, queues, and constraint storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered successor searches give AC-6 O(e d squared) time, while chosen supports and inverse dependency lists use O(e d) auxiliary space.
assumptions_latex: The dependency-list and successor-search invariant holds.
Compatibility tests and list operations take constant time.
\(e\) counts binary constraints, giving \(O(e)\) directed arcs.
knowledge_statements.title: AC-6 Time and Auxiliary-Space Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency requirement when AC-6 state crosses backtracking restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After domains are restored during backtracking, the chosen-support map, dependency lists, and successor-search positions must be restored or rebuilt consistently. Reusing mismatched state can omit reconsideration after a chosen support is deleted or can skip a restored earlier support, so sound closure is no longer guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-6 support, dependency, and search-position state must be restored consistently with restored domains.
assumptions_latex: Search may restore previously deleted domain values.
Incremental AC-6 state may be retained across propagation episodes.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-State Restoration Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant linking chosen supports, inverse dependency lists, and amortized replacement search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each current \(a\in D_i\) and directed arc \((i,j)\), AC-6 records one current support \(s_{ij}(a)\in D_j\), and \((i,a)\) occurs on the dependency list keyed by \(b\) exactly when \(s_{ij}(a)=b\). When \(b\) is deleted, only its former dependents require replacement search. With a fixed order on \(D_j^0\), replacement search resumes strictly after \(b\); candidates preceding \(b\) were already rejected for this arc-value pair and cannot become supports while the relation is fixed and domains only shrink.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-6 inverse dependency lists identify exactly whose chosen support was deleted, and ordered successor searches never rescan earlier rejected candidates.
assumptions_latex: Binary relations remain fixed.
Domains change only by deletion during the propagation episode.
Dependency entries are moved consistently when replacement supports are installed.
Candidate domains have fixed orders and replacement search is exhaustive over later current candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (i,a)\in L_j(b)\iff s_{ij}(a)=b,\qquad\text{each arc-value pair examines each candidate at most once}.

dependency list keyed by supporting value b of variable j

knowledge_statements.title: AC-6 Dependency-List and Successor-Search Invariant
AC-6 Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental arc consistency using one current support and dependency lists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each directed arc \((i,j)\) and value \(a\in D_i\), maintain one current support \(s_{ij}(a)\in D_j\), when one exists, and place \(a\) on the dependency list of that support. When \(b\in D_j\) is deleted, reconsider only values listed as depending on \(b\); search for a replacement support, update the dependency list if found, and delete the value otherwise. Process resulting deletions until no dependency list is activated or some domain is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-6 keeps one support per value-arc pair and revisits a value only when its recorded support is deleted.
assumptions_latex: The network is finite and binary.
Support searches enumerate candidates without omitting any current support.
Dependency lists contain every value whose recorded support is their key.

children.title: AC-7 Family

knowledge_statements.title: AC-7 Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental arc consistency reusing support information across opposite arc directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a current support for each value-arc pair as in AC-6, together with records permitting a compatibility fact established while processing \((i,j)\) to serve the opposite direction \((j,i)\). When a recorded support is deleted, first consult reusable reciprocal information; if it supplies a surviving support, register it, otherwise search the relevant domain and delete the unsupported value. Propagate deletions through dependency lists until quiescence or domain failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-7 extends single-support propagation by reusing compatible pairs across opposite directions, reducing repeated constraint checks when reciprocal information is available.
assumptions_latex: Constraints are binary and compatibility information can be associated with both directed views.
Every reused support is checked to remain in the current domain.
All invalidated dependencies are eventually processed.

children.title: Support-Reuse Differences

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Reuse Differences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational distinction between AC-6 and AC-7 support reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the single-support scheme characteristic of AC-6, a record \(s_{ij}(a)=b\) certifies support only for \(a\) on the directed arc \((i,j)\), and deletion of \(b\) activates its dependent values. AC-7 additionally exploits the same compatible pair to inform support processing for the opposite directed arc whenever the constraint representation permits this reciprocal reuse. Thus both schemes invalidate supports on deletion, but AC-7 can avoid compatibility tests already answered in the reverse direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-6 reuses a support within one directed arc; AC-7 additionally reuses compatible-pair information across the reverse arc.
assumptions_latex: A binary constraint is processed through two directed arcs.
Recorded supports are invalidated when their supporting values leave the current domain.
Reverse-direction reuse preserves the orientation of each value pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AC-7 performs no more compatibility retesting than the corresponding AC-6 execution when reciprocal records are available, without changing the resulting closure.

notation.meaning: b is the recorded support of a on directed arc (i,j)

review_flags: The comparison depends on the canonical AC-6 and AC-7 formulations and needs a direct source.

children.title: Family Applicability Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Family Applicability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-based selection criterion for incremental-support arc-consistency families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite binary constraints, choose an incremental-support family according to the cost of finding, validating, and storing supports. A single-support method such as AC-6 is applicable when supports can be enumerated incrementally and dependency lists fit memory. AC-7 is advantageous only when compatibility facts can be reused safely between opposite directed arcs and repeated constraint tests are material. If neither incremental enumeration nor reciprocal reuse is available, correctness remains possible, but the intended efficiency advantage over generic revision is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-6 suits constraints with incremental support search; AC-7 is most useful when support facts can also be reused across reverse arcs.
assumptions_latex: The constraint network is finite and binary.
The comparison uses identical domains, constraints, and propagation semantics.
Implementations validate every cached support against current domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Applicability is determined by support-search structure and reusable compatibility information, not by a different notion of arc consistency.

notation.meaning: current finite domain of variable i
directed view of a binary constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time and auxiliary-space bounds for monotone ordered last-support searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e\) be the number of binary constraints and \(d\) the maximum initial domain size. For each directed arc-value pair, the last-support pointer advances monotonically through at most \(d\) candidates during one propagation episode. Across \(O(ed)\) such pairs, this gives \(O(ed^2)\) compatibility tests. The pointer table has \(O(ed)\) entries, so auxiliary space is \(O(ed)\), excluding domains, queues, and constraint storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotone last-support pointers give AC-2001 O(e d squared) time and O(e d) pointer storage in one propagation episode.
assumptions_latex: Domains only shrink during the propagation episode.
Each supporting domain has a fixed candidate order.
Compatibility tests and pointer updates take constant time.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for forward-only support pointers across state restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Resuming strictly after a previous last-support pointer is sound only while candidates skipped earlier cannot reenter the domain. If backtracking restores domain values, pointers must be restored to a compatible saved state or reinitialized; otherwise a restored support preceding the retained pointer may be skipped and a supported value may be deleted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward-only AC-2001 pointers require monotone deletion or compatible pointer restoration after backtracking.
assumptions_latex: Support candidates use a fixed order.
Backtracking may restore deleted domain values.

knowledge_statements.title: Last-Support Pointer Restoration Boundary
AC-2001 Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary arc-consistency filtering under monotone domain deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_{xy}\subseteq D_x^0\times D_y^0\) be binary, with current domains \(D_x,D_y\) and a fixed ordering of \(D_y^0\). For every \(a\in D_x^0\), store \(L[x,a,y]\), initially undefined. To revise \(D_x\) against \(D_y\), retain \(a\in D_x\) if \(L[x,a,y]\in D_y\) and \((a,L[x,a,y])\in C_{xy}\). Otherwise scan values of \(D_y\) following the previous pointer, or from the beginning if undefined, until finding \(b\) with \((a,b)\in C_{xy}\); then set \(L[x,a,y]:=b\). If none exists, delete \(a\). Repeat directed-arc revisions triggered by deletions until no domain changes or some domain is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-2001 enforces binary arc consistency by retaining a last support for each directed variable-value pair and resuming later support searches beyond invalidated supports.
assumptions_latex: \(D_x^0\) and \(D_y^0\) are finite and fixedly ordered.
Domains change only by deletion during one propagation episode.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, every remaining value has a support across every incident directed binary constraint, unless a domain is empty.

Cached last support of value a in the domain of y.
