knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounds Filtering and Binary Arc Consistency Are Incomparable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength boundary between global bounds filtering and arc consistency on pairwise disequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(D_1=D_2=\{1,2\}\) and \(D_3=\{1,2,3\}\), the Hall interval \([1,2]\) makes global bounds filtering set \(D_3=\{3\}\), while every binary disequality is arc consistent and performs no deletion. Conversely, with \(D_1=\{2\}\) and \(D_2=\{1,2,3\}\), arc consistency on \(x_1\ne x_2\) deletes the interior value 2 from \(D_2\), while bounds filtering need not alter its supported endpoints 1 and 3. Thus neither closure uniformly dominates the other on explicit domains with holes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global bounds filtering exploits multi-variable Hall intervals, while binary arc consistency can remove singleton-forbidden interior values; neither always dominates.
assumptions_latex: The binary decomposition is enforced to arc consistency.
Global bounds filtering is required to support bounds but need not remove unsupported interior values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case from-scratch bounds for specified representative implementations, rather than universal bounds for the consistency notions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\) be the number of variables, \(p\) the number of represented values, \(m=\sum_i|D_i|\), and \(d=\max_i|D_i|\). Matching-based domain filtering using Hopcroft--Karp and residual-graph analysis runs in \(O(m\sqrt{n+p})\) time. Representative specialized algorithms enforce range consistency in \(O(n^2)\) time and bounds consistency in \(O(n\log n)\) time after endpoint sorting. Generic AC-3 on the \(\Theta(n^2)\) binary disequalities has the coarse bound \(O(n^2d^3)\). These algorithm-specific bounds do not imply that every stronger filter is slower on every instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representative matching, interval, and generic binary algorithms occupy different worst-case cost points, although actual ordering remains implementation- and instance-dependent.

The range and bounds bounds refer to specialized from-scratch interval algorithms.

assumptions_latex: All domains are finite subsets of \(\mathbb Z\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative pruning-strength frontier for the principal global AllDifferent filters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every domain state, the closures satisfy \(P_{\mathrm{DC}}(D)\subseteq P_{\mathrm{RC}}(D)\subseteq P_{\mathrm{BC}}(D)\), where inclusion means that the stronger filter leaves no more values than the weaker one. Domain filtering requires supports using original domains; range filtering permits hull values for untested variables; bounds filtering requires support only for current endpoints. The inclusions can be strict. Consequently, selecting a filter trades stronger pruning against the additional matching, range, or Hall-interval computations needed to establish the corresponding supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AllDifferent domain consistency is stronger than range consistency, which is stronger than bounds consistency; stronger levels generally require more support computation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hull Support Can Mask Domain Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp separation between hull-based bounds consistency and domain consistency for GCC.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two variables have domains \(D_1=D_2=\{1,3\}\), and require exactly one occurrence of value \(2\), with permissive bounds for values \(1\) and \(3\). Over the hulls \([1,3]\), every endpoint of either variable has a support by assigning the other variable value \(2\). Over the actual domains, no assignment can use value \(2\), so the GCC is infeasible. Hence hull-based bounds consistency does not imply domain consistency.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial Baseline for GCC Endpoint Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case bound for rebuilding and repeatedly testing forced circulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If one feasible-circulation test costs \(T_{\mathrm{circ}}(V,E)\), a sweep over at most two endpoints per variable costs \(O(nT_{\mathrm{circ}}(V,E))\). Since at most \(\sum_i(|R_i^0|-1)\) deletions preserve nonempty hulls, a rebuild-after-each-deletion implementation costs \(O(n(1+\sum_i(|R_i^0|-1))T_{\mathrm{circ}}(V,E))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The forced-circulation baseline is polynomial per sweep, and finite endpoint contraction bounds the number of rebuilding sweeps.
assumptions_latex: A circulation test costs at most T_circ(V,E).
A sweep tests no more than two current endpoints per variable.
Deleted endpoints are never restored.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Baseline for GCC Endpoint Filtering

assumptions_latex: Domains are finite integer sets with hulls \(R_i=[\ell_i,u_i]\cap\mathbb Z\).
Value occurrence bounds satisfy \(0\le l_v\le u_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounds filtering reaches a fixpoint where every remaining endpoint has a feasible global-cardinality support over the hulls.

notation.meaning: Number of variables assigned value v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds consistency for global cardinality constraints under the integer-hull convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An endpoint \(a\in\{\ell_i,u_i\}\) is bounds supported when there exists an assignment \(s\) such that \(s(x_i)=a\), \(s(x_j)\in R_j\) for every \(j\ne i\), and \(l_v\le c_v\le u_v\) for every value \(v\). The global-cardinality constraint is bounds consistent exactly when both endpoints of every non-singleton hull, and the unique endpoint of every singleton hull, are bounds supported. Bounds filtering repeatedly removes unsupported endpoints and reports failure when a hull becomes empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each current endpoint must extend, using other variables' hulls, to an assignment satisfying every value's lower and upper occurrence bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Global-Cardinality Bounds Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is appropriate for an endpoint-support characterization, but global-cardinality bounds consistency has convention-sensitive variants. No cited source confirms this hull convention, endpoint criterion, or fixpoint statement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard global-cardinality semantics coupled to an assignment-cost variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given assignment costs \(c_{iv}\), occurrence bounds \(l_v,u_v\), and a cost variable \(z\), \(\operatorname{costGCC}(X,l,u,c,z)\) holds exactly when \(l_v\le |\{i:x_i=v\}|\le u_v\) for every \(v\) and \(z=\sum_i c_{i,x_i}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cost GCC enforces value-occurrence bounds and makes z equal the sum of selected assignment costs.
assumptions_latex: All variables and domains are finite.
Every current assignment literal has a defined integral cost.

notation.meaning: Cost of assigning value v to variable i.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost Global-Cardinality Constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of minimum-cost upper-bound tests to enforce equality with a noninterval cost domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality \(z=C(f)\), the tests \(C_{\min}\le\max D(z)\) and \(C_{iv}\le\max D(z)\) are exact only for the relaxation \(C(f)\le U\). They are not sufficient for an arbitrary finite \(D(z)\): if the attainable costs are \(\{0,2\}\) and \(D(z)=\{1\}\), then the minimum cost is at most \(\max D(z)\), yet no cost-compatible flow exists. Exact equality support requires \(C(f)\in D(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-cost tests enforce an upper cost limit but can miss failure when the equality cost domain has holes.
assumptions_latex: The constraint contains the equality \(z=C(f)\).
The finite domain of z may have holes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_{iv}\le\max D(z)\centernot\implies\exists f:\ f_{iv}=1\land C(f)\in D(z).

notation.meaning: Minimum feasible-flow cost with assignment i=v forced.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Cost-Domain Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Layered-State Filtering for Arbitrary Cost Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-state filtering for cost-GCC equality, including cost domains with holes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Process variables in order using states \((i,\gamma,q)\), where \(i\) variables have been assigned, \(\gamma_v\) is the occurrence count of value \(v\), and \(q\) is accumulated cost. Extend by \(x_{i+1}=v\) only if \(v\in D_{i+1}\) and \(\gamma_v<u_v\). A terminal state is accepting exactly when \(l_v\le\gamma_v\le u_v\) for every \(v\) and \(q\in D(z)\). Forward and backward reachability retain exactly assignment literals and cost values lying on accepting paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A layered dynamic program over occurrence vectors and accumulated costs enforces exact equality support even when the cost domain has holes.
assumptions_latex: Variable, value, and cost domains are finite.
Assignment costs are integral.
Accumulated costs are represented by an exact dense or sparse state map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i=v\text{ is retained}\iff\exists\text{ accepting path using }x_i=v,\qquad q\in D(z)\text{ is retained}\iff\exists\text{ accepting path of cost }q.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Layered-State Filtering for Arbitrary Cost Domains

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state certificate for incompatibility with an arbitrary cost-variable domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be the set of costs of terminal layered states satisfying all occurrence bounds, and let \(Q_{iv}\) be the corresponding set when \(x_i=v\) is forced. Then \(Q\cap D(z)=\varnothing\) certifies failure, while \(Q_{iv}\cap D(z)=\varnothing\) certifies deletion of \(x_i=v\). A recurrence-closed reachability table whose initial state, transitions, and terminal labels are checked exactly is a certificate of these disjointness claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact reachable-cost sets certify failure or literal deletion when they are disjoint from the cost-variable domain.
assumptions_latex: The table is closed under every legal layered transition.
Occurrence bounds and cost-domain membership are checked exactly.

notation.meaning: Terminal feasible costs when assignment i=v is forced.

knowledge_statements.title: Reachable-Cost Disjointness Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-sensitive state-space bound for the exact layered cost-GCC filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S\) layered states and \(A\) legal state transitions are materialized, forward/backward filtering takes \(O(S+A)\) time and \(O(S+A)\) space. A coarse state bound is \(S\le(n+1)W\prod_v(u_v+1)\), where \(W\) is the number of represented accumulated-cost labels. Thus the method is finite but may be exponential in the number of values and pseudo-polynomial in a densely represented cost span.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reachability is linear in the materialized layered graph, whose occurrence-vector and cost dimensions may be exponential or pseudo-polynomial.
assumptions_latex: Duplicate states with the same layer, occurrence vector, and cost are merged.
All represented states and transitions fit in memory.

notation.meaning: Number of represented accumulated-cost labels across a layer's cost range.

knowledge_statements.title: Layered-State Complexity Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forced-Assignment Min-Cost Filtering for an Upper-Bounded Cost GCC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain filtering for the variant requiring a GCC assignment flow of total cost at most U.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the GCC by its integral assignment-flow network and let \(U\) be an upper cost limit. Compute the minimum feasible-flow cost \(C_{\min}\); fail if no feasible flow exists or \(C_{\min}>U\). For every assignment literal \(x_i=v\), compute \(C_{iv}=\min\{C(f):f\text{ is a feasible GCC flow},\ f_{iv}=1\}\), taking \(+\infty\) when no such flow exists, and delete \(v\) exactly when \(C_{iv}>U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an upper-bounded cost GCC, retain exactly those assignments whose cheapest forced feasible flow respects the cost limit.
assumptions_latex: The flow network represents the hard GCC exactly.
Integral assignment-arc costs and a finite upper bound \(U\) are given.
Each constrained min-cost-flow problem is solved exactly.

notation.meaning: minimum feasible GCC-flow cost with assignment i=v forced

knowledge_statements.title: Forced-Assignment Min-Cost Filtering for an Upper-Bounded Cost GCC

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Oracle Complexity of Forced-Assignment Cost Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case bound using independent exact min-cost-flow reoptimization for every assignment literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m=\sum_i|D_i|\) be the number of assignment arcs and let \(T_{\mathrm{MCF}}(V,A)\) bound one exact min-cost feasible-flow solve on the GCC network. Computing one unrestricted optimum and independently reoptimizing with every assignment arc forced takes \(O((m+1)T_{\mathrm{MCF}}(V,A))\) time and polynomial working space whenever the selected min-cost-flow algorithm has those guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct forced-arc propagator needs at most one unrestricted and one constrained min-cost-flow solve per assignment literal.
assumptions_latex: Each forced-assignment subproblem uses a network of size \(O(V+A)\).
The selected exact min-cost-flow algorithm has running-time bound \(T_{\mathrm{MCF}}(V,A)\).

notation.meaning: running-time bound for one exact min-cost feasible-flow solve

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Complexity of Forced-Assignment Cost Filtering

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable lower-bound certificate for unrestricted or forced-assignment cost-GCC flow problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the selected GCC min-cost-flow problem, optionally with \(f_{iv}=1\), as a linear program whose flow polyhedron is integral. Any verified feasible solution of its LP dual has value \(d\le C^*\), where \(C^*\) is the minimum integral feasible-flow cost. If a primal feasible flow and a dual feasible solution have equal value, they certify \(C^*=d\). Consequently, a verified dual bound \(d>U\) certifies failure or deletion for the corresponding unrestricted or forced problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal and dual min-cost-flow witnesses certify the cost lower bounds used for failure and forced-assignment deletion.
assumptions_latex: The flow formulation is exact for the selected hard GCC variant.
Primal and dual feasibility and objective values are checked exactly.
The network-flow polyhedron is integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\le C^*,\qquad C(f)=d\Rightarrow C^*=d,\qquad d>U\Rightarrow\text{no admissible flow of cost at most }U.

notation.meaning: minimum cost of the selected unrestricted or forced flow problem

knowledge_statements.title: Min-Cost-Flow Dual Bound Certificate

assumptions_latex: Assignment \(x_i=v\) has integer cost \(c_{iv}\), and occurrence bounds define feasible global-cardinality assignments.
A cost variable \(z\) has current domain contained in \([L,U]\cap\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every retained assignment and cost bound participates in a feasible cost-compatible flow.

notation.meaning: Cost of an integral assignment flow

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost-flow filtering for a cost global-cardinality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Build the global-cardinality flow network and give assignment arc \((x_i,v)\) cost \(c_{iv}\). Compute a minimum-cost feasible integral flow. If no feasible flow exists or \(C_{\min}>U\), report failure; otherwise tighten the lower bound of \(z\) to at least \(C_{\min}\). For each assignment arc, compute the minimum feasible flow cost \(C_{iv}\) subject to \(f_{iv}=1\), using residual shortest paths or an equivalent reoptimization. Delete \(v\) from \(D_i\) whenever \(C_{iv}>U\), and iterate after any domain or cost-bound change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use minimum-cost feasible flows to tighten the cost lower bound and remove assignments whose cheapest supporting flow exceeds the allowed upper cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Cost Global-Cardinality Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the precise cost-GCC semantics and filtering level need a source. The procedure only uses the upper bound U and tightens the lower bound of z; it does not establish the conclusion that every retained cost bound participates in a feasible cost-compatible flow, especially for a noninterval domain of z.

children.title: Among Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering for constraints counting variables whose values belong to a designated set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of Among Fixpoint Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence bound for the seed's contracting filtering loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every nonterminal pass of the seed filter deletes at least one value from some finite domain, including possibly \(D(N)\). Since deleted values are never restored, the loop terminates after at most \(\sum_i|D_i^0|+|D^0(N)|\) value deletions, and therefore after at most that many state-changing passes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Among filtering loop terminates after finitely many domain deletions.
assumptions_latex: All initial domains are finite.
Filtering is contracting and never restores a deleted value.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination of Among Fixpoint Filtering

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relational semantics of Among before filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \operatorname{Among}(N,[x_1,\ldots,x_n],S)\text{ holds exactly when }N=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1[x_i\in S].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among makes N equal the number of listed variables assigned a value in the fixed set S.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a fixed value set.
All variables have finite domains.
knowledge_statements.title: Among Constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition explaining membership filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce Booleans \(b_i\) satisfying \(b_i=1\iff x_i\in S\). Then Among is equivalent after projection to \(\bigwedge_i(b_i\leftrightarrow x_i\in S)\land N=\sum_i b_i\). Every undecided membership Boolean admits both values independently, so the attainable counts are exactly the integers in \([p,q]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among is a sum of channelled membership Booleans, yielding every count between p and q.
assumptions_latex: Each variable whose domain meets both S and its complement independently admits either membership choice.

notation.meaning: Indicator that variable i takes a value in S.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean-Sum Decomposition of Among

assumptions_latex: Variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) have finite domains, \(S\) is a fixed value set, and \(N\) is an integer count variable.
Define \(p=|\{i:D_i\subseteq S\}|\) and \(q=|\{i:D_i\cap S\ne\varnothing\}|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At the fixpoint, every remaining value of \(N\) and every remaining membership choice has support for \(N=|\{i:x_i\in S\}|\).

notation.meaning: Number of variables forced into S
Number of variables that can take a value in S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership-based filtering for the Among counting constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replace \(D(N)\) by \(D(N)\cap[p,q]\). If the result is empty, report failure. If \(\max D(N)=p\), remove every value in \(S\) from each domain meeting both \(S\) and its complement. If \(\min D(N)=q\), remove every value outside \(S\) from each such domain. Recompute \(p\) and \(q\) and repeat until unchanged. Because each undecided variable contributes independently either zero or one, every integer count between \(p\) and \(q\) is attainable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Count variables forced or able to lie in the designated set, tighten N to that interval, and force memberships when either count bound becomes tight.
knowledge_statements.title: Among Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Among filtering. The p,q reasoning is plausible, but the exact fixpoint/support claim for an arbitrary finite domain D(N), including removal by intersection with an interval and boundary forcing, needs an authoritative counting-constraint source.

children.title: NValue Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering for constraints controlling the number of distinct assigned values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact projection of NValue onto its count coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m=\min_s|U(s)|\) and \(M=\max_s|U(s)|\) over complete assignments from the current nonempty domains. Every integer \(q\) with \(m\le q\le M\) is attained by some assignment. Hence \(\{|U(s)|:s\in\prod_iD_i\}=[m,M]\cap\mathbb Z\), and NValue is feasible for count domain \(D(N)\) exactly when \(D(N)\cap[m,M]\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every integer between the minimum and maximum attainable numbers of distinct values is attainable.
assumptions_latex: All variable domains are finite and nonempty.
A complete assignment independently selects one value from each current domain.

notation.meaning: Distinct values used by assignment s.
Minimum and maximum attainable distinct-value counts.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval of Attainable Distinct-Value Counts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact representation of the largest attainable NValue count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form the bipartite graph \(G=(X\cup V,E)\) with \((x_i,a)\in E\) exactly when \(a\in D_i\). Then \(\max_s|U(s)|=\nu(G)\), the cardinality of a maximum matching. Consequently \(|U(s)|\ge q\) is feasible exactly when \(q\le\nu(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum attainable number of distinct assigned values equals the maximum matching size in the variable–value graph.
assumptions_latex: Variables have nonempty finite domains.
The variable–value incidence graph is represented explicitly.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Distinct-Value Matching Representation

assumptions_latex: Variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) have finite domains and \(N\) is an integer variable.
The constraint is \(N=|\{x_i:1\le i\le n\}|\), counting distinct assigned values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact filtering retains precisely the variable values and count values having a common support satisfying the distinct-value equation.

notation.meaning: Set of values used by assignment s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact support condition for domain filtering of the NValue constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A value \(a\in D_i\) is supported if there exists an assignment \(s\) with \(s(x_i)=a\), \(s(x_j)\in D_j\) for all \(j\), and \(|U(s)|\in D(N)\). A count \(r\in D(N)\) is supported if some such assignment satisfies \(|U(s)|=r\). Exact NValue filtering deletes every unsupported \(a\) and every unsupported \(r\), reporting failure if any domain becomes empty. At its fixpoint, every remaining variable-value pair and every remaining count value has a support in one common constraint solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep exactly those assignments and count values that extend to a tuple using an allowed number of distinct values.
knowledge_statements.title: NValue Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role can express exact support, but the title does not select domain consistency and the record presents exact filtering without citing its computational status or an authoritative NValue definition. A precise source is needed to determine the intended filtering variant.

children.title: Counting-Structure Relations
children.top_down_role: Shared counting abstractions across Among versus NValue filtering.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Among and NValue Do Not Determine One Another
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit non-equivalence of the sibling counting abstractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{a,b,c\}\) and \(S=\{a,b\}\). Assignments \((a,a,c)\) and \((a,b,c)\) both have Among count \(2\), but their NValue counts are \(2\) and \(3\). Conversely, \((a,a,c)\) and \((a,c,c)\) both have NValue count \(2\), but their Among counts are \(2\) and \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal Among counts can hide different distinct-value counts, and equal NValue counts can hide different fixed-set counts.
assumptions_latex: At least three variables and three values are available.
knowledge_statements.title: Among and NValue Do Not Determine One Another

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-loss boundary between Among and NValue projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Among depends linearly on multiplicities \(c_v\), whereas NValue depends on the nonlinear predicates \(c_v>0\). Aggregate sums \(\sum_{v\in S_j}c_v\) therefore need not determine the positive-support pattern unless the aggregates reconstruct every relevant occurrence coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate multiplicities generally lose the support pattern needed to determine NValue.
assumptions_latex: The available occurrence aggregates need not identify every coordinate c_v.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicity Versus Support Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Cardinality as the Common Occurrence Layer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural relation among GCC, Among, and NValue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_v=|\{i:x_i=v\}|\). Global cardinality imposes coordinate bounds \(l_v\le c_v\le u_v\); Among over \(S\) uses \(\sum_{v\in S}c_v\); and NValue uses \(|\{v:c_v>0\}|\). Thus the three constraints respectively apply coordinate restrictions, a linear projection, and a support-cardinality projection to one occurrence vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GCC, Among, and NValue share occurrence counts but use coordinate bounds, a fixed-set sum, and a positive-support count respectively.
assumptions_latex: All variables range over a common finite universe V.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Cardinality as the Common Occurrence Layer

assumptions_latex: Variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) have finite domains over a value universe \(V\).
For each \(v\in V\), let \(y_v\) indicate whether value \(v\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Among and NValue are respectively linear aggregation and positive-support aggregation of the same occurrence variables.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Occurrence-variable representation linking Among, NValue, and global cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The occurrence counts satisfy \(\sum_{v\in V}c_v=n\) and \(c_v=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1[x_i=v]\). For any fixed \(S\subseteq V\), the Among count is \(N_S=\sum_{v\in S}c_v=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1[x_i\in S]\). The NValue count is \(N_{\mathrm{val}}=\sum_{v\in V}y_v\), with \(y_v=1\) exactly when \(c_v>0\). Hence both constraints project the same value-occurrence structure, but Among sums multiplicities over a fixed set whereas NValue counts positive occurrence classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among sums occurrences in a fixed value set, while NValue counts how many occurrence counts are positive; both derive from value multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.title: Counting-Structure Relations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits Counting-Structure Relations, and the occurrence identities are internally coherent. No inspectable source is supplied for the asserted structural relationship among Among, NValue, and occurrence variables.

children.title: Filtering-Strength Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Domain or parameter regimes limiting pruning strength for these counting constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity split between lower-count and upper-count feasibility on explicitly represented unrestricted finite domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m=\min_s|U(s)|\) and \(M=\max_s|U(s)|\), where \(U(s)=\{s(x_i):1\le i\le n\}\). When \(k\) is part of the input, deciding \(m\le k\), equivalently feasibility of \(\operatorname{AtMostNValue}(x,k)\), is NP-complete. Conversely, \(M\) equals the maximum-matching cardinality of the variable–value incidence graph, so deciding \(M\ge k\), equivalently feasibility of \(\operatorname{AtLeastNValue}(x,k)\), is polynomial-time solvable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-distinct feasibility is NP-complete, whereas maximum-distinct feasibility is computable by bipartite matching.
assumptions_latex: Every variable has a nonempty finite domain represented explicitly.
The threshold \(k\) is part of the input.
\(U(s)\) denotes the distinct values used by a complete assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{AtMostNValue}\text{ feasibility is NP-complete, while }\operatorname{AtLeastNValue}\text{ feasibility is polynomial-time solvable}.

notation.meaning: Set of values used by assignment s.
Minimum and maximum attainable distinct-value counts.

knowledge_statements.title: AtMost–AtLeast NValue Tractability Boundary

assumptions_latex: NValue domains are arbitrary finite subsets of a common value universe.
Filtering must compute the exact minimum feasible number of distinct assigned values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Computing this exact lower bound, and therefore enforcing exact NValue bounds or domain consistency in general, is NP-hard.

notation.meaning: Minimum possible number of distinct assigned values

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hardness boundary for exact NValue filtering on unrestricted finite domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a set-cover instance with universe elements indexed by variables and candidate sets indexed by values, put value \(v\) in \(D_i\) exactly when the corresponding candidate set contains element \(i\). Any complete assignment chooses, for every element, one candidate set containing it; its distinct assigned values are precisely the chosen sets. Therefore \(m(D)\) equals the minimum set-cover size. Computing \(m(D)\) is NP-hard, so a polynomial-time filter cannot generally establish the exact lower count bound, unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\). Polynomial NValue propagators must consequently use restricted domains or incomplete lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact NValue lower-bound filtering is NP-hard on arbitrary domains because minimizing the distinct chosen values is exactly a set-cover problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Filtering-Strength Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the set-cover correspondence is plausible, but the NP-hardness claim requires a specific complexity citation. The statement also contains reduction/proof text, which is prohibited for this knowledge layer and must be removed once the sourced theorem boundary is established.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle bound for the seed's complete budget-support filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m=\sum_i|D_i|\), and let \(T_{\mathrm{MCF}}\) bound one minimum-cost-flow computation on the soft-GCC network. Computing the global minimum once and reoptimizing separately with each assignment literal forced enforces the seed's budget-support test in \(O((m+1)T_{\mathrm{MCF}})\) time. Hence the filter is polynomial for explicitly represented finite domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One global and at most one forced minimum-cost-flow solve per domain literal give a polynomial complete budget-support filter.
assumptions_latex: Minimum-cost flow is solved exactly.
The network size is polynomial in the explicit domain representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Forced-Value Filtering by Reoptimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics of the violation measure filtered by the seed algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an assignment \(s\), let \(N_a(s)=|\{i:s_i=a\}|\). The variable-based soft-GCC violation is \(\operatorname{viol}(s)=\sum_{a\in V}((\ell_a-N_a(s))_+ +(N_a(s)-u_a)_+)\). The budgeted constraint accepts exactly assignments with \(s_i\in D_i\subseteq V\) and \(\operatorname{viol}(s)\le B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-based soft GCC charges each unit of occurrence deficit or excess and accepts assignments within budget B.
assumptions_latex: \(D_i\subseteq V\) for every variable.
Occurrence bounds and B are nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Based Soft Global Cardinality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-equivalence of common soft-GCC violation semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The variable-based deficit/excess measure is not interchangeable with a value-based measure that counts only how many values violate their occurrence bounds, nor with arbitrary weighted penalties. An excess of \(k>1\) on one value costs \(k\) under the variable-based measure but one under the value-based measure. Flow arc costs must therefore encode the declared violation measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different soft-GCC metrics can accept and rank assignments differently, so their filtering networks are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: Some occurrence bound can be violated by more than one unit.
knowledge_statements.title: Violation-Measure Variant Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between variable-based soft GCC and hard GCC.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the deficit/excess measure, \(\operatorname{viol}(s)\le0\) holds exactly when every occurrence count lies within its prescribed interval. Thus a zero-budget variable-based soft GCC has exactly the satisfying assignments of the corresponding hard GCC.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero violation budget, variable-based soft GCC reduces exactly to hard GCC.
assumptions_latex: The violation is the sum of occurrence deficits and excesses.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Budget Hard-GCC Specialization

assumptions_latex: Finite variables \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) with current domains \(D_i\).
Finite value set \(V\), bounds \(0\leq \ell_a\leq u_a\leq n\) for each \(a\in V\), and violation-cost upper bound \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every deleted value has no completion of violation cost at most \(B\); every retained value has such a completion.

notation.meaning: Number of variables assigned value \(a\) by assignment \(s\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard min-cost-flow filtering formulation for a soft global cardinality constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-based soft cardinality filtering with a hard upper bound on total violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct the standard assignment-count min-cost flow network whose integral feasible flows represent assignments \(s\in\prod_i D_i\) and whose flow cost equals \(c(s)\). Compute its minimum cost \(c^*\). For every \(i\) and \(a\in D_i\), compute \(c^*_{i,a}=\min\{c(s):s\in\prod_jD_j,\ s_i=a\}\), either by a forced arc or by residual-network shortest paths. If \(c^*>B\), report failure. Otherwise delete \(a\) from \(D_i\) exactly when \(c^*_{i,a}>B\). At termination, output the reduced domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Min-cost flow finds the least cardinality violation and removes each value whose best forced completion exceeds the permitted violation budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Soft Cardinality Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied for the min-cost-flow construction or residual-path filtering claim. The assumptions also do not state that every domain is contained in V, so the stated cost/network correspondence is not fully determined.

children.title: Support Scanning
children.top_down_role: Search across extensional tuples for current value supports.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case cost of restart-after-sweep scanning over an explicit positive table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q_0=\sum_i|D_i^0|. With literal-indexed lists T_{i,a} and O(r)-time tuple-validity tests, one sweep costs O(r^2|T|). A restart-after-sweep implementation performs at most Q_0+1 sweeps and therefore uses O(Q_0r^2|T|) time and O(r|T|+Q_0) explicit-index space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Naive repeated support scanning is polynomial in the explicit table size and needs at most one more sweep than the initial number of literals.
assumptions_latex: T is an explicit positive table of arity r.
Every nonfinal sweep deletes at least one literal.
Tuple validity is tested in O(r) time.
review_flags: This bounds the stated naive restart-after-sweep implementation, not an optimal table propagator.
knowledge_statements.title: Naive Fixed-Point Support-Scanning Bound

assumptions_latex: A positive extensional constraint has scope \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\), current domains \(D_i\), and finite allowed table \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting domains are generalized arc consistent for the single table constraint.

notation.meaning: Tuple validity under the current domains.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct support-search characterization of generalized arc consistency for positive tables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Naive full-table support scanning for a positive extensional constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Repeatedly inspect every current literal \(x_i=a\), where \(a\in D_i\). Scan \(T_{i,a}\) until finding a tuple \(t\) satisfying \(t_j\in D_j\) for every \(j\). If no such tuple exists, delete \(a\) from \(D_i\). Continue until no deletion occurs; if some domain becomes empty, report failure. Otherwise return the fixed-point domains. At the fixed point, each remaining literal occurs in at least one currently valid allowed tuple.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each variable-value pair, scan allowed tuples for a currently valid support and delete the value when no support exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Support Scanning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-scanning algorithm and GAC conclusion are standard and internally consistent, but no inspectable constraint-programming source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Tuple Residues
children.top_down_role: Cached supporting tuples reused by extensional filtering.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A valid tuple can witness all of its coordinate literals simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If t\in T is valid under the current domains, then t supports x_i=t_i for every coordinate i. The same stored tuple may therefore be referenced as the residue of any or all of its coordinate literals without separate tuple copies; sharing does not alter the validity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One valid allowed tuple can be shared as the cached support of every literal occurring in it.
assumptions_latex: T is a positive table of arity r.
t is valid in every current coordinate domain.

notation.meaning: A coordinate literal witnessed by the tuple.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Tuple Residues

assumptions_latex: A positive table \(T\) is maintained under changing finite domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid residue certifies support; an invalid residue provides no support information and must be replaced or followed by a complete search.

notation.meaning: Current validity predicate for a tuple.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard residue definition used by table-constraint propagators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residues cache witnesses; they are not permanent logical supports when domains change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tuple residue for a literal \(x_i=a\) is a stored tuple \(R[i,a]\in T\) satisfying \(R[i,a]_i=a\) at the time it is recorded. Relative to current domains, it is an active residue exactly when \(\operatorname{valid}_D(R[i,a])\) holds. An active residue is a directly checkable support for \(x_i=a\). The residue may remain stored after becoming invalid, but then it is only a search hint and does not certify support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tuple residue is a cached allowed tuple for a value; it certifies support only while all its coordinates remain in their current domains.
knowledge_statements.title: Tuple Residues

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residue definition matches the leaf and is mathematically coherent, but it has no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Scan–Residue Interaction
children.top_down_role: Use of cached tuples to limit repeated support scans.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residue-First Sweep Cost and Worst-Case Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost of cached-tuple validation followed by literal-indexed fallback scans in one positive-table sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q=\sum_i|D_i| and U=\{(i,a):R[i,a]\text{ is absent or invalid}\}. If tuple validity inspects at most r coordinates, one residue-first sweep costs O\!\left(rQ+r\sum_{(i,a)\in U}|T_{i,a}|\right). Since \sum_{i,a}|T_{i,a}|=r|T|, its worst-case cost is O(rQ+r^2|T|).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid residues avoid fallback scans, but universal residue failure leaves the same asymptotic worst case as naive support scanning.
assumptions_latex: T is an explicit positive table of arity r.
Candidate tuples are indexed by literal.
Tuple validity is checked coordinatewise.
review_flags: The bound assumes literal-indexed candidate lists and direct coordinate validity tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Residue-First Sweep Cost and Worst-Case Boundary

assumptions_latex: A positive table \(T\), current domains \(D_i\), and optional residues \(R[i,a]\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure deletes \(a\) exactly when no currently valid tuple in \(T\) supports \(x_i=a\).

notation.meaning: Validity of a tuple in current domains.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard residue-first support scan for positive extensional constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residue-first scanning combines constant-time witness reuse with complete fallback search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each literal \(x_i=a\), first test whether \(R[i,a]\) exists and \(\operatorname{valid}_D(R[i,a])\) holds. If so, retain \(a\) without scanning. Otherwise scan all tuples \(t\in T\) with \(t_i=a\) until a valid tuple is found. On success set \(R[i,a]\leftarrow t\) and retain \(a\); if the scan is exhausted, delete \(a\). Repeat after deletions until a fixed point is reached. Residue failure never alone justifies deletion; only exhaustion of the complete support set does.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check a cached support first; when it is invalid, scan for a replacement, and delete the value only after the complete scan fails.
knowledge_statements.title: Scan–Residue Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residue-first complete support scan fits the container and is precise, but the claimed exact deletion behavior lacks an inspectable source and locator.

children.title: Residue Invalidation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Table or domain changes that render cached tuple supports unusable.

assumptions_latex: Search updates may delete domain values and may later restore them during backtracking.
A residue \(R[i,a]\) stores only a tuple, without an independent validity certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Residues require validity checks after deletions, while restoration can reactivate an old residue but cannot make unchecked residue reuse sound.

notation.meaning: Validity of tuple \(t\) at search state \(q\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validity behavior follows directly from domain membership under monotone descent and backtracking restoration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes monotone domain descent from nonmonotone restoration in residue maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Along a monotone descent with \(D_j(q')\subseteq D_j(q)\), validity is one-way: \(\neg\operatorname{valid}_{q}(t)\) implies \(\neg\operatorname{valid}_{q'}(t)\), whereas \(\operatorname{valid}_{q}(t)\) need not imply \(\operatorname{valid}_{q'}(t)\). After restoration, an invalid tuple may become valid again. Consequently a residue is invalidated whenever any coordinate leaves its domain; it may be trailed, discarded, or retained as a hint, but it certifies support at state \(q\) only after \(\operatorname{valid}_{q}(R[i,a])\) is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain deletion can invalidate a cached tuple; backtracking can reactivate it, but every reused residue must be valid in the current state.
knowledge_statements.title: Residue Invalidation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotone-deletion and restoration statements are internally correct, but no source is supplied for the residue-maintenance regime.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time, storage, and restoration boundary for simple reduction over an explicit table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With constant-time domain-membership tests, scanning every tuple coordinate and marking surviving tuples and their projected values takes O(r|T|+Q) time, where Q=\sum_i|D_i|, and O(|T|+Q) auxiliary marking space when survivors are materialized. Destructive retention is sound along monotone descent; restoration requires trailing, copying, persistence, or recomputation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simple reduction is linear in the explicit table representation, while backtracking requires reversible table state or recomputation.
assumptions_latex: T is explicitly represented.
Domain membership is testable in constant time.

notation.meaning: Total number of current domain values.
Number of explicitly stored tuple coordinates.

review_flags: Streaming or implementation-specific reversible representations can change auxiliary space.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Reduction Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact closed form of simple reduction for one positive table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For D=(D_1,\ldots,D_r), let S_D=\{t\in T:\forall i,\ t_i\in D_i\} and D_i'=D_i\cap\pi_i(S_D). Then S_{D'}=S_D, the reduction operator R(D)=D' is idempotent, and D_i' is exactly the set of values in D_i supported by T under D.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For one positive table, deleting invalid tuples and projecting the survivors reaches the exact fixed point in one pass.
assumptions_latex: T is a finite positive table.
Only this table defines the reduction.

notation.meaning: Allowed tuples compatible with domains D.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Pass Closure and Idempotence

assumptions_latex: A positive table \(T\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^r U_i\) and current domains \(D_i\subseteq U_i\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the reduced table contains exactly the currently feasible tuples and every remaining value occurs in one of them.

notation.meaning: Current set of surviving allowed tuples.
Projection of surviving tuples onto coordinate \(i\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical simple tabular reduction rule for positive tables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simple tabular reduction by explicit removal of invalid tuples and unsupported values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(S\leftarrow T\). Repeatedly replace \(S\) by \(\{t\in S:\forall i,\ t_i\in D_i\}\), then replace each domain by \(D_i\leftarrow D_i\cap\pi_i(S)\). Stop when neither \(S\) nor any domain changes. If \(S=\varnothing\), report failure; otherwise return \(S\) and the reduced domains. Because tuple validity and projections are recomputed after every change, the fixed point enforces generalized arc consistency for this constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Remove tuples conflicting with current domains, then remove values absent from the surviving table, repeating to a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.title: Simple Tabular Reduction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduction algorithm and fixed-point GAC claim fit the topic, but no authoritative table-filtering citation with a specific locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-Table realization that visits only currently nonzero live-tuple words and supports search restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store \(L\) as a reversible sparse bitset: a word array together with a sparse-set index of its nonzero words. For each changed variable, intersect the active words with the union of literal masks for its current domain and remove indices whose live word becomes zero. Test \(x_i=a\) by intersecting \(M_{i,a}\) with the active live words. Trail or copy the modified words and sparse-set boundary so backtracking restores the ancestor live set. Empty \(L\) reports failure; deleting every literal with empty intersection enforces domain consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact-Table combines literal masks with a reversible sparse live bitset, scanning active words and restoring them on backtracking.
assumptions_latex: The positive table and literal masks are fixed within the search.
Only active nonzero live words are scanned.
Modified live words and sparse-set state are restored on backtracking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The restored, deletion-fixpoint domains are domain consistent for the explicit positive table}.

notation.meaning: Reversible sparse bitset of live tuples.
Static support mask for literal x_i=a.

knowledge_statements.title: Reversible Sparse-Bitset Compact-Table Update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense baseline and active-word complexity of Compact-Table mask operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\) tuples stored in \(b=\lceil m/w\rceil\) machine words, one dense mask intersection or literal-support test takes \(O(b)\) word operations. If the reversible sparse bitset currently has \(q\le b\) nonzero words, the corresponding active-word scan takes \(O(q)\). Directly testing every current literal therefore takes \(O(q\sum_i|D_i|)\) word operations, with \(O(b\sum_i|D_i|)\) as the dense worst case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact-Table support tests scale with the number of active live-tuple words, bounded by the total tuple-bitset length.
assumptions_latex: Bitwise operations on a \(w\)-bit machine word take constant time.
Literal masks are precomputed.
The bound excludes additional residue optimizations owned by the scan-residue sibling.

notation.meaning: Words in a dense tuple bitset.

knowledge_statements.title: Word-Parallel Support-Test Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Required handling of backtracking or other nonmonotone domain enlargement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A live bitset updated only by destructive intersection is incorrect across domain restoration: a tuple bit cleared because of a descendant-domain deletion may become compatible after backtracking but cannot be recreated by further intersections. Correct nonmonotone operation must restore a trailed or copied ancestor bitset, or recompute \(L\) from the restored domains and static literal masks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Destructive intersections are valid only between restorations; backtracking must restore or recompute cleared tuple bits.
assumptions_latex: A domain value may be restored after deletion.
Without restoration, the live bitset supports only bit-clearing intersection updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D'\supset D\not\Rightarrow L(D')\text{ can be obtained from }L(D)\text{ by intersections alone}.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Restoration Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct live-set invariant within a deletion-only search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(L\) initially marks exactly the positive-table tuples compatible with the domains at entry to a search state, then, under domain deletions only, intersecting \(L\) with the masks induced by every changed domain maintains \(L=\{t\in T:\forall i,\ t_i\in D_i\}\). Thus tuple bits decrease monotonically and a literal \(x_i=a\) is supported exactly when \(L\wedge M_{i,a}\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: During deletion-only propagation, the live bitset equals the currently compatible tuples and only loses bits.
assumptions_latex: The table is positive and explicit.
Domains change only by deletion until the search state is left.
Every changed coordinate is incorporated into the live bitset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L=\bigcap_i\bigvee_{a\in D_i}M_{i,a},\qquad x_i=a\text{ supported}\iff L\wedge M_{i,a}\ne0.

notation.meaning: Static tuple mask for literal x_i=a.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Live-Tuple Invariant

assumptions_latex: A positive table has tuples indexed by \(0,\ldots,m-1\), with current domains \(D_i\).
For each literal \(x_i=a\), a bitset \(M_{i,a}\) marks exactly the table tuples having coordinate \(a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The final domains are generalized arc consistent for the table constraint, and \(L\) marks exactly its currently valid tuples.

notation.meaning: Bitset of tuples compatible with the current domain of coordinate \(i\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard bitset compact-table filtering invariant and update rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-parallel positive-table filtering using a live-tuple bitset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(L\) with all tuple bits set. After any domain change, update \(L\leftarrow L\wedge\bigwedge_{i=1}^r V_i\), where \(V_i=\bigvee_{a\in D_i}M_{i,a}\). If \(L=0\), report failure. For every \(a\in D_i\), delete \(a\) when \(L\wedge M_{i,a}=0\). Recompute affected \(V_i\) and repeat until stable. With machine-word bitsets, intersections and nonemptiness tests operate wordwise; the algorithm outputs the fixed-point domains and live-tuple bitset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bitsets represent live tuples and literal supports; intersections remove invalid tuples, and an empty literal intersection causes value deletion.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Table Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No exact Compact-Table source is supplied. Moreover, the monotonically intersected live bitset is sound for domain deletion but not arbitrary domain restoration; the update regime must be sourced and explicitly restricted or restoration handling specified.

children.title: Negative Tables
children.top_down_role: Extensional filtering based on explicitly forbidden tuples.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact full-recomputation filter for explicitly listed complete negative tables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each round compute \(F_D=F\cap\prod_iD_i\) and, for every literal \(x_i=a\), count the tuples in \(F_D\cap Q_{i,a}\). Delete \(a\) exactly when this count equals \(\prod_{j\ne i}|D_j|\), report failure when \(|F_D|=\prod_j|D_j|\), and repeat after deletions. The deletion fixpoint is domain consistent. One full round costs \(O(r|F|+d)\) time and \(O(|F|+d)\) auxiliary space, where \(d=\sum_i|D_i|\); naive repetition takes at most \(d\) deleting rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Count compatible forbidden completions; delete a literal when they fill its entire completion space.
assumptions_latex: Forbidden tuples are explicit, complete, and duplicate-free.
Cartesian-product cardinalities are represented without arithmetic overflow.
The stated bound uses full recomputation rather than an incremental data structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The deletion fixpoint is domain consistent for }U\setminus F.
knowledge_statements.title: Compatible-Forbidden-Tuple Counting Filter

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact support and failure tests for a negative table of distinct complete tuples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a\in D_i\), let \(Q_{i,a}=\{s\in\prod_jD_j:s_i=a\}\) and \(F_D=F\cap\prod_jD_j\). Then \(a\) is supported exactly when \(Q_{i,a}\nsubseteq F_D\), equivalently \(|F_D\cap Q_{i,a}|<\prod_{j\ne i}|D_j|\). The constraint fails exactly when \(|F_D|=\prod_j|D_j|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value is unsupported exactly when every current completion containing it is explicitly forbidden.
assumptions_latex: The forbidden table contains distinct complete tuples.
Every current domain is finite.
Negative-table semantics are those of the immutable definition seed.

notation.meaning: Forbidden tuples compatible with all current domains.
Current complete assignments containing literal x_i=a.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Table Literal Support Criterion

assumptions_latex: Finite universes \(U_1,\ldots,U_r\) and a finite forbidden table \(F\subseteq\prod_iU_i\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An assignment satisfies the negative table exactly when it is not one of the explicitly forbidden tuples.

notation.meaning: Explicit set of forbidden complete tuples.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of a negative extensional constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete-tuple negative representation of an extensional constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The negative table constraint determined by \(F\) is the relation \(C_F=U\setminus F\). For current domains \(D_i\subseteq U_i\), a tuple \(s\in\prod_iD_i\) satisfies the constraint if and only if \(s\notin F\). Thus tuples absent from \(F\) are allowed implicitly; membership in \(F\), rather than membership in an allowed table, is the rejection test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative table lists forbidden complete assignments; every assignment in the Cartesian universe not listed is allowed.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative Tables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complete-tuple negative-table definition is precise and appropriate, but it lacks a constraint-programming citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Short Tables
children.top_down_role: Extensional filtering based on compact tuples containing generalized entries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact filtering of a positive wildcard short table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Call \(p\in P\) usable when \(p_j\in D_j\) for every specified coordinate \(j\in I_p\). A literal \(x_i=a\) is supported exactly when some usable \(p\) either specifies \(p_i=a\) or leaves coordinate \(i\) unspecified. Delete literals lacking such a short support and repeat until stable. The fixpoint is domain consistent for \(\bigcup_{p\in P}[p]\), and failure occurs exactly when no short tuple is usable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value survives when a usable short tuple contains it or leaves its coordinate as a wildcard.
assumptions_latex: Short tuples use positive wildcard-cylinder semantics.
Domains and the short table are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i=a\text{ is supported}\iff\exists p\in P:\ p\text{ usable}\land(i\notin I_p\lor p_i=a).

notation.meaning: Coordinates specified by short tuple p.

knowledge_statements.title: Short-Table Domain-Consistency Filter

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-recomputation complexity for the positive short-table filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=\sum_{p\in P}|I_p|\), \(d=\sum_i|D_i|\), and let \(r\) be the arity. A full round can identify usable tuples and mark support from specified entries or wildcard coordinates in \(O(L+r|P|+d)\) time and \(O(|P|+d)\) auxiliary space. Since every nonterminal repeated round deletes at least one literal, naive full recomputation reaches a fixpoint after at most \(d\) deleting rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full short-support scanning is polynomial in represented table length and reaches a fixpoint after finitely many literal deletions.
assumptions_latex: The short table and domains are explicit.
Support from an unspecified coordinate can be marked collectively for that coordinate.
The bound concerns full recomputation, not a specialized incremental propagator.

notation.meaning: Total number of specified short-tuple entries.

knowledge_statements.title: Short-Support Full-Scan Bound

assumptions_latex: Finite universes \(U_1,\ldots,U_r\) are fixed.
Each short tuple assigns values to a subset of coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented relation is the union of the cylinders generated by the short tuples.

notation.meaning: Coordinate set specified by short tuple \(p\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard wildcard or short-support table semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive short tables interpreted as wildcard cylinders over unspecified coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A short tuple \(p\) is a partial assignment \((p_i)_{i\in I_p}\). It represents every complete assignment in \([p]\), with coordinates outside \(I_p\) unrestricted. A positive short table \(P\) represents the relation \(C_P=\bigcup_{p\in P}[p]\). Relative to current domains \(D_i\), a short tuple is usable exactly when \(p_i\in D_i\) for all \(i\in I_p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A short table lists partial assignments whose unspecified coordinates are wildcards; its allowed relation is the union of all represented completions.
knowledge_statements.title: Short Tables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cylinder semantics are coherent, but no source establishes that this is the intended positive short-table convention; short-support and wildcard-table terminology can vary.

children.title: Representation Conversion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Size or precision effects when translating between table representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semantic Conditions for Exact Table Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness criteria independent of conversion output size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive complete table \(A\subseteq U\) and negative complete table \(F\subseteq U\) represent the same relation exactly when \(F=U\setminus A\). A positive short table \(P\) and complete positive table \(A\) represent the same relation exactly when \(A=\bigcup_{p\in P}[p]\). Duplicate complete tuples and overlapping short-tuple cylinders do not change the represented relation, although they can increase representation or filtering cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact conversion uses set complementation for positive versus negative tables and cylinder union for short versus complete positive tables.
assumptions_latex: All representations use the same finite coordinate universes.
Positive and negative complete tables contain complete tuples.
Short tuples use positive wildcard-cylinder semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_A=C_F\iff F=U\setminus A,\qquad C_A=C_P\iff A=\bigcup_{p\in P}[p].

notation.meaning: Cylinder of complete extensions of short tuple p.

knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Conditions for Exact Table Conversion

assumptions_latex: The complete assignment universe is \(U=\prod_{i=1}^rU_i\) with \(|U|=N\).
Representations are explicit lists without auxiliary symbolic compression.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive-to-negative conversion has output size \(N-|A|\), while short-to-complete expansion has output size at most \(\sum_{p\in P}\prod_{i\notin I_p}|U_i|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: output-size bounds follow from explicit complement enumeration and wildcard expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-sensitive boundaries for converting complete positive, negative, and short tables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Converting an explicit positive table \(A\) to a negative table requires enumerating \(U\setminus A\), so its output contains exactly \(N-|A|\) tuples and requires \(\Omega(N-|A|)\) output time and space. Expanding a short table \(P\) into complete tuples generates at most \(E=\sum_{p\in P}\prod_{i\notin I_p}|U_i|\) tuple occurrences, with duplicates removable afterward. Both conversions can therefore be exponential in the arity \(r\), even when the input representation is polynomial in \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit complementation costs the size of the complement, while expanding wildcards can generate exponentially many complete tuples.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Conversion Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The output-count formulas are plausible, but the exponential-in-arity claim depends on the encoding of universes and values. A representation-complexity source and explicit encoding model are required.

children.title: Complement-Density Regimes
children.top_down_role: Tuple-density settings affecting the suitability of negative representation.

assumptions_latex: A relation has finite assignment universe \(U\), allowed set \(A\subseteq U\), and forbidden set \(F=U\setminus A\).
Storage cost is proportional to the number of explicitly listed complete tuples.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Negative storage is smaller exactly when \(|F|<|A|\), equivalently when \(|A|/|U|>1/2\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact explicit-list size comparison for complementary relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tuple-count comparison only; propagation overhead may shift the practical crossover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit positive table stores \(|A|=\rho|U|\) tuples, whereas its negative complement stores \(|F|=(1-\rho)|U|\) tuples. Hence the negative representation is strictly smaller when \(\rho>1/2\), the positive representation is strictly smaller when \(\rho<1/2\), and their tuple counts agree when \(\rho=1/2\). This threshold concerns representation size and does not assert equal filtering cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: By tuple count, list forbidden tuples when allowed assignments exceed half the universe; this does not by itself determine propagation speed.
knowledge_statements.title: Complement-Density Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-half threshold follows under the stated tuple-count storage model and fits the leaf, but no representation source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Short-Tuple Coverage Regimes
children.top_down_role: Constraint structures that admit effective coverage through generalized tuples.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity of minimizing an exact positive short-table cover when the entire finite assignment universe and target membership are explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the finite universe \(U\) and membership of every \(s\in U\) in \(A\) are explicitly represented. Given \(k\), deciding whether there are at most \(k\) short tuples \(P\) with \(A=\bigcup_{p\in P}[p]\) is NP-complete. A proposed cover is checkable in polynomial time in this explicit-universe encoding, but finding a minimum-cardinality exact cover is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With an explicitly enumerated universe, finding the fewest wildcard cylinders that cover exactly the target relation is NP-hard.
assumptions_latex: The full finite assignment universe and target-relation membership are explicitly enumerated.
Every candidate short tuple must cover no assignment outside the target relation.
The threshold \(k\) is part of the input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists P:\ |P|\le k\land A=\bigcup_{p\in P}[p]\text{ is NP-complete under the explicit-universe encoding}.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum Exact Short-Tuple Cover Hardness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence for Boolean-domain positive short tables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When every coordinate is Boolean, each short tuple is the conjunction of the literals fixing its specified coordinates, and a positive short table is the disjunction of those conjunctions. Thus exact short-tuple coverage of a Boolean relation is exactly a DNF representation of its characteristic function; overlap means that an assignment satisfies multiple terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over Boolean domains, positive short tables are precisely DNF formulas, with each short tuple acting as a conjunction term.
assumptions_latex: Every coordinate universe is \(\{0,1\}\).
Short tuples use positive wildcard-cylinder semantics.

notation.meaning: Characteristic function of the target relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean DNF Correspondence

assumptions_latex: A positive short table \(P\) is defined over \(U=\prod_{i=1}^rU_i\).
Each short tuple \(p\) denotes the cylinder \([p]\) of its complete extensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete coverage holds exactly when \(U=\bigcup_{p\in P}[p]\); relative coverage of a relation \(A\) holds exactly when \(A\subseteq\bigcup_{p\in P}[p]\).

notation.meaning: Multiplicity with which assignment \(s\) is covered.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: set-cover characterization of wildcard short-tuple coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage predicates for wildcard short tuples, including gaps and overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The collection \(P\) completely covers \(U\) if and only if \(\forall s\in U,\ \kappa_P(s)\geq1\), equivalently \(U=\bigcup_{p\in P}[p]\). It covers a target relation \(A\) if and only if \(\forall s\in A,\ \kappa_P(s)\geq1\). Coverage is exact for \(A\) if additionally \(\forall s\in U\setminus A,\ \kappa_P(s)=0\). The representation is disjoint exactly when \(\kappa_P(s)\leq1\) for every \(s\in U\); otherwise cylinders overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Short tuples cover a target relation when every allowed complete assignment extends one; exact coverage additionally excludes all forbidden assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Short-Tuple Coverage Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coverage, exactness, and overlap conditions are internally consistent and the content kind fits, but the record lacks a short-table source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity of forward-backward filtering for a deterministic finite automaton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m=\sum_{i=1}^n|D_i|\). With constant-time deterministic transition lookup, computing all forward and backward state sets and testing every position-value support takes \(O(|Q|m)\) time in a direct implementation and \(O(n|Q|)\) state-set space. On the explicitly unfolded layered transition graph, the same computation is linear in its vertices and compatible arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular-constraint filtering is linear in the unfolded compatible transition graph, or O(|Q| times total domain size) directly.
assumptions_latex: M=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\text{ is deterministic}.
Transition lookup and state-set membership take constant time.
knowledge_statements.title: Layered Automaton Filtering Complexity

assumptions_latex: The variables are \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) with finite domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\subseteq\Sigma\).
A deterministic finite automaton \(M=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\) specifies the accepted words.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After filtering, \(a\in D_i\) remains exactly when it occurs at position \(i\) in some accepted word compatible with every current domain.

notation.meaning: deterministic finite automaton defining the regular constraint
states reachable after positions 1 through i
states from which an accepting suffix after position i exists

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-consistency filtering for a regular constraint represented by a deterministic finite automaton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R_0=\{q_0\}\) and compute \(R_i=\{\delta(q,a):q\in R_{i-1},\ a\in D_i\}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Initialize \(S_n=F\) and compute \(S_{i-1}=\{q\in Q:\exists a\in D_i,\ \delta(q,a)\in S_i\}\) backward. For each position \(i\), delete \(a\in D_i\) unless there exists \(q\in R_{i-1}\) with \(\delta(q,a)\in S_i\). Failure is reported if a domain becomes empty; otherwise the reduced domains are returned. Each retained value has a complete accepting support, so the resulting regular constraint is domain consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and backward automaton reachability removes exactly those symbols that cannot occur at their position in any currently feasible accepted word.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular-Constraint Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward–backward filtering algorithm is mathematically coherent and fits this algorithm container, but no inspectable source is cited for its domain-consistency claim.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case complexity for binary-normal-form grammar filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be in binary normal form, let \(n\) be the sequence length, and let \(P_2\) and \(P_1\) be its binary and terminal productions. A CYK-style chart examines \(O(n^2)\) spans and \(O(n)\) split points per span, giving \(O(|P_2|n^3+|P_1|n)\) time and \(O(|N|n^2)\) Boolean chart space. A top-down support pass may rescan successful production-split alternatives within the same asymptotic time without materializing all witnesses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary-normal-form grammar filtering has cubic worst-case dependence on sequence length and quadratic chart space.
assumptions_latex: G=(N,\Sigma,P,S)\text{ is in binary normal form}.
Terminal-domain membership is testable in constant time.
review_flags: Materializing every successful production-split witness can require additional space.
knowledge_statements.title: Cubic Chart-Filtering Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ambiguity Does Not Change Support Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of grammar ambiguity on exact value support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a context-free grammar \(G\), a value \(a\in D_i\) is supported exactly when there exists a domain-compatible word \(w\in L(G)\) with \(w_i=a\). Multiple parse trees for the same word do not create different variable assignments and do not alter this existential support condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Grammar ambiguity can create many parses, but filtering depends only on whether at least one compatible parse supports a value.
assumptions_latex: X_1,\ldots,X_n\text{ range over terminal symbols}.
The grammar constraint requires the resulting word to belong to \(L(G)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\in D_i\text{ is supported}\iff\exists w\in L(G):w_i=a\land\forall k\;w_k\in D_k.
knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguity Does Not Change Support Semantics

assumptions_latex: The variables are \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) with finite terminal domains \(D_i\subseteq\Sigma\).
A context-free grammar \(G=(N,\Sigma,P,S)\) defines the permitted length-\(n\) words.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The remaining value \(a\in D_i\) has a parse-tree support for some domain-compatible word generated by \(G\).

notation.meaning: nonterminal A derives a compatible substring occupying positions i through j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chart-based domain-consistency filtering for a fixed-length context-free grammar constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convert \(G\) to an equivalent binary normal form, treating any necessary empty-word case separately. Build a chart in which \(T[A,i,j]\) holds when nonterminal \(A\) derives a word of length \(j-i+1\) whose symbol at every position \(k\) belongs to \(D_k\). Compute the chart bottom-up from terminal productions and binary productions. Mark entries participating in a derivation of \(T[S,1,n]\) by a top-down support pass. Delete \(a\in D_i\) unless a marked terminal production generating \(a\) covers position \(i\). Report failure if \(T[S,1,n]\) is false; otherwise return the reduced domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parsing chart and support pass delete each terminal value that belongs to no grammar derivation compatible with the current domains.
knowledge_statements.title: Grammar-Constraint Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The chart and support-pass formulation fits grammar-constraint filtering, but the normal-form and domain-consistency claims lack an inspectable authoritative citation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity of one filtering pass on an explicit layered acyclic decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an explicitly stored layered DAG \(B=(V,E)\), testing arc labels against their layer domains, forward reachability, backward co-reachability, and supported-label collection each require at most one scan of the relevant vertices and arcs. One complete pass therefore takes \(O(|V|+|E|)\) time and \(O(|V|)\) auxiliary marking space, or \(O(|V|+|E|)\) space including the diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact path filtering of an explicit layered decision diagram is linear in its vertices and arcs.
assumptions_latex: B=(V,E)\text{ is explicitly stored, layered, and acyclic}.
Arc-label membership in the corresponding domain is testable in constant time.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Time Filtering in Diagram Size

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filtering guarantees for exact, restricted, and relaxed decision diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_B\) be the relation represented by accepting paths of \(B\), and let \(R\) be the intended relation. Path filtering is domain consistent for \(R_B\). If \(R_B=R\), it is domain consistent for \(R\). If \(R_B\subsetneq R\), deleting values unsupported in \(B\) is not generally sound for \(R\). If \(R\subsetneq R_B\), every deletion remains sound for \(R\), but paths in \(R_B\setminus R\) can preserve values having no support in \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filtering is exact for the diagram's own relation; restricted diagrams can cause unsound deletions, while relaxed diagrams are sound but may miss deletions.
assumptions_latex: R_B\text{ is the set of tuples labeling accepting paths of }B.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_B=R\Rightarrow\text{exact filtering};\qquad R\subseteq R_B\Rightarrow\text{sound but potentially incomplete filtering}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Boundary for Approximate Diagrams

assumptions_latex: A layered acyclic decision diagram has layers \(V_0,\ldots,V_n\), a root \(r\in V_0\), and accepting terminals \(T\subseteq V_n\).
Every edge from \(V_{i-1}\) to \(V_i\) carries a value in the finite domain of \(X_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The filtered domains contain exactly the labels of root-to-accepting paths compatible with all current domains.

notation.meaning: current domain of variable at layer i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact domain filtering on a layered acyclic decision diagram encoding feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Delete every edge \(e\) between layers \(V_{i-1}\) and \(V_i\) for which \(\lambda(e)\notin D_i\). In a forward pass, mark vertices reachable from \(r\) through undeleted edges; in a backward pass, mark vertices that can reach some terminal in \(T\).
