Retain precisely those edges whose tail is forward reachable and whose head is backward reachable. Replace each domain by \(D_i'=\{\lambda(e):e\text{ is a retained edge from }V_{i-1}\text{ to }V_i\}\). Report failure if no accepting terminal is reachable; otherwise return \(D_1',\ldots,D_n'\), which are domain consistent relative to the represented relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pruning incompatible edges and vertices outside root-to-terminal paths leaves exactly the values supported by assignments represented in the decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Diagram Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The layered path-pruning algorithm is precise and appropriate for this container, but its exact domain-consistency claim has no cited source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap-safe support filtering for an integer-weighted layered automaton with a total-cost domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb Z\) be the current admissible set of total costs. Define \(A_i(q)\) as the costs of domain-compatible paths from the initial state to \(q\) after \(i\) symbols and \(B_i(q)\) as the costs of compatible paths from \(q\) after layer \(i\) to an accepting state. Compute these sets by forward and backward set propagation. A value \(a\in D_i\) is supported exactly when some transition \(e=(q,a,q')\) and costs \(\alpha\in A_{i-1}(q)\), \(\beta\in B_i(q')\) satisfy \(\alpha+w(e)+\beta\in C\). Delete unsupported values, replace \(C\) by the attainable accepting costs in \(C\), and report failure if that intersection is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tracking attainable cost sets, rather than only extrema, gives exact filtering even when reachable costs have gaps.
assumptions_latex: The layered automaton is finite and acyclic over the fixed sequence length.
Transition weights and admissible total costs are integers.

notation.meaning: attainable compatible prefix costs at state q after layer i
attainable compatible accepting-suffix costs from state q

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Attainable-Cost Filtering

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity distinction between exact gapped-cost support and one-sided cost bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume nonnegative integer weights and retain only costs in \(\{0,\ldots,U\}\). If \(M\) is the number of transition incidences in the unfolded layered graph, attainable prefix and suffix sets require \(O(MU)\) elementary Boolean work and \(O(n|Q|U)\) bits. Exact support tests for an arbitrary admissible set \(C\subseteq\{0,\ldots,U\}\) admit the conservative bound \(O(MU^2)\) by enumerating prefix-suffix cost pairs. These bounds are pseudo-polynomial when \(U\) is binary encoded. In contrast, filtering only \(cost\le U\) requires least prefix and suffix costs and is polynomial in the layered graph size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact filtering for gapped integer costs is pseudo-polynomial in the numeric cost range, whereas a one-sided upper bound uses graph-polynomial shortest-path recurrences.
assumptions_latex: 0\le w(e)\le U\text{ and costs above }U\text{ are irrelevant}.
The automaton is represented as a finite layered DAG.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{sets}=O(MU),\quad T_{exact\ support}=O(MU^2),\quad S=O(n|Q|U)\text{ bits};\qquad cost\le U\text{ filtering is graph-polynomial}.

notation.meaning: number of transition incidences in the unfolded layered graph

review_flags: Bit-parallel set operations or specialized admissible-cost domains can improve the conservative elementary-operation bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Polynomial Cost-Domain Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to treating minimum and maximum path costs as an exact attainable interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a one-symbol weighted automaton has exactly two accepting transitions labeled \(a\), with costs \(0\) and \(2\). The minimum and maximum supported costs for \(a\) are \(0\) and \(2\), but cost \(1\) is unattainable. Thus for \(C=\{1\}\), equivalently \([1,1]\), value \(a\) has no support although \(1\) lies between its minimum and maximum path costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepting paths of costs zero and two show that extrema do not certify an intermediate cost of one.
assumptions_latex: The weighted automaton has no other accepting path.

notation.meaning: attainable accepting-path costs using value a

knowledge_statements.title: Min-Max Gap Counterexample

assumptions_latex: The finite domains satisfy \(D_i\subseteq\Sigma\), and a weighted automaton assigns each length-\(n\) word a path cost in an ordered additive cost structure.
The constraint requires an accepting path with total cost in the current admissible interval \([L,U]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every retained value lies on an accepting domain-compatible path whose total cost belongs to \([L,U]\).

notation.meaning: least compatible prefix cost reaching state q after layer i
least compatible accepting suffix cost from state q after layer i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-aware support filtering for a layered min-plus weighted automaton with an admissible cost interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute forward and backward dynamic programs for the least compatible prefix and suffix costs. For a transition \(e=(q,a,q')\) at layer \(i\), its least supported accepting cost is \(p_{i-1}(q)+w(e)+s_i(q')\). Delete \(a\in D_i\) if every layer-\(i\) transition labeled \(a\) has this quantity greater than \(U\). When the lower bound \(L\) is restrictive, analogously compute greatest attainable prefix and suffix costs and delete \(a\) when every labeled transition has greatest supported cost below \(L\). Report failure when no accepting path has cost in \([L,U]\); otherwise return the reduced domains and attainable cost bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and backward cost dynamic programs remove symbols that cannot lie on an accepting path within the permitted total-cost interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-Automaton Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Minimum and maximum path costs do not establish the existence of a cost in [L,U] when attainable costs have gaps. Exact interval-support filtering requires attainable-cost sets or additional assumptions on the cost structure; no source resolves the semantics.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Filtering for a Constant Element Array
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct domain-consistency filter for Y=c_I.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed constants \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\), set \(D_I'=\{j\in D_I:c_j\in D_Y\}\) and \(D_Y'=D_Y\cap\{c_j:j\in D_I'\}\). Failure occurs exactly when either reduced domain is empty; otherwise every retained index is supported by its constant and every retained result value is supplied by a retained index.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain exactly indices whose constants remain possible results and result values supplied by retained indices.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(Y\) have finite domains.
Every array entry is a fixed constant and \(D_I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Filtering for a Constant Element Array

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact filtering for Y=A_I when all participating variable objects are distinct.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(I\), \(Y\), and all variable entries \(A_j\) are pairwise distinct variable objects. Iterate: delete \(j\in D_I\) when \(D_{A_j}\cap D_Y=\varnothing\); delete \(y\in D_Y\) when no remaining \(j\) has \(y\in D_{A_j}\); and, when \(D_I=\{j\}\), replace both \(D_{A_j}\) and \(D_Y\) by their intersection. Constant entries use singleton domains. Report failure if a required domain becomes empty. At the fixed point every retained value of every participating variable has support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For distinct index, result, and entry variables, fixed-point index/result pruning plus intersection of a forced entry enforces domain consistency.
assumptions_latex: \(D_I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and all domains are finite.
The variable objects \(I,Y,A_1,\ldots,A_m\) are pairwise distinct; constants are treated as singleton-domain entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The fixed point is domain consistent for }Y=A_I.
review_flags: The pairwise-distinct variable-object assumption is essential to the completeness claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Consistent Element Filtering Without Aliasing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary of entry-wise element rules when positions share variable objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_1=A_2=Z\), \(D_I=\{1,2\}\), \(D_Z=\{0,1\}\), and \(D_Y=\{0\}\). Every remaining index selects \(Z\), so \(Y=A_I\) is equivalent to \(Y=Z\), making \(1\in D_Z\) unsupported. A rule that intersects an entry with \(Y\) only when \(I\) is a singleton does not delete it. Aliased formulations therefore require support tests over variable identities, not independent position domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all remaining positions alias one variable, that variable is selected even when the index is not fixed.
assumptions_latex: Array positions are permitted to reference the same finite-domain variable.

notation.meaning: variable shared by multiple array positions

knowledge_statements.title: Aliased Entries Require Identity-Aware Support

assumptions_latex: The index variable \(I\) has finite domain \(D_I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the result variable is \(Y\), and array entries are variables or constants \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\).
All variable domains are finite, and the constraint is \(Y=A_I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting domains are domain consistent for \(Y=A_I\).

notation.meaning: entry selected when I equals j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-consistency filtering for the variable-index element constraint \(Y=A_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Iterate the following deletions to a fixed point. Remove \(j\in D_I\) whenever \(D_{A_j}\cap D_Y=\varnothing\). Remove \(y\in D_Y\) whenever no \(j\in D_I\) satisfies \(y\in D_{A_j}\). For every \(j\in D_I\), remove \(a\in D_{A_j}\) when \(D_I=\{j\}\) and \(a\notin D_Y\); entries whose indices are not forced require no such deletion because they need not be selected. Report failure if any required domain becomes empty. At the fixed point, every index and result value has a compatible selection, and every value of a forced entry is supported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Element filtering removes impossible indices and unsupported result values, and intersects the selected entry with the result whenever the index is fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Element-Constraint Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-point rules are standard for distinct array-entry variables or constants, but the record does not specify whether entries may alias one another or Y. That affects the domain-consistency conclusion, and no source fixes the intended semantics.

children.title: Sum-Constraint Filtering
children.top_down_role: Propagation specialized to aggregate sum constraints.

assumptions_latex: The variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) have finite integer domains, and the constraint is \(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\mathrel{\bowtie} b\), where \(\bowtie\in\{=,\leq,\geq\}\).
Filtering uses domain extrema and exact integer arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every deletion follows from an infeasible residual interval for the sum constraint.

notation.meaning: minimum and maximum of the domain of X_i
minimum and maximum attainable interval bounds for the total sum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds filtering for unit-coefficient integer sum equalities and inequalities.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(L=\sum_{i=1}^n\ell_i\) and \(U=\sum_{i=1}^n u_i\). For equality, failure occurs if \(b\notin[L,U]\); update each variable by intersecting its domain with \([b-(U-u_i),\ b-(L-\ell_i)]\). For \(\sum_iX_i\leq b\), failure occurs if \(L>b\), and delete values \(x\in D_i\) with \(x+L-\ell_i>b\). For \(\sum_iX_i\geq b\), failure occurs if \(U<b\), and delete values \(x\in D_i\) with \(x+U-u_i<b\). Iterate after domain changes and return the fixed-point domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual minimum and maximum sums tighten each variable and detect failure for unit-coefficient sum equalities or inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Sum-Constraint Filtering

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic-operation cost of one unit-coefficient bounds-filtering sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(L=\sum_i\ell_i\) and \(U=\sum_i u_i\) once in \(O(n)\) arithmetic operations. Each residual pair \(L-\ell_i,U-u_i\) and its bound update then costs \(O(1)\). Hence one complete residual-sum sweep costs \(O(n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintaining aggregate extrema makes one complete residual-sum filtering sweep linear in the number of variables.
assumptions_latex: Exact arithmetic operations have unit cost.
Intersecting a bounds representation with an integer interval takes constant time.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Time Residual-Sum Sweep

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Bounds Can Retain an Unsupported Interior Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary between residual bounds filtering and domain consistency on holey domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D(x)=\{0,1,2\}\), \(D(y)=\{0,2\}\), and \(x+y=2\), residual bounds leave \([0,2]\) for \(x\), although \(x=1\) has no support. The only satisfying tuples are \((0,2)\) and \((2,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual bounds can retain an unsupported interior value when another variable has a domain hole.
assumptions_latex: Filtering uses only current domain extrema.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Bounds Can Retain an Unsupported Interior Value

children.title: Linear-Constraint Filtering
children.top_down_role: Propagation for weighted linear relations over finite domains.

assumptions_latex: The variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) have finite integer domains, coefficients \(a_i\in\mathbb Z\), and right-hand side \(b\in\mathbb Z\).
The constraint is \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_iX_i\mathrel{\bowtie}b\), with \(\bowtie\in\{=,\leq,\geq\}\), and arithmetic is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned domains satisfy bounds consistency with respect to the interval relaxation of the linear constraint.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-aware bounds filtering for a single finite-domain integer linear constraint.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(m_i=\min_{x\in D_i}a_ix\), \(M_i=\max_{x\in D_i}a_ix\), \(L=\sum_i m_i\), and \(U=\sum_i M_i\). For equality, delete \(x\in D_i\) when \(a_ix+[L-m_i,U-M_i]\) excludes \(b\). For a less-than inequality, delete \(x\) when \(a_ix+L-m_i>b\); for a greater-than inequality, delete \(x\) when \(a_ix+U-M_i<b\). Apply sign-correct endpoint rounding when converting contribution bounds back to bounds on \(X_i\). Iterate to a fixed point, reporting failure when the relevant aggregate interval cannot meet \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sign-aware residual contribution bounds prune values and detect infeasibility in one integer linear equality or inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Constraint Filtering

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interval Fixed Point Can Miss Divisibility Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete incompleteness of residual interval filtering for integer equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(2X+2Y+2Z=3\) with \(D_X=D_Y=D_Z=\{0,1\}\). For either value of any selected variable, the required residual is \(3\) or \(1\), both contained in the other two terms' residual interval \([0,4]\); residual interval filtering therefore deletes nothing. Every attainable left-hand side is even, so the equality is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual intervals leave every value in 2X+2Y+2Z=3 although parity makes the equality infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y,Z\) are binary integer variables.
Filtering uses only residual minimum and maximum contributions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The interval filter has a nonempty fixed point, but the equality has no integer solution}.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval Fixed Point Can Miss Divisibility Infeasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between polynomial residual-bound propagation and exact domain consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary variables and binary-encoded integer coefficients, deciding whether a designated value extends to a solution of \(\sum_i a_iX_i=b\) is NP-complete through the subset-sum special case. Consequently, complete domain filtering for unrestricted finite-domain integer linear equalities is NP-hard, whereas one residual-interval propagation round uses polynomially many arithmetic operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact value support for a binary linear equality is NP-complete, so residual-bound propagation cannot generally enforce domain consistency in polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\in\{0,1\}\), with coefficients and right-hand side encoded in binary.
Support assigns every remaining variable within its current domain.
knowledge_statements.title: NP-Hardness of Complete Linear-Equality Filtering

children.title: Sum–Linear Specialization
children.top_down_role: Structural relationship between sum constraints and general linear constraints.

assumptions_latex: The linear constraint has coefficients \(a_i=1\) for every \(i\).
The variables have finite integer domains and all aggregate computations use exact arithmetic.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(a_i=1\) for all \(i\), the term bounds in linear filtering satisfy \(m_i=\ell_i\) and \(M_i=u_i\). Consequently, for \(\sum_iX_i=b\), the residual test \(x+[L-\ell_i,U-u_i]\ni b\) is equivalent to retaining \(x\in[b-(U-u_i),b-(L-\ell_i)]\). For \(\sum_iX_i\leq b\), it becomes \(x+L-\ell_i\leq b\); for \(\sum_iX_i\geq b\), it becomes \(x+U-u_i\geq b\). Thus no coefficient-sign branching or division is needed, and the general linear bounds filter specializes to the sum filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With every coefficient equal to one, general linear residual bounds become exactly the simpler sum-filtering formulas.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Sensitive Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contrast between coefficient-insensitive interval propagation and coefficient-sensitive reachable-sum filtering for a 0–1 linear equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Computing all term extrema and one round of residual interval filtering takes \(O(n)\) arithmetic operations, apart from domain-update costs. A standard dense-table dynamic program for reachable weighted partial sums uses \(O(nW)\) time and \(O(W)\) working memory, where \(W=\sum_{i=1}^n |a_i|\). This bound is pseudo-polynomial because \(W\) may be exponential in the binary encoding length of the coefficients. Small coefficient sums therefore permit exact reachable-sum filtering at pseudo-polynomial cost, whereas interval filtering does not enumerate the coefficient-sized sum range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For binary variables, interval filtering takes linear arithmetic work per round, while dense exact reachable-sum filtering is pseudo-polynomial in the sum of the absolute coefficients.
assumptions_latex: The constraint is \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_iX_i=b\), where \(X_i\in\{0,1\}\), \(a_i\in\mathbb Z\), and \(b\in\mathbb Z\).
Reachable sums are represented by a dense table after shifting the possible sum interval to nonnegative indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dense exact reachable-sum filtering has time complexity \(O(nW)\) and working-memory complexity \(O(W)\), with \(W=\sum_{i=1}^n|a_i|\), while one residual interval-filtering round uses \(O(n)\) arithmetic operations apart from domain updates.

Thus exact support filtering is not expected to be polynomial in \(n+\sum_i\log(1+|a_i|)+\log(1+|b|)\), whereas an \(O(nW)\) reachable-sum bound is polynomial when coefficients are unary encoded or \(W=\sum_i|a_i|\) is polynomially bounded.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Wraparound Can Falsely Reject a Feasible Linear Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete unsoundness from unchecked fixed-width aggregate bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In signed 8-bit two's-complement arithmetic, consider \(100X+100Y-100Z=100\) with \(X,Y,Z\in\{0,1\}\). The assignment \((1,1,1)\) is feasible and the right-hand side is representable. An unchecked computation of the maximum term contribution sum forms \(100+100+0=200\), which wraps to \(-56\). Using this corrupted upper bound can exclude the representable target \(100\) and falsely report failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unchecked 8-bit aggregation wraps the mathematical upper bound 200 to -56 and can reject a feasible constraint with representable target 100.
assumptions_latex: Signed addition uses modulo-256 two's-complement wraparound.
Overflow is not checked before the aggregate bound is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Wraparound Can Falsely Reject a Feasible Linear Constraint

assumptions_latex: Signed intermediate arithmetic uses a fixed-width range \([I_{\min},I_{\max}]\).
A linear filter computes products \(a_ix\), aggregate bounds, and residual expressions from finite integer domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Machine-arithmetic filtering is sound only when every possible intermediate lies in \([I_{\min},I_{\max}]\), or when checked or wider arithmetic replaces overflowing operations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for fixed-width implementations of linear and sum propagation.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sufficient precondition for safely evaluating every full weighted sum is \([-S,S]\subseteq[I_{\min},I_{\max}]\), where \(S=\sum_i|a_i|B_i\). Implementations must additionally check each product and any transient expression, such as \(L-m_i\) or \(U-M_i\), because evaluation order can overflow even when the final mathematical result is representable. If unchecked arithmetic wraps or saturates outside its specified semantics, computed lower bounds may increase or upper bounds may decrease spuriously, causing deletion of supported values or failure declarations. Sound filtering therefore requires checked operations, sufficiently wide integers, arbitrary-precision arithmetic, or a proven bound for every intermediate expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unchecked fixed-width overflow can reverse or corrupt propagation bounds; soundness requires representable intermediates or checked, wider, or arbitrary-precision arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.title: Arithmetic Overflow Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R_0=\{(0,0)\}\). For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), form \(R_i=\{(c+w_ix,p+v_ix):(c,p)\in R_{i-1},\ x\in D_i,\ c+w_ix\leq C\}\), merging identical states and retaining all value information needed by the bound \(P\). Compute analogous suffix states. Delete \(x\in D_i\) unless some compatible prefix state and suffix state combine with choice \(x\) to give total weight at most \(C\) and, when present, total value at least \(P\). Report failure if no final state satisfies the bounds; otherwise return the reduced domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prefix and suffix knapsack dynamic programs remove each binary choice that cannot extend to a capacity-feasible completion meeting any required value bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conservative pseudo-polynomial bound for filtering binary capacity-and-profit knapsack constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=1+\sum_i|v_i|\). For fixed literal \(X_k=x\), feasibility of \(\sum_iw_iX_i\le C\) and \(\sum_iv_iX_i\ge P\) can be decided by a dense dynamic program over capacity and the shifted profit interval in \(O(nCQ)\) time and \(O(CQ)\) working memory. Testing at most two literals for each binary variable independently therefore enforces domain consistency in \(O(n^2CQ)\) time and \(O(CQ)\) working memory. These bounds are pseudo-polynomial in binary-encoded numeric data; prefix/suffix reuse may improve them but requires representation-specific combination costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense capacity-profit dynamic program gives a safe pseudo-polynomial O(n²CQ) bound for testing all binary literals exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\in\{0,1\}\), \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), \(v_i\in\mathbb Z\), and \(C\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why independent propagation of binary nonoverlap constraints need not achieve global disjunctive domain consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Arc consistency on every binary nonoverlap disjunction guarantees only that each endpoint value has support against each other activity separately. Those pairwise supports may require mutually incompatible orders or start times, so the binary fixpoint can retain a value having no completion to a schedule of all activities. Global disjunctive filtering can therefore be strictly stronger.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact support filtering for finite-domain nonoverlap on a unary resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The disjunctive-resource constraint is the conjunction, over all distinct activities \(i,j\), of \(S_i+p_i\leq S_j\) or \(S_j+p_j\leq S_i\). For each candidate \(s\in D_{S_i}\), test whether there exist starts \(s_j\in D_{S_j}\) for all \(j\neq i\) such that \(S_i=s\) and all occupied half-open intervals are pairwise disjoint. Delete \(s\) exactly when no such completion exists. Repeat after deletions until no domain changes; report failure if a domain becomes empty. The returned domains are domain consistent for the global disjunctive-resource constraint, independently of the search procedure used for the support tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact disjunctive-resource filtering removes a start time precisely when it cannot be extended to a pairwise nonoverlapping schedule.

Then \(est_i=0\), \(lst_i=2\), and \(CP_i=[2,2)=\varnothing\), so \(P(t)=0\) everywhere and timetable propagation detects no overload or unsupported start. Nevertheless, all three activities must execute within \([0,4)\), whose capacity is \(4\), while their total required processing is \(6\); the instance is infeasible.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compulsory-part timetable propagation for one cumulative resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each activity define \(est_i=\min D_i\), \(lst_i=\max D_i\), and its compulsory part \(CP_i=[lst_i,est_i+p_i)\) when \(lst_i<est_i+p_i\), otherwise \(CP_i=\varnothing\). Construct the profile \(P(t)=\sum_{i:t\in CP_i}r_i\). Report failure if \(P(t)>R\) for some \(t\). For each activity \(i\), form \(P_{-i}(t)=\sum_{j\ne i:t\in CP_j}r_j\) and delete every \(s\in D_i\) for which some \(t\in[s,s+p_i)\) satisfies \(P_{-i}(t)+r_i>R\). Recompute bounds and compulsory parts until no domain changes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic edge-finding condition for nonpreemptive activities sharing a unary resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the set of schedules satisfying the current release times, deadlines, durations, and pairwise nonoverlap constraints. For a nonempty activity set \(\Omega\) and \(i\notin\Omega\), the forward edge-finding condition is \[\forall\sigma\in S\;\forall j\in\Omega:\ C_j(\sigma)\le S_i(\sigma).\] When this condition is certified, activity \(i\) must occur after the right edge of \(\Omega\), so the sound propagation is \[S_i\ge \min_{\sigma\in S}\max_{j\in\Omega}C_j(\sigma).\] The time-reversed condition analogously forces \(i\) before every activity in \(\Omega\) and tightens its latest completion time.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case cost without incremental aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=|I|\), at most \(n^2\) candidate intervals are examined. Computing each \(W(a,b)\) by scanning all activities takes \(O(n)\) arithmetic operations; hence direct enumeration takes \(O(n^3)\) time and \(O(n)\) auxiliary space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct critical-interval checker uses cubic time and linear auxiliary space.
assumptions_latex: q_i(a,b)\text{ is evaluated in constant arithmetic time}.
|A|\le n\text{ and }|B|\le n.
knowledge_statements.title: Complexity of Direct Critical-Interval Enumeration

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Energetic Bound Filtering by Hypothetical Restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound finite-domain bound filtering using energetic overload detection as a rejection oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a hypothetical tightening \(H\) of an activity's start or completion bound, temporarily impose \(H\), recompute the affected \(est_i\) and \(lct_i\), and run the finite critical-interval energetic overload check. If some interval satisfies \(\sum_i r_iq_i(a,b)>R(b-a)\), then \(H\), and every stronger bound restriction that implies \(H\), has no feasible extension and may be rejected. Repeating retained strict bound deletions reaches a fixpoint whenever the representable bound domains are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tentatively impose a bound and reject it, together with stronger restrictions, when it creates a certified energetic overload.
assumptions_latex: Activities are mandatory and nonpreemptive on one cumulative resource.
Every overload check uses the bounds after imposing the hypothetical restriction.
Representable bound domains are finite.
Only strict, logically entailed bound deletions are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every rejected bound restriction has no feasible extension, and repeated strict filtering terminates}.
knowledge_statements.title: Energetic Bound Filtering by Hypothetical Restriction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Energetic Inequalities Are Not Sufficient for Nonpreemptive Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packing boundary for the minimum-overlap interval-energy condition on a cumulative resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a cumulative resource have capacity \(R=3\). Two mandatory nonpreemptive activities have common release time \(0\), common deadline \(3\), durations \(p_1=p_2=2\), and demands \(r_1=r_2=2\). They cannot overlap because \(r_1+r_2=4>3\), while sequential execution requires four time units, so the instance is infeasible. Nevertheless, every interval \([a,b)\) satisfies \(\sum_i r_iq_i(a,b)\le3(b-a)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two demand-two, duration-two activities in a three-unit window pass every minimum-overlap energy test at capacity three but cannot be packed nonpreemptively.
assumptions_latex: The activities are mandatory and nonpreemptive.
knowledge_statements.title: Energetic Inequalities Are Not Sufficient for Nonpreemptive Feasibility
Energetic Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval-energy feasibility condition for a nonpreemptive cumulative resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let activity \(i\) have earliest start \(est_i\), latest completion \(lct_i\), duration \(p_i\), demand \(r_i\), earliest completion \(ect_i=est_i+p_i\), and latest start \(lst_i=lct_i-p_i\). For an interval \([a,b)\), the minimum processing time that every feasible placement of activity \(i\) executes inside the interval is \[q_i(a,b)=\max\{0,\min(p_i,b-a,ect_i-a,b-lst_i)\}.\] Every feasible cumulative schedule satisfies \[\sum_i r_iq_i(a,b)\le R(b-a)\qquad\text{for every }a<b.\] Therefore, an interval violating this inequality certifies infeasibility. A tentative value or bound update may be rejected when it makes the same necessary inequality fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every interval must provide enough resource energy for the minimum amount of each nonpreemptive activity that must execute inside it; an energy overload proves infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive and have fixed positive durations and demands.
\(est_i+p_i\le lct_i\) for every activity.
\(R>0\) is the cumulative-resource capacity.

notation.meaning: earliest start, earliest completion, latest start, and latest completion of activity i
minimum processing of activity i forced into the interval
required resource energy in the interval

review_flags: The corrected minimum-overlap formula and energetic inequality require an authoritative scheduling reference with a specific locator.

children.title: Combined Scheduling Filters
children.top_down_role: Complementarity, dominance, and interaction among timetable, edge-finding, and energetic filters.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-aware worklist implementation of fair combined scheduling filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a queue with all constituent scheduling filters. Repeatedly remove an enabled filter \(F_j\), apply it, report failure if a domain becomes empty, and enqueue every filter whose watched input information changed. If the watch relation enqueues every filter that a change can enable, queue exhaustion returns the same common fixpoint as exhaustive fair iteration while avoiding executions whose inputs are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete dependency-aware worklist reaches the combined common fixpoint while skipping unaffected filters.
assumptions_latex: Filters are contracting, monotone, and solution preserving on a finite store.
The watch relation is complete: every filter potentially enabled by a change is eventually enqueued.

notation.meaning: Store when the worklist is exhausted.

knowledge_statements.title: Event-Driven Combined Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why invoking each constituent filter once need not compute combined filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Scheduling filters need not commute: a deletion by \(F_i\) can enable a deletion by \(F_j\), which may re-enable \(F_i\). Applying every filter only once, or indefinitely omitting an enabled filter, therefore need not reach a common fixpoint and can make the result depend on invocation order. Re-execution to quiescence under fairness is required for the common-fixpoint guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One pass or unfair activation can miss deductions because constituent filters may repeatedly enable one another.
assumptions_latex: At least two filters exchange deductions through shared domain information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_k\circ\cdots\circ F_1(D)\text{ need not be a common fixpoint}.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Pass and Unfair-Scheduling Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength of a common fixpoint relative to each constituent scheduling filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D^*\) be the greatest common fixpoint below \(D\) of contracting, monotone filters \(F_1,\ldots,F_k\). Then \(D^*\subseteq F_j(D)\subseteq D\) for every \(j\). Adding another sound contracting monotone filter can only preserve or reduce the resulting common fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combined fixpoint propagation is at least as strong as one application of any constituent, and adding a sound filter cannot weaken it.
assumptions_latex: Every constituent filter is contracting and monotone.
The greatest common fixpoint below the input is computed.

notation.meaning: Combined greatest common fixpoint below the input.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined-Filter Dominance
Combined Scheduling Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair fixpoint composition of sound timetable, edge-finding, and energetic propagators on finite domain stores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a finite domain store and let \(F_1,\ldots,F_k\) be contracting, monotone, solution-preserving scheduling filters, such as timetable, edge-finding, and energetic filters. Initialize \(D^{(0)}=D\). Repeatedly choose an enabled filter fairly and set \(D^{(m+1)}=F_j(D^{(m)})\). Stop with failure if a domain becomes empty; otherwise stop when \(F_j(D^*)=D^*\) for every \(j\). The descending iteration terminates on a finite store. Its nonfailure result is the greatest common fixpoint below \(D\), is independent of the fair activation order, and preserves exactly the solutions represented by \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combined filtering fairly applies monotone, contracting, solution-preserving scheduling filters until failure or their order-independent greatest common fixpoint is reached.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_j\) is contracting, monotone, and solution preserving on the domain-store order.
The domain-store lattice below \(D\) is finite.
Activation is fair until every filter is quiescent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates with failure or the greatest common fixpoint \(D^*\subseteq D\), while preserving all solutions.

notation.meaning: greatest common fixpoint below the input store

review_flags: A propagation fixpoint theorem and scheduling-composition reference with specific locators are required.

children.title: Graph-Structured Filtering Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Representative filtering interfaces; graph algorithms and routing formulations remain cross-linked.

children.title: Connectivity Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering for connected graph structures, including strength regimes and failure boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static propagation cost for the pure edge-Boolean spanning-connectivity constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A depth-first low-link traversal of (V,E_?) tests connectivity and identifies every bridge. One complete static propagation call therefore takes O(|V|+|E_?|) time and O(|V|) auxiliary space, apart from graph storage and emitted domain updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One DFS detects failure and every mandatory optional edge in linear time.
assumptions_latex: The possible graph is represented by adjacency lists.
The graph is finite and undirected.

notation.meaning: Edges permitted by the current Boolean domains.

review_flags: This is a static per-call bound, not an incremental backtracking bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Time Connectivity Propagation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete Edge Filtering for Spanning Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain consistency of a pure undirected spanning-connectivity constraint over Boolean edge variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E_1\subseteq E_? and require E_1\subseteq F\subseteq E_? with (V,F) connected. A completion exists exactly when (V,E_?) is connected. Conditional on feasibility, every permitted edge has selection support, while an optional edge e has exclusion support exactly when (V,E_?\setminus\{e\}) is connected. Thus complete filtering forces exactly the bridges of (V,E_?) and makes no other edge-literal deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Possible-graph connectivity and bridge detection completely filter the Boolean edge domains of pure spanning connectivity.
assumptions_latex: The graph is finite and undirected over a fixed spanning vertex set V.
No degree, cost, cardinality, or other side constraint is conjoined.
review_flags: Completeness is restricted to the pure connectivity interface without side constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete Edge Filtering for Spanning Connectivity
Connectivity Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bridge-based filtering for an undirected spanning-connectivity constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be undirected, with Boolean edge variables. Write \(E_1\) for forced edges and \(E_?\) for edges not forced absent, so every completion satisfies \(E_1\subseteq F\subseteq E_?\). Requiring \((V,F)\) to be connected yields two sound rules. If \((V,E_?)\) is disconnected, the constraint fails. If \(e\in E_?\) is a bridge of \((V,E_?)\), then every connected completion contains \(e\), so set its variable to one. More generally, every cut \(\delta(U)\) must retain at least one possible edge; if exactly one remains, that edge is forced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connectivity filtering fails when the possible graph is disconnected and forces the sole possible edge across any cut, including every possible-graph bridge.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
Every vertex must belong to the selected connected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Disconnected possible graphs fail, and singleton possible cuts force their unique edge.

notation.meaning: edge cut between U and its complement

review_flags: The graph facts are standard, but a source for their global-constraint filtering use is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The disconnected-graph, bridge, and singleton-cut rules are sound for spanning connectivity, but no global-constraint filtering source or exact locator is cited.

children.title: Tree Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering specialized to tree structures, spanning structural restrictions and pruning consequences.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-call complexity of complete filtering for the pure spanning-tree edge interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Connected-component labels for (V,E_1) detect a forced cycle and every optional edge whose selection closes one. A depth-first low-link traversal of (V,E_?) detects disconnection and every bridge. All unsupported Boolean edge values are therefore found in O(|V|+|E_?|) time and O(|V|) auxiliary space in a static propagation call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forced-cycle checks and possible-bridge detection completely filter the pure tree interface in linear time.
assumptions_latex: The possible graph is represented by adjacency lists.
The computation is a static propagation call.
review_flags: Incremental and backtrackable implementations have different amortized bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Time Static Tree Filtering

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete Filtering Characterization for a Spanning Tree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Boolean-edge support tests under a pure undirected spanning-tree constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E_1\subseteq E_?. A spanning tree T satisfying E_1\subseteq T\subseteq E_? exists exactly when (V,E_1) is acyclic and (V,E_?) is connected. At a feasible state, an optional edge e=uv has support for value one exactly when u and v are in different components of (V,E_1); it has support for value zero exactly when (V,E_?\setminus\{e\}) remains connected. Complete filtering therefore removes value one precisely from edges closing a forced-forest cycle and value zero precisely from bridges of the possible graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forced-cycle and possible-bridge rules together completely filter a pure spanning-tree constraint.
assumptions_latex: The graph is finite and undirected.
Every vertex must be spanned.
No side constraint restricts the chosen tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e=1\text{ is supported}\iff u,v\text{ are in distinct }E_1\text{-components},\quad e=0\text{ is supported}\iff (V,E_?\setminus\{e\})\text{ is connected}.

notation.meaning: An optional edge with endpoints u and v.

review_flags: Completeness is restricted to the pure spanning-tree interface without side constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete Filtering Characterization for a Spanning Tree
Tree Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cycle, cut, and bridge filtering for an undirected spanning-tree constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) have forced-edge set \(E_1\) and possible-edge set \(E_?\), and require a completion \(T\) with \(E_1\subseteq T\subseteq E_?\) that is a spanning tree. Failure follows if \((V,E_?)\) is disconnected, if \((V,E_1)\) contains a cycle, or if \(|E_1|>|V|-1\). Every bridge of \((V,E_?)\) is forced into \(T\). Conversely, any optional edge whose endpoints already lie in the same connected component of the forest \((V,E_1)\) is forced absent, because selecting it would create a cycle. These rules preserve every spanning-tree completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tree filtering combines connectivity checks with acyclicity: possible bridges are mandatory, while edges closing a forced cycle are forbidden.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite undirected graph.
\(E_1\subseteq E_?\subseteq E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated failure, forcing, and exclusion rules are necessary for every spanning-tree completion.
review_flags: A global-tree-constraint filtering reference with an exact locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated connectivity, cycle, bridge, and forced-forest rules are sound for an undirected spanning-tree constraint, but they lack a cited filtering reference with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Connectivity–Tree Interaction
children.top_down_role: Relations between general connectivity filters and tree-specific structural filtering.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete edge-domain filtering for a pure spanning-tree constraint obtained by combining the two structural filters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E_1\subseteq E_? in a finite undirected graph, with the sole requirement of a spanning tree T satisfying E_1\subseteq T\subseteq E_?. A completion exists exactly when (V,E_1) is a forest and (V,E_?) is connected. At a feasible state, an optional edge e=uv has selection support exactly when u and v lie in different components of (V,E_1), and it has exclusion support exactly when (V,E_?\setminus\{e\}) is connected. Hence forced-forest cycle exclusion together with possible-graph bridge forcing is generalized arc consistent. The equation |T|=|V|-1 is exact but yields no additional edge deletion at that joint fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a pure spanning-tree constraint, cycle filtering on forced edges plus bridge filtering on possible edges is complete.
assumptions_latex: The graph is finite and undirected over a fixed spanning vertex set.
No side constraint is conjoined with the spanning-tree requirement.
review_flags: The exact decomposition is restricted to the pure edge-Boolean spanning-tree constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Connectivity–Acyclicity Propagation Decomposition
Connectivity–Tree Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction of spanning connectivity, acyclicity, and selected-edge cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite undirected graph \((V,F)\) with \(V\ne\varnothing\), any two of the following conditions imply the third: \((V,F)\) is connected; \((V,F)\) is acyclic; and \(|F|=|V|-1\). Consequently, a propagator maintaining spanning connectivity may share cut deductions with a tree propagator, while the tree propagator may additionally use cycle exclusion and the cardinality equation. In particular, once \(|V|-1\) edges are forced, all remaining optional edges are absent; and if an acyclic forced forest has \(c\) components, every completion needs exactly \(c-1\) additional edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spanning tree is characterized by connectivity plus acyclicity or the correct edge count, enabling cut, cycle, and cardinality deductions to reinforce one another.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(F\) are finite.
The selected graph spans every vertex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Connectivity, acyclicity, and \(|F|=|V|-1\) are pairwise sufficient to imply the remaining condition.

notation.meaning: number of components of the forced forest

review_flags: A source connecting the standard tree characterization to propagator interaction is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-graph characterization is standard and the propagator interaction fits the container, but neither the characterization nor its propagation use has a cited source and specific locator.

children.title: Circuit Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering for circuit structures, including admissible graph regimes and pruning boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial matching-based necessary filtering for a successor-form Hamiltonian-circuit constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form the bipartite graph with one left and one right copy of \(V\), placing edge \((v_L,w_R)\) exactly when \(w\in D_v\). Every Hamiltonian circuit induces a perfect matching. Therefore absence of a perfect matching certifies infeasibility, and an arc \((v,w)\) may be deleted when its bipartite edge belongs to no perfect matching. Surviving matchings are only cycle covers and need not form one circuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfect-matching filtering enforces the predecessor-successor assignment relaxation, but a surviving cycle cover may contain several subtours.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and successor domains exclude self-arcs.
The bipartite graph explicitly represents the current successor domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
eg\exists	ext{ perfect matching}\implies
eg\exists	ext{ Hamiltonian circuit},\qquad e
otin igcup\mathcal M\implies e	ext{ is unsupported}.

notation.meaning: left successor-variable copy and right predecessor-value copy of vertices
set of perfect matchings in the bipartite domain graph

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment-Relaxation Filtering for Circuits

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary for exact value-support filtering of an unrestricted successor circuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an explicit directed graph \(H=(V,A)\) and a designated arc \(e\in A\), deciding whether \(H\) has a directed Hamiltonian circuit containing \(e\) is NP-complete. Consequently, enforcing domain consistency for an unrestricted circuit constraint is NP-hard, although matching, subtour, and connectivity necessary-condition filters are polynomial-time procedures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Designated-arc Hamiltonian-circuit support is NP-complete, so complete circuit filtering is NP-hard.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite directed graph represented explicitly.
Support for \(e\) means a Hamiltonian circuit containing \(e\).

notation.meaning: directed graph of currently allowed successor arcs

review_flags: NP-hardness concerns complete filtering, not the polynomial necessary-condition filters.
knowledge_statements.title: Hardness of Complete Circuit Filtering

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree and Connectivity Conditions Are Incomplete
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary of elementary structural tests for circuit feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=K^{\leftrightarrow}_{2,3}\), the complete bipartite graph with both orientations of every cross-part edge. Every vertex has a possible predecessor and successor and \(H\) is strongly connected. Every directed cycle in \(H\), however, alternates between the two parts, so no cycle can visit all five vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strongly connected bidirected graph K2,3 passes local predecessor and successor tests but has no Hamiltonian circuit.
assumptions_latex: The two bipartition classes have cardinalities \(2\) and \(3\), with no within-class arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ satisfies the stated necessary tests but has no Hamiltonian circuit}.

notation.meaning: bidirected complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes two and three

knowledge_statements.title: Degree and Connectivity Conditions Are Incomplete
Circuit Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filtering successor variables constrained to form one directed Hamiltonian circuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each vertex \(v\in V\) have a successor variable \(x_v\in D_v\subseteq V\setminus\{v\}\), and require the arcs \((v,x_v)\) to form one directed Hamiltonian circuit. Sound filtering enforces distinct successors and one predecessor per vertex. It fails if fixed arcs contain a directed cycle on a proper subset of \(V\), and it deletes an arc that would close such a fixed proper cycle. The directed domain graph \(H=(V,\{(v,w):w\in D_v\})\) must also be strongly connected; failure of strong connectivity certifies that no Hamiltonian circuit completion exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Circuit filtering enforces unique predecessors and successors, prevents premature subtours, and rejects a domain graph that is not strongly connected.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and \(|V|\ge2\).
Self-successor values are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every retained assignment must admit completion to one Hamiltonian directed circuit.

notation.meaning: directed graph of currently possible arcs

review_flags: A circuit-global-constraint source is required for the filtering formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predecessor, subtour, and strong-connectivity conditions are necessary and fit circuit filtering. A source is required, and the conclusion should not be read as claiming that every retained individual arc has a Hamiltonian completion unless domain consistency is explicitly established.

children.title: Path Filtering
children.top_down_role: Filtering for path structures, endpoint regimes, and structural pruning consequences.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hardness of Complete Fixed-Endpoint Path Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary for exact arc-support filtering of fixed-endpoint Hamiltonian paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an explicit directed graph, distinct fixed endpoints \(s,t\), and a designated allowed arc \(e\), deciding whether some Hamiltonian \(s\)-to-\(t\) path contains \(e\) is NP-complete. Thus complete domain filtering for unrestricted fixed-endpoint path constraints is NP-hard, although endpoint reachability and transferred circuit relaxations remain polynomial necessary filters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Designated-arc support for a fixed-endpoint Hamiltonian path is NP-complete.
assumptions_latex: The graph, endpoints, and designated arc are explicit finite input.
A support visits every vertex exactly once from \(s\) to \(t\).
knowledge_statements.title: Hardness of Complete Fixed-Endpoint Path Filtering

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial necessary conditions for a Hamiltonian path with fixed endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the current directed domain graph \(H=(V,A)\) contains a Hamiltonian path from fixed start \(s\) to fixed terminal \(t\), then every vertex is reachable from \(s\) and \(t\) is reachable from every vertex. Therefore either a vertex unreachable from \(s\), or a vertex from which \(t\) is unreachable, certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every vertex must be reachable from the fixed start and able to reach the fixed terminal.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is the finite directed graph of currently allowed path arcs.
\(s\ne t\) are fixed endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\exists v\in V:s\not\leadsto v)\lor(\exists v\in V:v\not\leadsto t)\implies\text{no Hamiltonian }s\text{-}t\text{ path}.

notation.meaning: directed reachability from u to v in the current domain graph

knowledge_statements.title: Endpoint Reachability Certificates
Path Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hamiltonian directed path filtering through a virtual closing arc.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix distinct endpoints \(s,t\in V\). A directed Hamiltonian path from \(s\) to \(t\) has indegree zero at \(s\), outdegree zero at \(t\), and indegree and outdegree one at every other vertex. Introduce the fixed virtual arc \((t,s)\). Then an arc set \(P\) is an \(s\)-to-\(t\) Hamiltonian path exactly when \(P\cup\{(t,s)\}\) is a directed Hamiltonian circuit. Thus circuit filtering may be applied to the augmented graph, with deductions about the virtual arc ignored and all deductions about original arcs transferred to the path domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hamiltonian path with fixed endpoints becomes a Hamiltonian circuit by adding a virtual arc from the terminal vertex to the start.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
\(s,t\in V\) are distinct fixed endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ is an }s\text{-}t\text{ Hamiltonian path}\iff P\cup\{(t,s)\}\text{ is a Hamiltonian circuit}.\)

notation.meaning: fixed path start and terminal vertices

review_flags: The virtual-arc reduction needs an authoritative graph-constraint locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-endpoint virtual-closing-arc representation is mathematically correct and appropriate as a representation, but no authoritative graph-constraint locator supports the filtering transfer.

children.title: Circuit–Path Variants
children.top_down_role: Shared restrictions, variant interfaces, and transitions between circuit and path formulations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size and filtering-transfer property of the dummy-vertex variant interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adding one dummy vertex and at most one incoming and one outgoing dummy arc per admissible endpoint enlarges a directed path instance by \(O(|V|)\) arcs. Under the dummy-vertex correspondence, every original arc occurs in a feasible path exactly when it occurs in the corresponding augmented circuit. Hence exact support and sound deletion of original arcs transfer in both directions; deductions concerning only dummy arcs encode endpoint choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dummy-vertex construction has linear size and preserves support of every original arc, while dummy-arc support represents endpoint support.
assumptions_latex: The augmented circuit is constrained to visit the dummy vertex exactly once.
Dummy outgoing arcs represent admissible starts and dummy incoming arcs represent admissible terminals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\in A\text{ has path support}\iff a\text{ has augmented-circuit support}.

notation.meaning: dummy vertex closing a path into a circuit

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Preserving Linear-Size Path–Circuit Reduction
Circuit–Path Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dummy-vertex reduction for endpoint-variable Hamiltonian path variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) describe allowed arcs for a Hamiltonian path whose start and terminal vertices may be chosen. Add a dummy vertex \(d\) and arcs \((d,v)\) and \((v,d)\) for every admissible start and terminal vertex \(v\), respectively. There is a Hamiltonian path in \(G\) from an admissible start \(s\) to an admissible terminal \(t\) exactly when the augmented graph has a Hamiltonian circuit containing \((d,s)\) and \((t,d)\). Removing \(d\) and its two incident selected arcs recovers the path; fixing either incident arc specializes the representation to one fixed endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding one dummy vertex converts variable-endpoint Hamiltonian paths into circuits; fixing its incident arcs fixes either or both path endpoints.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite directed graph.
The dummy vertex occurs exactly once in the augmented circuit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hamiltonian path variants correspond bijectively to augmented circuits through \(d\).

notation.meaning: dummy vertex closing a path into a circuit

review_flags: A source for dummy-vertex circuit/path variants and propagation transfer is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dummy-vertex correspondence is coherent for the stated admissible endpoint sets and fits the variants container, but the reduction and propagation-transfer interpretation lack a cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Propagation Implementation
children.top_down_role: Solver-kernel structures supporting correct, incremental, and efficient propagation.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Propagation kernel, propagators, views, automatic derivation, and data structures
Fixpoint reasoning, events, priorities, multiple propagators, and staged propagators

children.title: Propagator Posting
children.top_down_role: Registration, attachment, and posting-time interactions within the propagation kernel.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic requirement on the installed activation metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The metadata installed while posting \(p\) must be sufficient for initialization to evaluate the current store and, if \(p\) remains live, for every future store change capable of invalidating its quiescence to cause an activation through the lifecycle mechanism. Missing a required dependency can leave \(p\) permanently inactive after relevant contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posting must install enough dependency information for initial evaluation and every later change that can make the propagator useful again.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) may remain live after initialization.
Activation is driven by installed dependencies or an equivalent mechanism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every quiescence-destroying future contraction is covered by installed activation metadata.}
knowledge_statements.title: Posting Installation Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Installation phase preceding first effective evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Posting constraint \(c\) constructs or selects a sound propagator \(p\), associates it with the variables and event classes on which it depends, and installs the lifecycle metadata required for subsequent initialization and reactivation. Posting itself is distinct from the first effective execution and from handling a contradiction discovered there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posting installs a sound propagator and its event dependencies; initialization and immediate failure are separate lifecycle phases.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is sound for \(c\).
The engine provides event subscriptions or an equivalent activation mechanism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\text{ is installed with activation metadata sufficient to enter initialization and later reactivation.}
review_flags: Construction and registration details vary across propagation engines.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Posting

children.title: Propagator Initialization
children.top_down_role: Initial state preparation, first activation regimes, and initialization boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent first-execution phase for a newly installed propagator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a newly installed propagator \(p\) at store \(D\), initialization executes \(p\), or performs an equivalent posting-time test. It returns failure, retirement when permanent entailment is established, or a nonfailed store \(D'\subseteq D\) together with incremental state and watches valid for \(D'\). A nonretired propagator is then suspended or scheduled according to the engine's lifecycle policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialization performs the new propagator's first effective evaluation and leaves failure, retirement, or valid post-execution state for later activation.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is sound and contracting.
Any retained incremental state and watches can be validated against the resulting store.
review_flags: Exact ordering of watch installation and execution is engine-dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Initialization Outcomes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safe Omission of a Separate First Run
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which initialization need not invoke the propagator separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A separate initial invocation of \(p\) may be omitted only when posting has already performed an equivalent evaluation—establishing failure, permanent entailment, or a post state observationally equivalent to running \(p\) on the current store. Watch registration alone is insufficient because later events need not encode information already present when \(p\) was installed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first run may be skipped only when posting has already performed an equivalent evaluation; merely registering watches is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: Event notifications ordinarily describe later changes rather than the complete preexisting store.
Equivalence includes the resulting contraction, incremental state, and watches.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{skip}(p,D)\text{ is safe only if posting already establishes an outcome equivalent to }\operatorname{run}(p,D).
knowledge_statements.title: Safe Omission of a Separate First Run

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant for cached incremental state and watches after initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If initialization retains \((\sigma_p,W_p)\), both must describe the resulting store \(D'\), not the pre-execution store \(D\). Otherwise a later incremental invocation may interpret events relative to an obsolete baseline and differ from a fresh sound invocation on the same descendant store.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cached state and watches retained after initialization must correspond to the resulting store.
assumptions_latex: \(D'\subseteq D\) is the store after the initial effective evaluation.
\(p\) retains state across invocations.
knowledge_statements.title: Post-Initialization State Consistency

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and each variable \(x\in V\) has a finite current domain \(D(x)\).
\(p\) is a sound, contracting propagator with an implementation-defined watch specification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is either retired, suspended with registered watches, or reports failure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain propagator initialization immediately after posting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(D\) and a newly posted propagator \(p\), register the variables and event classes requested by \(p\), then execute \(p(D)\). If execution returns failure, report inconsistency. Otherwise let \(D'\subseteq D\) be the returned store. If \(p\) is subsumed at \(D'\), remove its watches and retire it; otherwise install its updated watches, mark it suspended, and emit every domain event induced by the transition from \(D\) to \(D'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Register the new propagator's watches, run it once, report failure if inconsistent, and otherwise retire it if subsumed or suspend it for future relevant events.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Initialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and initialization scope fit the leaf, but watch registration, initial execution, event emission, and retirement ordering are implementation-dependent claims with no cited source or locator.

children.title: Posting-Time Failure Handling
children.top_down_role: Immediate inconsistency, redundant posting, and initialization failure cases.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic certificate for immediate inconsistency discovered during initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the pre-posting store, \(C\) the previously posted constraints, and \(p\) a sound propagator for new constraint \(c\). If initialization derives an empty domain or another sound contradiction for \(C\cup\{c\}\) under \(D\), then the augmented model has no solution represented by \(D\), so reporting posting-time failure is sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty domain or another sound contradiction during initialization certifies that the augmented model has no solution in the current store.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is sound for \(c\).
The reported contradiction is sound for \(C\cup\{c\}\) under \(D\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sound Posting-Time Failure Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absence of Immediate Failure Is Not Satisfiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness boundary of posting-time contradiction detection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If sound but incomplete posting-time propagation returns a nonfailed store \(D'\), this establishes only that the selected propagation procedure derived no contradiction. It does not imply that \(C\cup\{c\}\) has a solution represented by \(D'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successful posting means no immediate contradiction was found, not that the augmented model is satisfiable.
assumptions_latex: Posting-time propagation is sound but not assumed complete for satisfiability.

notation.meaning: Nonfailed store returned by posting-time propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Absence of Immediate Failure Is Not Satisfiability

assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the current finite-domain store before posting.
\(p\) is sound and contracting, and posting is required to preserve the solutions of the accumulated model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure is reported exactly when initialization proves \(D'=\bot\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate inconsistency detected while a propagator is posted and initialized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize and execute \(p\) on \(D\). If the result is \(\bot\), return failure before propagation reaches a quiescent store; no successful post state is produced. If posting is transactional, restore \(D\) and remove registrations created for \(p\). If the result is a store \(D'\neq\bot\), commit \(D'\), enqueue propagators awakened by its events, and continue ordinary propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagator that detects inconsistency during posting causes immediate failure; transactional solvers also undo its provisional domain changes and registrations.
knowledge_statements.title: Posting-Time Failure Handling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits posting-time failure handling, but rollback, registration removal, commit, and enqueue behavior vary by solver and have no supporting citation.

children.title: Propagator Suspension
children.top_down_role: Dormancy regimes, suspension conditions, and retained propagator state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions for placing a live propagator into a dormant off-queue state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A live propagator \(p\) may be suspended at store \(D\) only after its current execution obligation is discharged, no failure or permanent entailment has occurred, and its current propagation procedure is quiescent at \(D\). The retained activation condition must cover every descendant contraction that can make another execution necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagator may sleep only after its current work is quiescent and its retained activation condition covers every future change that could enable more pruning.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is sound and contracting.
Suspension removes \(p\) from immediate runnable status.
Future stores are descendants under domain contraction.
review_flags: Quiescence is relative to the propagator's declared execution procedure; a non-idempotent implementation may require explicit self-rescheduling.
knowledge_statements.title: Suspension Eligibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: False closure caused by invalid dormant-state entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p\) is suspended while its current execution obligation is not quiescent, or if a later contraction makes execution necessary without satisfying its retained activation condition, the runnable queue can become empty while \(p\) could still contract the store. Such suspension invalidates queue exhaustion as a closure test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sleeping too early or with incomplete watches can make the queue appear empty even though the propagator can still prune.
assumptions_latex: The missed current or future execution would contract the store.
No other mechanism schedules \(p\).
knowledge_statements.title: Premature or Under-Watched Suspension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Current-store dormancy versus permanent retirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suspension asserts only that no execution is presently required at \(D\) and that future relevant contractions will reactivate \(p\). Subsumption is stronger: \(p\) is permanently unnecessary throughout every descendant store covered by the entailment test. A suspended propagator retains activation state; a subsumed propagator may be retired.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Suspension is temporary current-store quiescence, whereas subsumption establishes that the propagator will never be needed in descendant stores.
assumptions_latex: The subsumption test is sound for all represented descendant stores.
knowledge_statements.title: Suspension Is Distinct from Subsumption

assumptions_latex: \(p\) has just executed successfully on store \(D\).
The solver supplies event classes whose notifications cover every change that can make \(p\) non-idempotent at a descendant store.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) remains dormant until a watched event occurs or it is retired.

notation.meaning: Watch set installed by the propagator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational suspension after a successful propagation step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The propagator \(p\) may enter the suspended state at \(D\) when it has completed its current execution, has not failed, is not subsumed, and has installed a watch set \(W_p(D)\). Suspension removes \(p\) from the runnable queue while retaining its watches. Correctness requires that every descendant store \(D'\subseteq D\) at which rerunning \(p\) could prune further must be preceded by an event in \(W_p(D)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A successful, non-subsumed propagator may sleep off-queue only when its registered events cover every future change that could enable more pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Suspension

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits suspension, and the wake-up-completeness condition is plausible, but its precise lifecycle and watch semantics require an authoritative constraint-programming source.

children.title: Propagator Rescheduling
children.top_down_role: Reactivation triggers, scheduling eligibility, and queue-entry consequences.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Queue-side handling after a suspended propagator becomes runnable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When lifecycle activation makes suspended propagator \(p\) runnable, rescheduling records an obligation for a future execution and inserts or marks \(p\) according to the scheduler's queue policy. If \(p\) is already represented by a queued or running entry, the implementation may coalesce the request only if the new activation remains accounted for by that execution or by retained pending state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescheduling turns activation into a future execution obligation; coalescing is safe only when the new activation remains accounted for.
assumptions_latex: A valid suspension-to-queue activation has occurred.
The scheduler can represent a pending execution obligation.
Coalescing preserves required activation information.
review_flags: Concrete queue flags, event summaries, and insertion policies are implementation-dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Rescheduling Request Handling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when an activation is erased before any accounting execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an activation of \(p\) is removed or coalesced without being covered by the current execution and without retaining another pending obligation, \(p\) may return to suspension at a store \(D\) with \(p(D)\subsetneq D\). Queue-state changes must therefore preserve each activation until an accounting execution, failure, or subsumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping a reactivation before any execution accounts for it can leave a propagator asleep while it can still prune.
assumptions_latex: A relevant activation occurs.
No execution, failure, subsumption, or retained pending state accounts for it.

notation.meaning: Store after the lost rescheduling request.
Propagator whose execution obligation was lost.

knowledge_statements.title: Lost Rescheduling Obligation

assumptions_latex: \(p\) is suspended with watch set \(W_p\).
At least one event matching \(W_p\) has occurred since the last execution of \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is queued exactly once for a future execution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate-free rescheduling of a suspended propagator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On delivery of an event \(e\in W_p\), test the queue-membership flag of \(p\). If \(p\notin Q\), set the flag and insert \(p\) into \(Q\) according to the scheduler's priority policy. If \(p\in Q\), do not insert another copy, but retain any implementation-defined event summary. When \(p\) is selected for execution, remove it from \(Q\), clear the flag, and run it on the then-current store.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matching event queues a suspended propagator once; further matching events may be summarized but cannot create duplicate queue entries.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Rescheduling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits rescheduling, but duplicate suppression, queue flags, retained event summaries, and flag-clearing order are implementation-specific and uncited.

children.title: Suspension-to-Queue Transitions
children.top_down_role: Lifecycle boundaries linking dormant propagators to renewed queue participation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness and efficiency requirements for the transition predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Activation is sound when \(\alpha_p(D,D')=0\) implies that no new execution obligation for \(p\) is required at \(D'\). A false positive, \(\alpha_p=1\) when \(p\) remains quiescent, causes redundant work but does not lose pruning. A false negative, \(\alpha_p=0\) when another execution is required, leaves \(p\) suspended incorrectly and can lose propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over-triggering is safe but wasteful; under-triggering can miss pruning and is incorrect.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) was quiescent when suspended at \(D\).
The activation mechanism is the only path from suspension to a new execution obligation.

notation.meaning: Decision whether contraction D to D' activates p.

knowledge_statements.title: Activation Soundness and Precision

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical missed-wakeup failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p\) is suspended at \(D\), contraction to \(D'\) makes another execution necessary, and \(\alpha_p(D,D')=0\), then the transition remains at \(S_p\).
