knowledge_statements.title: Complete Self-Rescheduling Work List
Non-Idempotent Rescheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work-list scheduling when one application need not exhaust a propagator's possible pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite store lattice \(\mathcal D\), propagators \(P\), initial store \(D_0\), and wake sets \(W(\Delta)\subseteq P\), initialize \(D\leftarrow D_0\) and \(Q\leftarrow P\). While \(Q\neq\varnothing\), remove \(p\), compute \(D'\leftarrow p(D)\), and, if \(D'\subsetneq D\), set \(\Delta\leftarrow D\setminus D'\), \(D\leftarrow D'\), and \(Q\leftarrow Q\cup W(\Delta)\cup\{p\}\) whenever idempotence of \(p\) is not guaranteed. Return \(D\) when \(Q=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a non-idempotent propagator prunes a store, enqueue it again along with propagators awakened by the change; stop only when the queue is empty.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\) is finite.
Every propagator is contracting.
Wake sets include every propagator whose result can change after the recorded deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=\varnothing\) implies \(p(D)=D\) for every correctly watched \(p\in P\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate kind, but correctness depends on a precise queue invariant and wake-set completeness. The expression D\setminus D' is not defined for an abstract domain store, and the empty-queue conclusion requires stronger scheduling semantics. No supporting source is cited.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy criterion among propagators implementing the same constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) and \(q\) be contracting store transformers and suppose \(p(D)\preceq q(D)\) for every store \(D\). Then every fixpoint of \(p\) is a fixpoint of \(q\). Thus adding \(q(D)=D\) does not strengthen the terminal fixpoint condition \(p(D)=D\), although executing \(q\) may still be computationally useful.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stability under an everywhere stronger propagator implies stability under a weaker one.
assumptions_latex: \(p(D)\preceq D\) and \(q(D)\preceq D\) for every store \(D\).
\(p(D)\preceq q(D)\) for every store \(D\).

notation.meaning: Propagator p is pointwise at least as pruning as q

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise-Dominated Propagators Are Fixpoint-Redundant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixpoint equivalence for a finite ordered pass through contracting propagators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_1,\ldots,p_m\) be contracting self-maps of a poset, and let \(P=p_m\circ\cdots\circ p_1\). Then \(P(D)=D\) if and only if \(p_i(D)=D\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete sequential pass is stable exactly when every constituent contracting propagator is stable.
assumptions_latex: For all \(D\) and \(i\), \(p_i(D)\preceq D\).

notation.meaning: One ordered pass through all propagators

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Fixpoints Equal Common Fixpoints

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complementary Propagator Family for One Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-typed soundness contract for several propagators attached to one constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma(D)\) be the assignments represented by store \(D\), and let \(R_c\) be the solution relation of constraint \(c\). A family \(P_c\) is sound for \(c\) when every \(p\in P_c\) is contracting and satisfies \(R_c\cap\gamma(D)\subseteq\gamma(p(D))\subseteq\gamma(D)\) for every store \(D\). Different members may enforce different necessary consequences of \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several propagators may implement complementary consequences of one constraint, provided each only removes assignments that cannot satisfy that constraint within the current store.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma\) maps stores to their represented assignments.
Every member of \(P_c\) is a store self-map.
review_flags: Uses an explicit concretization map to avoid comparing a tuple relation directly with a store.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Propagator Family for One Constraint
Multiple Propagators per Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound decomposition of one constraint into complementary propagators with shared fixpoint semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\) be a constraint with solution relation \(R_c\), and let \(P_c=\{p_1,\ldots,p_m\}\) be propagators such that every \(p_i\) is contracting and preserves all tuples in \(R_c\). Then any composition of members of \(P_c\) is sound for \(c\). Fair iteration to a common fixpoint \(D^\star\) satisfies \[R_c\cap D_0\subseteq D^\star\subseteq D_0,\qquad p_i(D^\star)=D^\star\quad(1\le i\le m).\] Different propagators may implement distinct necessary consequences of the same constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several sound propagators may represent complementary consequences of one constraint. Their fair common closure preserves every solution while combining their pruning.
assumptions_latex: Each \(p_i\) is contracting.
Each \(p_i\) preserves \(R_c\cap D\) for every store \(D\).
Fair iteration terminates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_c\cap D_0\subseteq D^\star\subseteq D_0\) and \(\forall i,\ p_i(D^\star)=D^\star\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle matches the topic, but R_c is a tuple relation while D_0 and D^star are domain stores, so the displayed inclusions require an explicit concretization of stores as tuple sets. The common-fixpoint claim also relies on termination supplied only as an assumption. No source is cited.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition under which terminal-stage stability implies stability of every earlier stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_1,\ldots,p_m\) be contracting stages and suppose \(p_m(D)\preceq p_s(D)\) for every store \(D\) and every \(s<m\). If \(p_m(D)=D\), then \(p_s(D)=D\) for every \(s\), so terminal-stage suspension represents a common stage fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the terminal stage always prunes at least as much as every earlier stage, its stability guarantees stability of all stages.
assumptions_latex: Every stage is contracting.
The terminal stage pointwise subsumes every earlier stage.
knowledge_statements.title: Terminal-Stage Subsumption Condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Terminal Stability Alone Does Not Stabilize Earlier Stages
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of suspension without subsumption or an explicit common-fixpoint check.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the chain \(0\preceq1\preceq2\), let \(p_1(2)=1\), \(p_1(1)=0\), \(p_1(0)=0\), and let \(p_2\) be the identity. Both stages are monotone and contracting, and \(p_2(2)=2\), but \(p_1(2)=1\ne2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A terminal stage may be stable while an earlier stage can still prune unless an actual strength or common-fixpoint condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Terminal Stability Alone Does Not Stabilize Earlier Stages

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent staged protocol whose suspension implies a common stage fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(s\leftarrow1\). Execute \(p_s\) on \(D\). After a strict reduction, update \(D\) and reset \(s\leftarrow1\). After a no-op, increment \(s\). Suspend only after every stage \(1,\ldots,m\) has produced no change in one uninterrupted pass. On a relevant external change, reset \(s\leftarrow1\). If the reachable store interval has finite height \(h\), the protocol performs at most \(h\) productive stage executions and at most \((h+1)m\) stage executions in total before suspension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart from the first stage after any pruning and suspend only after a complete no-change pass; finite store height guarantees termination.
assumptions_latex: Every stage is contracting.
The reachable store interval has finite height \(h\).
Relevant external changes restart the protocol.
Stage executions terminate.

notation.meaning: Height of the reachable store interval

review_flags: This conservative protocol does not require terminal-stage subsumption.
knowledge_statements.title: Resetting Full-Pass Staging Protocol

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered activation of several filtering stages for one propagator interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A staged propagator is an ordered finite family \((p_1,\ldots,p_m)\) of sound contracting store transformers together with a stage index. Its scheduler attempts earlier stages before later stages and advances only after the current stage is stable; a relevant external change invalidates the saved stage position and triggers reconsideration according to the dependency policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A staged propagator activates an ordered sequence of filtering procedures, escalating after stability and reconsidering earlier stages after relevant changes.
assumptions_latex: Each stage is sound and contracting.
The stage family is finite.
Relevant external changes are detectable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (p_1,\ldots,p_m)\text{ is executed under an ordered escalation policy}.
knowledge_statements.title: Staged Propagator Family
Staged Propagators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental propagation that activates successively stronger filtering stages only when cheaper stages stabilize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a constraint, let \(p_1,\ldots,p_m\) be sound, contracting stages ordered from cheaper to stronger. Initialize \(D\leftarrow D_0\) and \(s\leftarrow1\). Compute \(D'\leftarrow p_s(D)\). If \(D'\subsetneq D\), set \(D\leftarrow D'\), reset \(s\leftarrow1\), and reschedule the staged propagator. If \(D'=D\) and \(s<m\), advance \(s\leftarrow s+1\); if \(D'=D\) and \(s=m\), suspend it. On a relevant external domain change, reset or lower \(s\) according to the stage dependency policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run cheap filtering first, escalate after stabilization, and reset after pruning or relevant external change. Suspension occurs only after the strongest stage makes no change.
assumptions_latex: Each stage \(p_s\) is sound and contracting.
The stage index set is finite.
Wake conditions cover every external change relevant to a stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Suspension at \(s=m\) yields \(p_m(D)=D\) without discarding any feasible tuple.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the leaf, but staged-propagator policies vary by solver. Sound suspension and resetting require precise relationships among stages and wake dependencies; stability of only p_m does not by itself establish a common stage fixpoint. An authoritative implementation or theory source is required.

children.title: Interval Domains
children.top_down_role: Contiguous-domain storage regimes, supported operations, and representation limits.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior Deletion Is Lost by Interval Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal expressiveness boundary for two-endpoint storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integers \(a<b<c\), the exact domain \(S=\{a,c\}\) has interval hull \([a,c]_{\mathbb Z}\), which contains \(b\notin S\). Thus retaining values on both sides of an interior deletion forces the deleted value into a bounds-only representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds-only storage cannot preserve an interior hole while retaining values on both sides.
assumptions_latex: \(a<b<c\) are integers.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior Deletion Is Lost by Interval Hull

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integer Hull as the Best Interval Abstraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least integer interval containing a nonempty finite integer domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty finite \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z\), \(\operatorname{hull}_{\mathbb Z}(S)=[\min S,\max S]_{\mathbb Z}\) contains \(S\) and is contained in every integer interval containing \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interval from a finite set's minimum to maximum is its unique most precise interval overapproximation.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z\) is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{hull}_{\mathbb Z}(S)=\min\{I:S\subseteq I,\ I\text{ an integer interval}\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer Hull as the Best Interval Abstraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contiguous finite-integer domain represented by two endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An interval store for an integer variable \(x\) consists of integers \(\ell_x,u_x\) and decodes as \(D(x)=[\ell_x,u_x]_{\mathbb Z}=\{v\in\mathbb Z:\ell_x\leq v\leq u_x\}\). It is empty exactly when \(\ell_x>u_x\), singleton exactly when \(\ell_x=u_x\), and supports exact prefix or suffix deletion by moving the corresponding endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer interval domain stores two bounds and represents every integer between them.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is integer-valued.
\(\ell_x,u_x\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Integer Interval Domain
Interval Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contiguous finite-integer domains represented by their current lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer variable \(x\), an interval-domain representation stores two integers \(\ell_x\) and \(u_x\) and denotes \[D(x)=[\ell_x,u_x]_{\mathbb Z}=\{v\in\mathbb Z:\ell_x\le v\le u_x\}.\] The domain is empty exactly when \(\ell_x>u_x\). Removing a prefix or suffix is represented by increasing \(\ell_x\) or decreasing \(u_x\); deletion of an interior value is not representable without splitting or changing representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interval domain stores only integer lower and upper bounds. It represents every integer between them, but cannot directly represent holes.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is integer-valued.
Bounds \(\ell_x,u_x\) are integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(x)=\{v\in\mathbb Z:\ell_x\le v\le u_x\}\), with emptiness iff \(\ell_x>u_x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and its finite-integer semantics are precise and fit the leaf, but no cited source with an inspectable locator supports the record. The inventory's interval-arithmetic material is not evidence for this constraint-domain storage representation.

children.title: Sparse Domains
children.top_down_role: Explicit sparse-value storage, update characteristics, and suitable domain regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense-prefix and inverse-index implementation of an exact sparse-set domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For values indexed by \(0,\ldots,n-1\), maintain mutually inverse arrays \(\mathrm{dense},\mathrm{sparse}\) and a live-prefix length \(k\), with \(D=\{\mathrm{dense}[i]:0\leq i<k\}\). Membership is tested by the inverse index. Deleting a live value swaps it with \(\mathrm{dense}[k-1]\), updates both inverse positions, and decrements \(k\). Under stack-disciplined trailing, restoring saved prefix lengths restores the corresponding earlier domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense live prefix plus inverse indices gives constant-time membership and swap deletion, linear-live-set enumeration, and reversible stack-ordered updates.
assumptions_latex: Values have distinct indices in \(0,\ldots,n-1\).
The arrays remain mutual inverses.
Restoration follows stack-disciplined saved states.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Set Deletion and Restoration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite membership representation supporting arbitrary holes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_x\) be a finite indexed universe. A sparse-set domain stores exactly a subset \(S_x\subseteq U_x\) and decodes as \(D(x)=S_x\). Deletion replaces \(S_x\) by \(S_x\setminus\{v\}\); failure occurs exactly when \(S_x=\varnothing\), and assignment exactly when \(|S_x|=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse-set domain explicitly stores surviving values, represents arbitrary holes, and uses cardinality for failure and assignment tests.
assumptions_latex: \(U_x\) is finite and indexable.
Membership in \(S_x\) is maintained exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Sparse-Set Domain
Sparse Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite domains represented by explicit membership structures supporting arbitrary holes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_x\) be a finite universe for variable \(x\). A sparse-domain representation stores exactly a finite set \(S_x\subseteq U_x\), using an explicit set, sparse-set pair, or equivalent indexed membership structure, and denotes \[D(x)=S_x.\] Deleting \(v\) replaces \(S_x\) by \(S_x\setminus\{v\}\); membership is exact, so arbitrary holes are representable. The domain is failed exactly when \(S_x=\varnothing\) and assigned exactly when \(|S_x|=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse domain explicitly stores its surviving values, exactly represents arbitrary holes, and detects failure or assignment by set cardinality.
assumptions_latex: \(U_x\) is finite.
The representation maintains exact membership in \(S_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(x)=S_x\), with failure iff \(S_x=\varnothing\) and assignment iff \(|S_x|=1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit-membership representation is mathematically coherent and appropriately classified, but 'sparse domain' can denote particular sparse-set implementations rather than every explicit set structure. A constraint-solver source is needed to establish the intended terminology and claims.

children.title: Bitset Domains
children.top_down_role: Bit-parallel domain storage, operation profiles, and scale boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking-compatible mutation and propagation-delta extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Before overwriting a bitset word, record its word index and old value once at the current search level. For an update from \(B\) to \(B'\subseteq B\), the removed-value delta is \(\Delta=B\wedge\neg B'\). Restoring recorded words in reverse trail order reconstructs the prior domain. If \(c\) words change, trailing and restoration require \(O(c)\) stored words and \(O(c)\) word operations, apart from computing the update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trailing changed words makes mutable bitset domains exactly reversible and exposes deleted values through a bitwise delta.
assumptions_latex: Updates are contracting.
Each changed word is trailed at most once per search level before restoration.

notation.meaning: bitset of values removed by the update

knowledge_statements.title: Reversible Word-Trailed Bitset Updates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Word-Level Cost of Bitset Domain Operations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Space and operation bounds for a fixed indexed universe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a bitset domain have \(n\) indexed values and machine-word width \(w\), so \(q=\lceil n/w\rceil\) words are stored. Membership and deletion of a known indexed value take \(O(1)\) word operations. Intersection, union, difference, equality, emptiness testing, and population count take \(O(q)\) worst-case word operations. Enumerating \(d\) present values takes \(O(q+d)\) time with word scanning and set-bit extraction. Storage is \(\Theta(n)\) bits, excluding any value-to-index map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bitset uses linear bits, supports indexed membership and deletion in constant time, performs whole-set operations by word scanning, and additionally pays for values emitted during enumeration.
assumptions_latex: A value's bit index is available in constant time.
Machine-word Boolean operations and population count have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Word-Level Cost of Bitset Domain Operations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory and scanning limitation when bit positions cover a wide numeric span.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If integer values are mapped directly by offset over \([\ell,u]\), a bitset reserves \(R=u-\ell+1\) bits even when only \(d\ll R\) values are present. Its storage is \(\Theta(R)\) bits and a full word scan costs \(\Theta(\lceil R/w\rceil)\). Direct-offset bitsets therefore lose their density advantage on wide sparse universes; compressed indexing avoids span-proportional storage but requires an explicit value-index map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct-offset bitsets are inefficient for wide sparse numeric domains because their cost follows the represented span rather than the number of present values.
assumptions_latex: Bit position \(v-\ell\) directly represents integer value \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\ll R\Rightarrow \text{direct-offset bitset costs depend on }R\text{ rather than }d.

notation.meaning: width of the directly represented integer span

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Universe Boundary of Direct-Offset Bitsets
Bitset Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite domains encoded by membership bits relative to an indexed value universe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_x=\{a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1}\}\) be an indexed finite universe. A bitset domain stores \(b\in\{0,1\}^n\) and denotes \[D(x)=\{a_i\in U_x:b_i=1\}.\] Deletion of \(a_i\) clears \(b_i\); intersection with a represented set uses bitwise conjunction. Thus arbitrary subsets of \(U_x\) are represented exactly, emptiness is equivalent to a zero population count, and assignment is equivalent to population count one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bitset uses one membership bit per indexed value. Bit operations implement exact deletion, intersection, emptiness detection, and singleton detection.
assumptions_latex: \(U_x\) is finite and indexed.
Each bit position has a fixed value correspondence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(x)=\{a_i:b_i=1\}\), with failure iff \(\sum_i b_i=0\) and assignment iff \(\sum_i b_i=1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bitset representation is precise, internally consistent, and correctly classified, but it has no cited evidence. None of the supplied local sources supports constraint-domain bitset storage at a specific locator.

children.title: Domain-Representation Transitions
children.top_down_role: Hybrid use, switching boundaries, and workload-sensitive representation choice.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics-preserving conversion between concrete stores for one finite domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let states \(s\) and \(s'\) use representations \(R\) and \(R'\) with decoding maps \(\gamma_R\) and \(\gamma_{R'}\). An exact transition constructs \(s'\) such that \(\gamma_{R'}(s')=\gamma_R(s)\) and replaces the concrete state without changing the abstract domain. Subsequent deletions must continue to decode as subsets of this preserved domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correct representation transition changes concrete storage while preserving exactly the represented value set and monotone deletion semantics.
assumptions_latex: Both representations have exact decoding maps.
The represented domain is supported by the target representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Domain-Representation Conversion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Workload-model condition under which exact conversion recovers its conversion cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If retaining \(R\) costs \(c_R\) per anticipated operation, using \(R'\) costs \(c_{R'}\), exact conversion costs \(C_{R\to R'}\), and \(m\) modeled operations remain, switching is cheaper exactly when \(C_{R\to R'}+mc_{R'}<mc_R\). When \(c_R>c_{R'}\), this is equivalent to \(m>C_{R\to R'}/(c_R-c_{R'})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a fixed cost model, conversion is worthwhile exactly when future operational savings exceed its one-time cost.
assumptions_latex: Conversion is exact.
The constant per-operation costs model the anticipated workload.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{switching is modeled as beneficial}\iff C_{R\to R'}+mc_{R'}<mc_R.
knowledge_statements.title: Break-Even Condition for Representation Switching
Domain-Representation Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics-preserving conversion among interval, sparse, and bitset storage during monotone domain reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current finite domain \(D\) stored in representation \(R\), choose a target representation \(R'\), enumerate or otherwise encode exactly the members of \(D\), construct state \(s'\) satisfying \(\llbracket s'\rrbracket_{R'}=D\), transfer representation-independent metadata, and atomically replace \((R,s)\) by \((R',s')\). Recompute representation-specific caches and subscriptions before propagation resumes. A transition is correct precisely when it preserves the represented set and subsequent deletion operations remain monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert storage only by preserving the exact current value set, rebuilding representation-specific metadata, and retaining monotone deletion semantics.
assumptions_latex: The current represented domain \(D\) is finite.
Both representations have exact decoding maps.
Propagation is paused or the replacement is atomic.

notation.meaning: domain decoded from state s under R

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is a suitable kind for the transition leaf, and preservation of the decoded set is the correct central invariant. Claims about atomic replacement, cache rebuilding, subscriptions, and representation-independent metadata are implementation-specific and undefined here, with no supporting source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal expressiveness boundary of mandatory/possible-element approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(U=\{a,b\}\) and \(\mathcal D=\{\varnothing,\{a,b\}\}\), the best enclosure is \([\varnothing,\{a,b\}]\), which additionally contains \(\{a\}\) and \(\{b\}\). Thus set bounds cannot express that the two optional elements occur together.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set bounds cannot retain every correlation between optional elements.
assumptions_latex: \(a\ne b\).
knowledge_statements.title: Set Bounds Lose Optional-Element Correlation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-and-upper approximation for a finite set-valued variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) range over subsets of a finite universe \(U\), and let \(L,U'\subseteq U\). The pair \((L,U')\) denotes \(D(X)=\{S\subseteq U:L\subseteq S\subseteq U'\}\). Elements of \(L\) are mandatory and elements outside \(U'\) are forbidden. The domain is empty exactly when \(L\nsubseteq U'\), and singleton exactly when \(L=U'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set bounds store mandatory and possible elements; incompatible bounds mean failure and equal bounds mean assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is finite.
\(X\subseteq U\).
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Bounds Domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least set-bounds domain containing a nonempty exact family of sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty family \(\mathcal D\subseteq2^U\), the least set-bounds domain containing \(\mathcal D\) is \([\bigcap\mathcal D,\bigcup\mathcal D]=\{S:\bigcap\mathcal D\subseteq S\subseteq\bigcup\mathcal D\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The most precise set-bounds enclosure uses elements present in every exact set as mandatory and elements present in some exact set as possible.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal D\subseteq2^U\).

notation.meaning: exact family of possible set values

knowledge_statements.title: Best Set-Bounds Enclosure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Intersection and Complement of Set Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjunction and complement duality for set-bounds domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D_i=[L_i,U_i]\), \(D_1\cap D_2=[L_1\cup L_2,U_1\cap U_2]\), empty exactly when \(L_1\cup L_2\nsubseteq U_1\cap U_2\). Under set complement \(S\mapsto U\setminus S\), \([L,U']\) maps exactly to \([U\setminus U',U\setminus L]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjunction unions mandatory elements and intersects possible elements; set complement exchanges the bounds while reversing them.
assumptions_latex: All bounds are subsets of the same finite universe \(U\).

notation.meaning: all sets between the two inclusion bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection and Complement of Set Bounds
Set-Bounds Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-and-upper approximation for a finite set-valued decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a set variable over a finite universe \(U\). A set-bounds domain is a pair \((L,U')\) with \(L\subseteq U'\subseteq U\), denoting \[D(X)=\{S\subseteq U:L\subseteq S\subseteq U'\}.\] Elements of \(L\) are mandatory and elements outside \(U'\) are forbidden. The domain is inconsistent exactly when \(L\nsubseteq U'\), and it is assigned exactly when \(L=U'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set bounds store mandatory and possible elements. Feasible values are all sets between those bounds; inconsistency occurs when a mandatory element is not possible.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is finite.
\(X\) ranges over subsets of \(U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-bounds definition fits the topic and is standard, but the opening condition L\subseteq U' excludes the later inconsistent case L\nsubseteq U'. The pair should be introduced without that consistency restriction if inconsistency is to be characterized. No set-constraint source is cited.

children.title: Variable Views
children.top_down_role: Alternative variable interpretations, transformed access, and propagator reuse.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Propagator Transport through a Bijective View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound reuse of a propagator after an exact bijective change of variable coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:A\to B\) be bijective and let \(P_B\) be a sound contracting domain propagator in the transformed space. Define \(P_A(D)=D\cap f^{-1}(P_B(f(D)))\). Then \(P_A\) is sound and contracting for the inverse-image constraint. If \(P_B\) is idempotent, then \(P_A\) is idempotent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bijective variable view transports a propagator while preserving soundness, contraction, and idempotence.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bijective.
\(P_B\) is sound and contracting.
\(P_B(f(D))\subseteq f(D)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_A\text{ is sound and contracting},\qquad P_B^2=P_B\Rightarrow P_A^2=P_A.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Transport through a Bijective View

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Offset, negation, and nonzero scaling variants for integer variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integers \(a\ne0\) and \(b\), the affine view \(y=ax+b\) exposes \(D(y)=\{av+b:v\in D(x)\}\). A restriction \(y\in E\) retains exactly those \(v\in D(x)\) with \(av+b\in E\). If \(D(x)=[\ell,u]_{\mathbb Z}\), the exact hull endpoints are \(a\ell+b,au+b\) for \(a>0\) and \(au+b,a\ell+b\) for \(a<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Offset, negation, and nonzero integer scaling are affine variable views; negative scaling reverses endpoint order.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is integer-valued.
\(a,b\in\mathbb Z\) and \(a\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Integer Variable Views

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A transformed variable represented through an underlying variable rather than independent storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) have domain \(D(x)\subseteq A\) and let \(f:A\to B\). A variable view \(y=f(x)\) has domain \(D(y)=f(D(x))\) and no independent authoritative domain. A restriction \(D(y)\leftarrow E\) is implemented as \(D(x)\leftarrow D(x)\cap f^{-1}(E)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable view presents a derived variable without separate storage, translating its pruning back to the underlying variable.
assumptions_latex: \(D(x)\subseteq A\).
Required image and inverse-image operations are computable.
knowledge_statements.title: Derived Variable View
Variable Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derived variables implemented by transformations of underlying variables rather than independent storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) have domain \(D(x)\), and let \(f:A\to B\) be a fixed transformation. A variable view \(y=f(x)\) has no independent domain store: it exposes \[D(y)=f(D(x))=\{f(a):a\in D(x)\}.\] A requested restriction \(D(y)\leftarrow E\subseteq B\) is implemented on the underlying variable by \[D(x)\leftarrow D(x)\cap f^{-1}(E).\] Queries, updates, and events for \(y\) are translated through \(f\) and its inverse-image operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable view represents a transformed variable without separate storage; domain queries use images, while pruning is translated back by inverse images.
assumptions_latex: \(D(x)\subseteq A\).
Images and inverse images under \(f\) are computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(y)=f(D(x))\) and restricting \(y\) to \(E\) restricts \(x\) to \(D(x)\cap f^{-1}(E)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct kind and the image/inverse-image formulation is coherent for an extensional exact view. Actual variable-view interfaces may impose additional restrictions on f and event translation, so the stated generality requires an authoritative source.

children.title: Domain Views
children.top_down_role: Alternative domain interfaces, representation adaptation, and update visibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Update and visibility boundary when several base values share one exposed value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If distinct \(a_1,a_2\in D\) satisfy \(f(a_1)=f(a_2)=b\), deleting exposed value \(b\) removes the entire fiber \(f^{-1}(\{b\})\) from \(D\). Conversely, deleting only \(a_1\) from the base leaves \(b\) exposed while \(a_2\) survives. Hence the view cannot independently control or observe members of one fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noninjective domain view treats all base values with the same exposed image as one update and visibility unit.
assumptions_latex: The view has exact image and inverse-image semantics.
knowledge_statements.title: Noninjective Domain-View Granularity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-interface adapter over authoritative underlying storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let authoritative storage represent \(D\subseteq A\), and let \(f:A\to B\). A domain view exposes \(E=f(D)\) without independent authoritative storage. Membership satisfies \(b\in E\iff D\cap f^{-1}(\{b\})\ne\varnothing\), and restricting the exposed domain to \(F\subseteq B\) updates the base to \(D\leftarrow D\cap f^{-1}(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A domain view adapts queries and restrictions to a transformed value space while retaining one authoritative underlying domain.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq A\).
Required image and inverse-image operations are computable.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Transformed-Domain View
Domain Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An adapter exposing transformed domain operations while retaining an underlying domain representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an underlying domain object represent \(D\subseteq A\), and let \(f:A\to B\). A domain view exposes the transformed set \(E=f(D)\) through an interface rather than materializing independent storage. Its membership query satisfies \(b\in E\iff D\cap f^{-1}(\{b\})\neq\varnothing\), and restricting the exposed domain to \(F\subseteq B\) performs \[D\leftarrow D\cap f^{-1}(F).\] The adapter is exact when every exposed query and update agrees with these image and inverse-image semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A domain view adapts queries and updates to a transformed value space while preserving one underlying domain as the authoritative storage.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq A\).
The required image and inverse-image operations are computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exposed domain equals \(f(D)\), and restriction to \(F\) updates the base domain to \(D\cap f^{-1}(F)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record coherently defines an exact transformed-domain adapter and uses the correct representation kind. However, 'domain view' is not uniform terminology across solvers, and no source establishes that this is the intended local concept.

children.title: View Composition
children.top_down_role: Layered views, compatibility boundaries, and effects on event propagation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete Event Translation through Composed Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract condition preventing missed wakeups across nested view layers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\tau_f(e)\) and \(\tau_g(e')\) be sets of possible output event classes caused by input events at two view layers. Define \(\tau_{g\circ f}(e)=\bigcup_{e'\in\tau_f(e)}\tau_g(e')\). If each component map contains every event observable at its output that its input event can cause, then the composed map contains every outer event caused by the base event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Event translations compose relationally; complete component overapproximations yield complete composed wakeups.
assumptions_latex: Each component event map overapproximates all output event classes caused by its input event.
Subscriptions depend only on the declared event classes.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete Event Translation through Composed Views

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Missed Inner Events Cannot Be Recovered
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wakeup failure caused by an incomplete inner event translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a base event causes an intermediate event \(e'\) relevant to an outer subscription but \(e'\notin\tau_f(e)\), then relational composition through \(\tau_f\) cannot produce any outer event solely reachable through \(e'\). A later view layer cannot recover a change that the inner layer did not report.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A missed event at an inner view layer remains missed after composition.
assumptions_latex: The omitted intermediate event can cause an outer subscribed event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e'\notin\tau_f(e)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{the required outer wakeup may be absent}.
knowledge_statements.title: Missed Inner Events Cannot Be Recovered

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flattening nested exact variable or domain transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let exact views use \(f:A\to B\) and \(g:B\to C\) over \(D\subseteq A\). Their composition is \(h=g\circ f\), with exposed domain \(h(D)=g(f(D))\). Restricting the outer domain to \(E\subseteq C\) updates the base to \(D\cap h^{-1}(E)=D\cap f^{-1}(g^{-1}(E))\). Thus nested and flattened exact views have identical query and pruning semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact views compose by ordinary function composition, and their inverse-image pruning composes in reverse order.
assumptions_latex: Both component views implement exact image and inverse-image semantics.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Functional Composition of Views
View Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compositional semantics for nested variable or domain transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:A\to B\) and \(g:B\to C\) define two exact views over a base domain \(D\subseteq A\). Their composition is the view \(h=g\circ f:A\to C\), whose exposed domain is \[h(D)=g(f(D)).\] For every requested restriction \(E\subseteq C\), the induced base-domain update is \[D\leftarrow D\cap h^{-1}(E)=D\cap f^{-1}(g^{-1}(E)).\] Hence nested exact views and the single composed view have identical query and pruning semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested exact views compose by function composition; their exposed domains and inverse-image pruning equal those of one composed view.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq A\).
Both component views implement exact image and inverse-image semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is the correct kind, and the image and inverse-image composition identities are mathematically precise and consistent with the prerequisite view records. No authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied, so it cannot pass candidate review.

children.title: Residue Caches
children.top_down_role: Cached support witnesses, reuse regimes, and invalidation boundaries.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cache Miss Is Not an Unsupportedness Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical status of absent or stale residue entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(R(i,a)\) is absent or invalid, the cache supplies no current witness, but this does not imply \[\{\tau\in C\cap\prod_jD_j:\tau_i=a\}=\varnothing.\] Removal requires a complete support search or another sound exclusion test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A missing or invalid residue does not prove that no support exists.
assumptions_latex: The residue cache is partial.
A sound support test is used after a cache miss.
knowledge_statements.title: Cache Miss Is Not an Unsupportedness Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic neutrality of correctly validated residue caching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A procedure that validates \(R(i,a)\), performs the original complete support search after a miss, and caches any witness found retains exactly the literals retained by the uncached complete support test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated residues accelerate support discovery without changing which literals a complete filter retains.
assumptions_latex: Cached tuples are validated before acceptance.
Fallback support search is complete.
knowledge_statements.title: Residues Preserve Filtering Semantics
Residue Caches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cached extensional supports retained across monotone domain reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq \prod_{i=1}^{r}D_i^0\) be a constraint and let the current domains satisfy \(D_i\subseteq D_i^0\). A residue cache is a partial map \(R:(i,a)\mapsto \tau\in C\) such that \(\tau_i=a\) when defined. The entry is a candidate support, not an assertion of current validity: before reuse it must be checked that \(\tau_j\in D_j\) for every \(j\). A failed entry may be replaced by any newly found valid support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residue cache remembers a previously found supporting tuple for a variable-value pair. The tuple must be revalidated against current domains before reuse.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is represented by tuples or admits a support-search oracle.
Domains evolve only by deletion between cache updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(i,a)=\tau\) is reusable exactly when \(\tau\in C\cap\prod_{j=1}^{r}D_j\) and \(\tau_i=a\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard residue definition for extensional constraint propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the residue-cache leaf and are mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source supports the terminology, revalidation rule, or replacement convention.

children.title: Last-Support Caches
children.top_down_role: Last-known support tracking, revisitation behavior, and constraint-specific uses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case work for one ordered support-list reconsideration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(S_{i,a}\) contains \(m\) candidates and validation costs \(T_{\mathrm{val}}\), a scan examining each position at most once finds a support or certifies absence in \(O(mT_{\mathrm{val}})\) time and uses \(O(1)\) additional cache space per literal. The cursor changes the starting position but not the worst-case full-scan bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete reconsideration scans at most the whole support list; caching the last position does not improve the worst-case full-scan bound.
assumptions_latex: The candidate list has fixed finite length m.
One reconsideration visits no position more than once.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete Last-Support Scan Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total cache representation when no candidate support exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordinary cache position in \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) exists only for \(m>0\). If the complete candidate list \(S_{i,a}\) is empty, the cache requires a null value \(\bot\), and emptiness certifies \(S_{i,a}\cap\prod_jD_j=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty candidate list needs a null cache state and immediately certifies absence of support.
assumptions_latex: S_{i,a}\text{ is the complete candidate list for }(i,a).
knowledge_statements.title: Empty Last-Support List
Last-Support Caches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-literal positions for resuming ordered support search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each literal \((i,a)\), let \(S_{i,a}=(\tau^1,\ldots,\tau^{m_{i,a}})\) enumerate the tuples of \(C\) whose \(i\)-th component is \(a\). A last-support cache stores an index \(L(i,a)\in\{1,\ldots,m_{i,a}\}\) of the most recently accepted support. On reconsideration, search begins at \(L(i,a)\), optionally wrapping cyclically, and sets \(L(i,a)=k\) upon finding \(\tau^k\in\prod_jD_j\). Failure after examining the complete list certifies absence of support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A last-support cache stores where support search last succeeded, so later searches resume there; a full unsuccessful scan establishes that no support remains.
assumptions_latex: Each support list \(S_{i,a}\) is finite and has a fixed order.
Current tuple validity can be tested against the domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A complete cyclic scan from \(L(i,a)\) either returns a valid support or establishes \(S_{i,a}\cap\prod_jD_j=\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: ordered support lists commonly retain a last successful search position

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but the exact indexed cyclic-search convention lacks evidence, and the definition does not handle an empty support list, for which the stated cache index set is empty.

children.title: Support-Cache Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity regimes, stale-cache risks, and restoration-sensitive support state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal counterexample to unchecked cache reuse and cache-miss pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{(0,0),(0,1)\}\), initially \(D_x=\{0\}\), \(D_y=\{0,1\}\), and \(K(x,0)=(0,0)\). After deleting \(0\) from \(D_y\), the cached tuple is invalid, but \((x,0)\) remains supported by \((0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deletion can stale one cached tuple while another support remains, so unchecked reuse and pruning from cache failure are both unsound.
assumptions_latex: D_x=\{0\},\ D_y=\{1\}\text{ after deletion}.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale Cached Tuple After Deletion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Domain Restoration Breaks One-Way Validity Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cache-validity behavior when search restores deleted values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under deletion-only evolution, a valid cached tuple may become invalid and an invalid tuple cannot become valid. Restoration breaks this one-way behavior: restoring a deleted component can make a formerly invalid tuple valid again. Reuse after restoration therefore requires revalidation or restored validity metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalidity is monotone only while domains shrink; restoring values can make a formerly invalid cached tuple valid again.
assumptions_latex: Validity requires every tuple component to belong to its current domain.
Search may restore deleted values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\operatorname{Valid}_{D'}(\tau)\land\operatorname{Valid}_{D}(\tau)\text{ is possible when }D'\subset D\text{ is later restored to }D.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain Restoration Breaks One-Way Validity Monotonicity
Support-Cache Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity predicate governing safe reuse of cached tuple supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\prod_{j=1}^{r}D_j^0\), let \(D_j\subseteq D_j^0\) be current domains, and suppose \(K(i,a)=\tau\). The cache entry is valid for literal \((i,a)\) precisely when \[\operatorname{Valid}_D(K,i,a)\iff \tau\in C\;\land\;\tau_i=a\;\land\;\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,r\},\ \tau_j\in D_j.\] Under domain deletion, validity can change from true to false but cannot change from false to true unless domains are restored or the cache entry is replaced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached tuple is valid exactly when it belongs to the constraint, contains the requested value, and all its components remain in current domains.
assumptions_latex: Domains change monotonically by deletion during the propagation phase.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Valid}_D(K,i,a)\) is the necessary and sufficient condition for reusing \(K(i,a)\) as a current support.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tuple support validity follows the standard generalized-arc-consistency predicate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity condition is precise, consistent with the plain statement, and appropriately classified as a condition, but it has no inspectable authoritative citation.

children.title: Watched Values
children.top_down_role: Value-level watch structures, triggering regimes, and support-monitoring uses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse index from watched values to active watch records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_{i,a}\) contain the active watch records subscribed to deletion of \(a\in D_i\). Storing one entry per subscription uses \(\Theta(s)\) references, where \(s\) is the number of active subscriptions. Deletion of \(a\) from \(D_i\) need inspect only \(Q_{i,a}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse lists keyed by variable-value literals use linear subscription space and localize deletion processing to the matching list.
assumptions_latex: \text{Each active subscription has one reverse-index entry}.
\text{Deletion notifications identify the removed variable-value literal}.

notation.meaning: active records watching deletion of value a from variable i

knowledge_statements.title: Literal-Indexed Watch Lists
Watched Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-level subscriptions used to avoid irrelevant propagator wakeups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For variables \(x_i\) with current domains \(D_i\), a watched-value state is a set \(W\subseteq\{(i,a):a\in D_i\}\) together with subscriptions to deletion events for its members. If an update changes domains from \(D\) to \(D'\), the propagator may remain dormant whenever \(W\subseteq\{(i,a):a\in D_i'\}\). Deletion of any watched value schedules either propagation or watch replacement; correctness requires the propagator invariant to remain certified while every watched value survives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Watched values are subscribed domain members. The propagator sleeps while they survive and reacts when one is deleted, provided their survival certifies its invariant.
assumptions_latex: The event system reports deletion of each subscribed value.
The watched-value invariant is explicitly maintained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W\subseteq\{(i,a):a\in D_i'\}\) is a sufficient dormancy condition whenever survival of \(W\) implies the propagator invariant.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: event-driven propagation may watch selected domain values

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits watched values, but the claimed dormancy behavior depends on an unspecified propagator invariant and scheduling semantics. No source establishes the stated abstraction.

children.title: Watched Tuples
children.top_down_role: Tuple-level watch structures, extensional-constraint uses, and storage boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and invalidation indexing for explicitly stored watched tuples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a currently valid finite watched-tuple set \(T\), let \(L_{i,a}=\{\tau\in T:\tau_i=a\}\). One occurrence-list entry per tuple component uses \(\Theta(\sum_{\tau\in T}|\operatorname{scope}(\tau)|)\) references. Deleting \(a\) from \(D_i\) directly invalidates exactly the watches in \(L_{i,a}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Occurrence lists use space linear in stored tuple components and identify exactly the current tuple watches invalidated by a value deletion.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ contains the valid watches immediately before the deletion}.
\text{Every tuple component has exactly one occurrence-list entry}.

notation.meaning: watched tuples using value a at coordinate i

knowledge_statements.title: Occurrence-Indexed Tuple-Watch Storage
Watched Tuples
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tuple-level witnesses whose invalidation triggers replacement or propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^{r}D_i^0\) and \(D_i\subseteq D_i^0\). A watched-tuple state is a finite set \(T\subseteq C\cap\prod_iD_i\) whose members witness a stated propagator invariant, together with subscriptions sufficient to detect invalidation of every \(\tau\in T\). A tuple becomes invalid when some \(\tau_i\notin D_i\). While all watched tuples remain valid, no wakeup is required solely to rediscover those witnesses; invalidation triggers replacement or full propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Watched tuples are current feasible witnesses. Component deletion invalidates a watch and triggers replacement or propagation; surviving watches avoid redundant witness searches.
assumptions_latex: Each watched tuple's validity can be monitored through component-value deletions.
The maintained invariant states what each watched tuple witnesses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\subseteq C\cap\prod_iD_i\) certifies continued availability of all witnesses represented by \(T\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: watched supports retain feasible tuples until a component value disappears

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tuple-watch representation is internally coherent and fits the leaf, but its wakeup and witness semantics are propagator-specific and unsupported by an inspectable citation.

children.title: Watch Replacement Regimes
children.top_down_role: Replacement conditions, retained-watch behavior, and stale-watch failure boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention condition before eager or deferred replacement is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w\) certify invariant \(I\) at store \(D\). After a contraction \(D'\subseteq D\), retaining \(w\) is sound whenever \(w\) remains valid and its validity still implies \(I(D')\). Replacement is required when either condition fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A watch may be retained while it remains valid and still certifies the maintained invariant.
assumptions_latex: D'\subseteq D.
w\text{ remains valid at }D'.
w\text{ valid at }D'\Longrightarrow I(D').
knowledge_statements.title: Valid-Watch Retention
Watch Replacement Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eager and deferred policies for replacing invalidated watched witnesses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a watched witness \(w\), current domains \(D\), and a finite candidate set \(S(w,D)\). When \(w\) becomes invalid, an eager regime immediately searches \(S(w,D)\), installs a valid \(w'\), or invokes full propagation if none exists. A deferred regime marks the watch invalid and performs the same search at the next required propagator execution. Output is either a replacement satisfying the watch invariant or the result of full propagation. Deferred replacement is sound only if no skipped event can require pruning before that execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invalid watch is replaced immediately or marked for replacement at the next propagation. Deferral is sound only when skipped events cannot delay required pruning.
assumptions_latex: Candidate search is complete over \(S(w,D)\).
Scheduling preserves every pruning obligation not certified by surviving watches.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update returns a valid replacement \(w'\in S(w,D)\) or executes the full propagator; eager and deferred regimes differ only in safe timing.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invalid watches admit eager or safely deferred replacement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate content kind, but the safe deferred-replacement condition is stated only abstractly and lacks an authoritative source defining the scheduling obligations.

children.title: Incremental Graph State
children.top_down_role: Maintained graph structures, change locality, and propagation reuse.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restoration Boundary for Decremental Graph State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking boundary for graph state maintained only under edge deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(q_t\) is maintained correctly only for updates \(E_{t+1}\subseteq E_t\). If backtracking restores \(E_s\supset E_t\), deletion-only updating cannot in general establish the invariant for \((V,E_s)\). Correct handling requires restoration of a saved state, an insertion-capable update, or reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deletion-maintained graph state is not automatically valid after backtracking restores edges; it must be rolled back, insertion-updated, or rebuilt.
assumptions_latex: The update procedure supports only edge deletions.
Backtracking may restore domain-induced edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_s\supset E_t\Longrightarrow q_s\text{ must be restored, insertion-updated, or reconstructed.}
knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Boundary for Decremental Graph State
Incremental Graph State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent graph summaries maintained under domain-induced edge updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(D)=(V,E(D))\) be a graph derived from current domains. An incremental graph state is a pair \((G(D),\sigma(D))\), where \(\sigma(D)\) is an auxiliary summary such as reachability labels, strongly connected components, or a spanning forest. For a domain delta \(\Delta\), an update operator \(U\) must satisfy \[U(G(D),\sigma(D),\Delta)=(G(D'),\sigma(D'))\] with \(G(D')\) equal to reconstruction from the new domains and \(\sigma(D')\) satisfying its defining graph invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental graph state stores a domain-derived graph and a certified graph summary. Processing a domain delta must produce the same graph and valid summary as reconstruction.
assumptions_latex: The graph construction \(D\mapsto G(D)\) is fixed.
The delta \(\Delta\) completely describes relevant domain changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After updating, both \(G(D')\) and \(\sigma(D')\) satisfy the same invariants as freshly constructed state.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incremental graph algorithms maintain a graph and invariant-preserving auxiliary state

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits incremental graph state, but reachability labels, strongly connected components, and spanning forests have different update invariants and regimes. No cited source supports their consolidation in this propagation context.

children.title: Incremental Matching State
children.top_down_role: Maintained matching structures, repair regimes, and filtering reuse.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edge Restoration Separates Maximum and Covering Invariants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restoration boundary for decrementally maintained matching state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be maximum in \(G'=(U\cup V,E')\), with \(E'\subset E\). After restoring \(E\), \(M\) remains feasible but need not remain maximum. By contrast, if \(M\) already saturates every designated variable vertex, edge insertion preserves that covering property. Thus maximum-matching state may require insertion augmentation, rollback, or recomputation, whereas an intact variable-covering witness remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoring edges can make a maximum matching nonmaximum, although an intact matching that already covers every required variable remains covering.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a matching contained in }E'.
E'\subset E\text{ after restoration.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ remains feasible in }E;\quad |M|\text{ may be below }\nu(G),\text{ while existing designated-vertex saturation is preserved.}
knowledge_statements.title: Edge Restoration Separates Maximum and Covering Invariants
Incremental Matching State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent matching witnesses for domain-value bipartite graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B(D)=(X\cup V,E(D))\) be the bipartite graph with \((x,a)\in E(D)\) exactly when \(a\in D_x\). An incremental matching state stores a matching \(M\subseteq E(D)\), commonly maximum or variable-covering when one exists. After edge deletions \(\Delta E\), retain \(M\setminus\Delta E\), unmatch endpoints of deleted matched edges, and search for augmenting paths until the required matching invariant is restored or its impossibility is certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental matching state retains unaffected matched edges after domain deletions and repairs broken matches by augmenting paths, or certifies that the required matching cannot exist.
assumptions_latex: Domains define the bipartite edges by membership.
The required invariant specifies maximum or variable-covering matching.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The repaired \(M'\subseteq E(D')\) satisfies the required matching invariant, or failure certifies that no such matching exists.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bipartite matching repair retains valid edges and augments after deletions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but maximum and variable-covering matchings are distinct requirements, and the repair/certification claim needs a source specifying which invariant and algorithm are intended.

children.title: Incremental Flow State
children.top_down_role: Maintained flow structures, residual-state reuse, and update boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental integral maximum-flow state when updates only insert arcs or increase capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be an integral feasible \(s\)-\(t\) flow under integral capacities \(u\). If \(u'_a\ge u_a\) on every old arc and inserted arcs have nonnegative integral capacity, then \(f\), extended by zero on inserted arcs, remains feasible. Residual augmentations from \(f\) reach a maximum flow for \(u'\); each augmentation increases the integral flow value by at least one, so at most \(\nu(u')-|f|\) augmentations are required. At termination, residual nonreachability defines an \(s\)-\(t\) cut of capacity equal to the returned flow value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capacity increases and arc insertions preserve the old integral flow, after which at most the increase in maximum-flow value many residual augmentations are needed.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is an integral feasible flow under \(u\).
All old and new capacities are finite nonnegative integers.
No old capacity decreases and no old positive-flow arc is deleted.
Each iteration augments along a residual \(s\)-\(t\) path until none exists.

notation.meaning: maximum flow value after the update

review_flags: The augmentation-count bound uses integral capacities; it is not asserted for arbitrary real capacities.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Capacity-Increase Reuse
Incremental Flow State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent feasible flows and residual networks under network updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a domain-derived capacitated network \(N(D)=(V,A,u,s,t)\), incremental flow state consists of a feasible flow \(f\) and its residual network \(N_f\). After an update produces capacities \(u'\) and arcs \(A'\), unchanged feasible flow values are retained; violations caused by deletion or capacity reduction are repaired by residual rerouting or flow cancellation. Residual augmentations then restore the required flow value or establish a cut certificate that the value is unattainable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental flow state retains feasible flow and residual information, repairs capacity-update violations, then augments or returns a cut certifying that the target flow is impossible.
assumptions_latex: Capacities are finite and nonnegative.
The update identifies every changed arc or capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting \(f'\) is feasible in \(N(D')\) and meets the target value, or an \(s\)-\(t\) cut certifies that no such value is feasible.

source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited max-flow/min-cut section supports the terminal cut certificate but not the incremental repair procedure. The required target flow value is also not introduced explicitly, so the stated algorithmic conclusion is not adequately supported.

children.title: Cross-Structure State Reuse
children.top_down_role: Shared state, conversion boundaries, and reuse across graph, matching, and flow filters.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semantic Equivalence Does Not Validate Internal State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between equivalent feasible-assignment representations and compatible incremental certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even if \(S_1(D)\) and \(S_2(D)\) represent the same feasible assignments, a state \(q_1\) satisfying \(I_1(S_1(D),q_1)\) is not thereby a valid state for \(S_2\). Sound reuse additionally requires a transfer map \(\phi\) satisfying \(I_2(S_2(D),\phi(q_1))\) and update semantics that account for every delta relevant to \(I_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representing the same solutions is insufficient for sharing incremental state; the target invariant and update semantics must also be preserved.
assumptions_latex: \(S_1(D)\) and \(S_2(D)\) have equal feasible-assignment projections.
Their maintained states may encode different witnesses, labels, or residual information.

notation.meaning: state maintained for the first structure

knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Equivalence Does Not Validate Internal State
Cross-Structure State Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility criterion for sharing state between related network representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let structures \(S_1(D)\) and \(S_2(D)\) have maintained states \(q_1\) and \(q_2\). State from \(S_1\) is reusable for \(S_2\) through a map \(\phi\) only if every admissible \(q_1\) satisfies \[I_1(S_1(D),q_1)\Longrightarrow I_2(S_2(D),\phi(q_1)),\] and every relevant domain delta can be translated without omitting an update affecting \(I_2\). Otherwise the transferred state is merely a search hint and must be revalidated before it can certify propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State may certify another structure only through an invariant-preserving map and complete delta translation. Otherwise it is only a hint requiring revalidation.
assumptions_latex: \(I_1\) and \(I_2\) explicitly define the respective state invariants.
Both structures refer to the same current domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Invariant preservation and complete delta translation are sufficient conditions for sound cross-structure reuse of \(\phi(q_1)\).

notation.meaning: structure k derived from domains D

knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Advisors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lightweight per-variable observers that summarize updates for a propagator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a propagator \(P\) over variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\), an advisor for \(x_i\) is a stateful callback \(A_i(q_i,\delta_i)=(q_i',h_i)\), where \(q_i\) is local advisor state, \(\delta_i\) describes a domain update, and \(h_i\) is a scheduling decision or summary delivered to \(P\). Advisor correctness requires that suppressing a full execution when \(h_i\) says dormant cannot omit pruning or failure detection required by \(P\)'s propagation contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagator advisor observes one variable's delta, updates lightweight local state, and recommends scheduling. A dormant recommendation is valid only if no required inference is missed.
assumptions_latex: Each relevant variable update produces a complete delta.
The propagator has a specified correctness and scheduling contract.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_i\) may suppress scheduling only when the updated advisor state certifies that executing \(P\) cannot produce a required new inference.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness criterion for compressed delta encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha\) map exact deletion sets to abstract events and let \(F_P(q,\Delta)\) denote the contract-relevant reaction of subscriber \(P\). The abstraction is sufficient precisely when \(\alpha(\Delta_1)=\alpha(\Delta_2)\) implies equivalent required reactions for every reachable \(q\).

assumptions_latex: F_P\text{ denotes the subscriber's required observable reaction}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact composition law for successive domain reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D_0\supseteq D_1\supseteq D_2\), define \(\Delta_{01}=D_0\setminus D_1\), \(\Delta_{12}=D_1\setminus D_2\), and \(\Delta_{02}=D_0\setminus D_2\). Then \[\Delta_{02}=\Delta_{01}\mathbin{\dot\cup}\Delta_{12},\qquad D_2=D_0\setminus\Delta_{02}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive exact deletion deltas combine by disjoint union into the exact overall delta.
assumptions_latex: D_2\subseteq D_1\subseteq D_0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact incremental descriptions of changes to a variable domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a variable domain changes from \(D\) to \(D'\subseteq D\), its deletion delta is \(\Delta=D\setminus D'\), optionally represented by equivalent bounds and hole information. It is complete when \(D'=D\setminus\Delta\). For any propagator state \(q(D)\), a delta update operator is correct when \[U(q(D),\Delta)=q(D')\] up to the state's defining invariant. An empty delta denotes no domain change and must not alter the abstract state.

assumptions_latex: The propagation phase changes domains only by deletion.
The delta representation can reconstruct every relevant change.

domain before and after the update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental coordination between a variable delta and its propagator-specific advisor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each subscribed variable \(x\), initialize advisor state \(a_x\) consistently with propagation state \(S\) and an empty delta \(\Delta_x\). Whenever the domain of \(x\) changes, merge the new change into \(\Delta_x\) and schedule the associated propagator if the merged delta can affect it. On execution, pass \((a_x,\Delta_x)\) to the advisor update, which may revise \(a_x\), report irrelevance, or request full propagation. Clear only the portion of \(\Delta_x\) consumed by that update. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operation-count bounds for value trailing below a choice-point marker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(r\) constant-size restoration records occur after a target marker, the additional trail space is \(\Theta(r)\), and restoration to that marker takes \(\Theta(r)\) record operations. With first-write-per-level trailing, \(r\) is bounded by the number of distinct location-level pairs first modified below the marker; trailing every write may instead make \(r\) equal the total number of writes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trail storage and undo time are linear in the number of records. First-write-per-level trailing records at most one old value for each location at each active level.
assumptions_latex: Each restoration record has constant size and constant execution cost.
The target marker is valid and every record after it must be undone.

notation.meaning: Restoration records after the target marker

review_flags: Revised the Builder's per-level bound to cover all descendant levels below the target marker.
knowledge_statements.title: Trail Space and Restoration Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary coverage condition for trail-based restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose location \(u\) has value \(a\) at a marker and is changed below it to \(b\ne a\). If no trail record or other reversible mechanism retains information sufficient to recover \(a\), restoration from the retained information cannot be guaranteed to reconstruct the marked state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mutation omitted from every restoration mechanism can survive backtracking and invalidate exact restoration.
assumptions_latex: Backtracking uses only the retained reversible information.
The old value \(a\) is not derivable from that information.
knowledge_statements.title: Unrecorded Mutation Breaks Exact Restoration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact restoration protocol for value-trailed mutable state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On creating choice point \(k\), save \(m_k=|T|\). Before overwriting a location whose marker-time value is not already protected for the current level, append its location and current value to \(T\), then perform the overwrite. To restore choice point \(k\), pop and execute records until \(|T|=m_k\). If every mutation below the marker is protected and records are executed in reverse order, the resulting state equals the state at marker creation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Save a trail marker, record each required old value before mutation, and undo records backward to the marker; complete coverage restores the exact marked state.
assumptions_latex: Every mutation below the marker is covered by a sufficient restoration record or an equivalent reversible mechanism.
Restoration records are executed in reverse mutation order.
The target marker is valid.
review_flags: The protocol permits either first-write-per-level recording or more frequent recording, provided undo coverage remains exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Marker-Based Reverse Undo

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restoration-log representation of mutable state during depth-first search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A value trail is a last-in-first-out sequence of records \((u,v)\), where \(u\) identifies a mutable location and \(v\) is the value that location must recover on undo. A choice-point marker identifies the trail prefix belonging to the state at that choice point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value trail stores old values in undo order, and a choice-point marker identifies how far the trail must be unwound to restore an earlier state.
assumptions_latex: Mutable state changes can be identified by location.
Restoration records are undone in reverse order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T[0:m_k]\text{ represents the trail prefix at choice point }k.

notation.meaning: Trail-prefix length saved at choice point k

knowledge_statements.title: Value-Trail Representation

assumptions_latex: Solver execution follows a rooted depth-first search tree.
Every mutable location changed below a choice point can be identified and restored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backtracking to level \(k\) restores exactly the state present when level \(k\) was entered.

notation.meaning: Trail marker at search level k

review_flags: No supplied locator supports trailing for reversible constraint-solver state.
Exact restoration-record conventions require an implementation source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value trailing for depth-first backtracking of mutable propagation state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the trail \(T\) empty and, on entering search level \(k\), store the marker \(m_k=|T|\). Before the first modification at level \(k\) of a mutable location \(u\), append a restoration record containing \(u\)'s preceding value, unless an equivalent record already protects that value at the current level. Apply subsequent updates in place. To backtrack to level \(k\), repeatedly remove and execute restoration records from \(T\) until \(|T|=m_k\), then discard markers for deeper levels. The output state \(S\) equals the solver state at entry to level \(k\), provided every state-changing operation obeys the trailing discipline.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trailing records overwritten values and replays those records backward to restore the state at a chosen search level.
