intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reason-clause and conflict-clause interface is a plausible standard CP–SAT formulation, but no inspectable specialized source or locator supports it.

children.title: CP–MIP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Propagation exchange between constraint programming and mixed-integer optimization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MIP Relaxation Outcomes as CP-Safe Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified outcomes returned by a minimization-oriented MIP service at a CP state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_D\) be the original feasible set under CP store \(D\), and let \(P_D\supseteq F_D\) be a MIP relaxation using the same minimization objective \(f\). If \(P_D=\varnothing\), then \(F_D=\varnothing\). Any certified lower bound \(L\le\min_{x\in P_D}f(x)\) also satisfies \(L\le\min_{x\in F_D}f(x)\); therefore a state may be pruned against incumbent value \(U\) when \(L\ge U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation infeasibility proves state infeasibility, and a certified MIP lower bound safely prunes a minimization state when it cannot beat the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(F_D\subseteq P_D\).
Both models use the same objective evaluation.
\(L\) is a certified lower bound for \(P_D\).

notation.meaning: Original feasible set under the CP store

knowledge_statements.title: MIP Relaxation Outcomes as CP-Safe Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local MIP Deductions Require Scope Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for deductions generated under CP-state assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(a^Tx\le b\) is known valid only for \(F_D\), it may be used while the assumptions defining \(D\) remain active. Installing it globally is sound only if it is valid for the global feasible set \(F\); otherwise a feasible point in \(F\setminus F_D\) may be removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut or bound derived under local CP assumptions must retain that scope unless separately proved globally valid.
assumptions_latex: \(F_D\subseteq F\).
The deduction is established for \(F_D\), not necessarily for \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall x\in F_D,\ a^Tx\le b)\centernot\Longrightarrow(\forall x\in F,\ a^Tx\le b).
knowledge_statements.title: Local MIP Deductions Require Scope Preservation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe operational cycle for domains, relaxations, bounds, cuts, infeasibility, and incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Encode the current CP store into MIP restrictions and solve or separate over \(P_D\). Import infeasibility or a certified objective bound only under the containment and objective scope used to derive it; import a cut or bound at its certified local or global scope; decode and validate every proposed incumbent in the original model. Apply CP reductions back to the MIP side only as restrictions valid under the same active state, then repeat until neither side produces a new valid deduction or the state is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exchange restrictions and certified MIP outcomes with explicit scope, and validate every decoded incumbent before using it.
assumptions_latex: The CP–MIP Channeling Contract holds.
Every imported deduction retains its validity scope.
Each accepted incumbent is checked in the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every exchange preserves }F_D\text{ and every accepted incumbent belongs to }F_D.
knowledge_statements.title: Scoped CP–MIP Exchange Cycle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bidirectional compatibility requirements for a CP model and a mixed-integer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A CP–MIP interface consists of compatible encoding and decoding maps between shared CP decisions and MIP variables. At CP store \(D\), the MIP region \(P_D\) must contain every encoded original solution in \(F_D\). Imported domain reductions or inequalities must be valid for their declared scope, and an imported incumbent must decode to a complete assignment that is validated against the original model and objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CP–MIP interface channels shared decisions while preserving all original solutions, scopes imported deductions, and validates decoded incumbents.
assumptions_latex: Encoding and decoding agree on shared decisions.
\(F_D\subseteq P_D\).
Objective values are evaluated consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{enc}(F_D)\subseteq P_D\text{ and every accepted incumbent decodes into }F_D.

notation.meaning: Original feasible set under CP store D

knowledge_statements.title: CP–MIP Channeling Contract

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the feasible set of the CP model.
\(P\) is a mixed-integer relaxation satisfying \(X\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounds, incumbents, and cuts exchanged through the interface remain valid for \(X\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard CP-MIP channeling and valid-cut interface formulation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization-oriented interface between constraint propagation and mixed-integer optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A CP-MIP interface supplies channeling maps between CP assignments and MIP variables. At a search state with domain product \(D\), the MIP side optimizes over a relaxation \(P_D\) satisfying \(X\cap D\subseteq P_D\). It may return a valid lower bound, a feasible incumbent decoded into \(X\), or an inequality valid for \(X\cap D\). The CP side may return tightened domains or valid constraints, and the MIP model may incorporate them only while preserving the containment \(X\cap D\subseteq P_D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CP and MIP components exchange channelled domains, valid relaxations, bounds, cuts, and feasible incumbents without losing original solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: CP–MIP Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The CP–MIP interface is plausible, but no source is supplied and the minimization objective needed to interpret returned lower bounds is not formally introduced.

children.title: Theory-Propagation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver interfaces exposing domain-specific propagation to a coordinating reasoning engine.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity contract for conflict and propagation explanations returned by a theory solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Theory conflicts and propagations must be backed by theory-valid clauses; their explanations need not be minimal.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha\) is the current set of assigned theory literals.
\(C,E\subseteq\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sound Theory Explanation Contract

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes optional propagation completeness from mandatory consistency checking and conflict blocking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Failure to report every entailed theory literal weakens pruning but does not invalidate reported \(T\)-valid lemmas. A complete combined decision procedure must nevertheless theory-check every candidate Boolean model and must eventually block each theory-inconsistent candidate with a sound lemma; these obligations alone do not replace completeness and termination of the Boolean and theory procedures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Missed theory propagations are safe, but unchecked or perpetually unblocked theory-inconsistent Boolean models destroy completeness.
assumptions_latex: Every reported theory lemma is \(T\)-valid.
The coordinating engine generates Boolean candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Propagation incompleteness is sound, but complete decision requires final theory checking and eventual conflict blocking.}
review_flags: Combined-procedure completeness also depends on complete terminating component procedures.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Theory Propagation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination result for a nonforgetting Boolean–theory loop over a finite abstraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the Boolean abstraction has finitely many total assignments, Boolean search terminates between theory calls, every theory call terminates, and every theory-inconsistent candidate causes permanent learning of a clause falsified by that candidate. If clause deletion or restarting cannot permit rejected candidates to recur indefinitely, the combined loop terminates with either a theory-consistent model or Boolean unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite Boolean abstraction terminates when component calls terminate and every theory-inconsistent candidate is eventually blocked from recurring.
assumptions_latex: The Boolean abstraction has finitely many total assignments.
Boolean search and every theory check terminate.
Every rejected total candidate is permanently blocked or otherwise cannot recur indefinitely.
review_flags: Unrestricted forgetting or restarting that permits indefinite recurrence invalidates the conclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Abstraction Termination of Theory-Lemma Search

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a Boolean skeleton interpreted modulo a theory \(T\).
\(\alpha\) is a partial assignment to theory atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Theory messages learned by Boolean search are \(T\)-valid consequences and therefore preserve \(T\)-satisfiability.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DPLL(T)-style exchange of theory consequences and conflicts with Boolean search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(F\), \(T\), and \(\alpha\), invoke a theory solver on the theory literals selected by \(\alpha\). If they are inconsistent, return a theory lemma \(
eg\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor
eg\ell_k\) with \(T\models
eg\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor
eg\ell_k\). If they imply an unassigned theory literal \(q\), return \(
eg\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor
eg\ell_k\lor q\), also entailed by \(T\). Add the returned clause to Boolean search; stop when a total theory-consistent assignment is found or the learned clauses make \(F\) unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theory solver returns entailed propagation and conflict clauses to Boolean search until a theory-consistent model or unsatisfiability is obtained.
knowledge_statements.title: Theory-Propagation Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The DPLL(T)-style protocol and algorithm content kind fit the leaf, but the theory-lemma and termination claims require a specialized source with a precise locator.

children.title: Hybrid Interface Translation
children.top_down_role: Translation of domains, bounds, explanations, and conflicts across hybrid interfaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness condition for translating explanations and conflicts between hybrid solver formalisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a target-side explanation satisfies \(M_2\models E_2\Rightarrow c_2\), communicating decoded formulas \(\rho_E(E_2)\) and \(\rho_C(c_2)\) is sound only if \(M_1\models\rho_E(E_2)\Rightarrow\rho_C(c_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A translated explanation is sound only when its decoded implication is valid in the source model.
assumptions_latex: \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are source and target models.
\(E_2\Rightarrow c_2\) is valid in the target model.
\(\rho_E\) and \(\rho_C\) decode target formulas into the source language.
review_flags: Target validity alone does not establish decoded source validity; the latter is an independent interface obligation.
knowledge_statements.title: Explanation-Preserving Interface Translation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semantic Fidelity Does Not Preserve Propagation Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between solution preservation and propagation equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact preservation of feasible assignments does not imply equality of source propagation and decoded target propagation. Propagation equivalence requires an additional closure correspondence, such as \(\rho(P_2(\tau(D)))=P_1(D)\) for every store \(D\) in the declared interface domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution-exact encoding can nevertheless propagate less strongly than its source representation.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau\) and \(\rho\) preserve feasible assignments.
\(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are propagation closures on compatible interface stores.
review_flags: Closure equality presupposes compatible store and decoding domains.
knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Fidelity Does Not Preserve Propagation Strength

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preimage Criterion for Sound Translated Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic safety condition for importing a target-side reduction into the source store.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_1(D)\) be the source-feasible assignments represented by store \(D\), let \(\tau\) translate source assignments, and let \(R_2\) be the target region retained after pruning. Enforcing membership in \(R_2\) through the interface is sound for the current source store if and only if \(\tau(F_1(D))\subseteq R_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A translated target reduction is safe exactly when it retains every translated source-feasible assignment in the current store.
assumptions_latex: \(F_1(D)\) is the set of source-feasible assignments compatible with the current store.
\(\tau\) is defined on every assignment in \(F_1(D)\).
Importing the reduction means requiring translated assignments to lie in \(R_2\).

notation.meaning: source-feasible assignments represented by the current store

knowledge_statements.title: Preimage Criterion for Sound Translated Pruning

assumptions_latex: \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are source and target models with solution sets \(S_1\) and \(S_2\).
\(\tau\) translates source assignments and \(\rho\) decodes target assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau\) and \(\rho\) define a sound, solution-preserving hybrid interface translation.

notation.meaning: solution sets of the two models

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: satisfaction-preserving translation is the standard correctness condition for hybrid encodings
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness condition for translating assignments, solutions, and propagated facts across solver formalisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The interface translation is solution preserving when \(x\in S_1\) implies \(\tau(x)\in S_2\), every \(y\in S_2\) satisfies \(\rho(y)\in S_1\), and \(\rho(\tau(x))=x\) on source variables for every \(x\in S_1\). A target-side inferred predicate \(p\) may be propagated to the source as \(q\) only if every translated source assignment satisfying the current interface state obeys \(p(\tau(x))\Rightarrow q(x)\). Objective translation additionally requires equality, or a declared order-preserving transformation, of corresponding objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid translation must preserve solutions, decode target solutions correctly, and translate only logically valid propagated facts and objective comparisons.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Interface Translation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated conditions plausibly express solution-preserving translation, but no cited source supports this particular combination of encoding, decoding, propagation, and objective conditions.

children.title: Propagation Complexity Boundary Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Complexity is organized by representation, structural regime, propagation strength, and decomposition rather than by isolated statement-level bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-counting enforcement of arc consistency for explicit binary relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every directed constraint arc and endpoint value, AC-4 stores the number of currently present supporting values and, for each value, the counters to which it contributes. Initialize these structures from the explicit allowed tuples. Whenever a value is deleted, decrement exactly the counters it supported; delete and enqueue a value when a required counter becomes zero. Each stored tuple contribution is initialized and processed only a constant number of times.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-4 maintains support counters so that stored allowed pairs are processed only constantly many times.
assumptions_latex: There are \(e\) binary constraints and every domain has size at most \(d\).
Allowed tuples and reverse support lists are explicit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{AC-4 enforces arc consistency using }O(ed^2)\text{ worst-case tuple-support work}.
knowledge_statements.title: AC-4 Support-Counting Algorithm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case time and space including explicit binary support structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A binary relation contains at most \(d^2\) allowed pairs. Across \(e\) relations, AC-4 initializes and processes \(O(ed^2)\) pair incidences, enforcing arc consistency in \(O(ed^2)\) worst-case time and using \(O(ed^2+nd)\) space for explicit support lists, counters, domains, and the deletion queue. The time bound matches the order of the largest explicit binary-table input.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AC-4 enforces arc consistency in O(ed²) worst-case time, matching the worst-case order of explicit binary tables.
assumptions_latex: The CSP has \(n\) variables, \(e\) explicitly stored binary constraints, and maximum domain size \(d\).
Tuple and support-list access has constant-time overhead.
knowledge_statements.title: AC-4 Extensional Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arc Consistency for a Binary Table
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local support condition enforced in the binary extensional regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a binary extensional constraint \(C_{xy}\subseteq D_x\times D_y\), the directed arc \((x,C_{xy},y)\) is arc consistent exactly when \(\forall a\in D_x\;\exists b\in D_y:(a,b)\in C_{xy}\). The constraint is arc consistent when this condition holds in both directions. Enforcement repeatedly deletes unsupported values until every directed arc satisfies the condition or a domain is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary table is arc consistent when every current value at either endpoint has a compatible current value at the other endpoint.
assumptions_latex: D_x,D_y\text{ are finite}.
C_{xy}\text{ is explicitly represented by allowed tuples}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AC(C_{xy})\iff(\forall a\in D_x\;\exists b\in D_y:(a,b)\in C_{xy})\land(\forall b\in D_y\;\exists a\in D_x:(a,b)\in C_{xy}).

notation.meaning: allowed-tuple relation on variables x and y

knowledge_statements.title: Arc Consistency for a Binary Table
Binary Extensional Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical AC-3 bound for explicitly represented binary finite-domain constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite binary CSP with \(n\) variables, \(e\) explicitly represented binary constraints, maximum current-domain size \(d\), and constant-time tuple-membership and domain-membership tests, AC-3 enforces arc consistency in \(O(ed^3)\) time and uses \(O(ed^2+nd)\) space when the explicit constraint tables are included in the space bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For binary table constraints, AC-3 enforces arc consistency in O(ed^3) time and uses O(ed^2+nd) space, including the explicit tables and domains.
assumptions_latex: The finite CSP has \(n\) variables, \(e\) binary extensional constraints, and maximum current-domain size \(d\).
Tuple-membership and domain-membership tests take constant time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AC-3 enforces arc consistency in \(O(ed^3)\) time and uses \(O(ed^2+nd)\) space, including the explicit input tables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally checkable support and failure certificates for explicit allowed-tuple constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an extensional constraint \(c\) with scope \(S_c\), current domains \((D_x)_{x\in S_c}\), and allowed table \(R_c\), a value \(a\in D_x\) is supported exactly when some \(t\in R_c\) satisfies \(t_x=a\) and \(t_y\in D_y\) for every \(y\in S_c\). Such a tuple certifies support. If complete filtering empties a domain, then \(R_c\cap\prod_{y\in S_c}D_y=\varnothing\), certifying local infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compatible listed tuple certifies value support; domain wipeout under complete table filtering certifies that no compatible allowed tuple exists.
assumptions_latex: \(R_c\) is an explicitly listed finite allowed-tuple relation.
All current domains are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\in D_x\text{ is supported}\iff \exists t\in R_c:\ t_x=a\land(\forall y\in S_c)\ t_y\in D_y.
knowledge_statements.title: Tuple-Support Certificates for Extensional GAC

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomiality Is Relative to the Materialized Table
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding boundary for the explicit-table enforcement bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filtering bound polynomial in the materialized table length is polynomial in the extensional input size. It need not be polynomial in an alternative encoding length \(|I|\) when the corresponding tables have superpolynomial size in \(|I|\), because materializing those tables may itself require superpolynomial time and space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial explicit-table filtering does not automatically remain polynomial under an exponentially more succinct encoding.
assumptions_latex: The complexity measure includes the complete materialized allowed-tuple tables.
The alternative encoding and table representation need not be polynomially related in size.

notation.meaning: alternative encoding of the represented relations

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomiality Is Relative to the Materialized Table
Bounded-Arity Extensional Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial enforcement bound measured in the full size of bounded-arity allowed-tuple tables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite CSP with \(n\) variables, maximum current-domain size \(d\), and constraints of arity at most a fixed constant \(k\), each represented by an explicit allowed-tuple relation \(R_c\). Let \(T=\sum_c |\operatorname{scope}(c)|\,|R_c|\). Repeated full-table filtering enforces generalized arc consistency in \(O(ndT)\) time and \(O(T+nd)\) space, hence in time polynomial in the explicit representation size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed-arity constraints represented by explicit allowed-tuple tables, repeated table filtering enforces generalized arc consistency in O(ndT) time and O(T+nd) space.
assumptions_latex: The finite CSP has \(n\) variables and maximum current-domain size \(d\).
Every constraint has arity at most a fixed constant \(k\) and is represented by an explicit allowed-tuple relation \(R_c\).
\(T=\sum_c |\operatorname{scope}(c)|\,|R_c|\) is the total tuple-incidence size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated full-table filtering enforces generalized arc consistency in \(O(ndT)\) time and \(O(T+nd)\) space.
review_flags: tighter algorithm-specific bound may be available

children.title: Implicit Representation Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity boundaries for constraints represented without explicit relation enumeration.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Encoded-Predicate and Oracle Cost Models Must Be Distinguished
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary complexity convention for implicit representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an encoded predicate, runtime includes predicate-evaluation time as a function of \(|I|\) and tuple length. For an oracle representation, a query bound counts oracle calls and becomes a bit-complexity bound only after a query-cost convention is supplied. Thus polynomially many abstract oracle calls need not constitute a polynomial-time encoded algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle-query complexity and encoded runtime cannot be interchanged without specifying the cost of a query.
assumptions_latex: The represented relation is accessed either by an encoded evaluator or an abstract oracle.

notation.meaning: number of oracle calls made on instance I

knowledge_statements.title: Encoded-Predicate and Oracle Cost Models Must Be Distinguished

assumptions_latex: An instance \(I\) encodes a finite relation \(R_I\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_r\).
The tuples of \(R_I\) are not required to be enumerated in the input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Support testing is the existential decision problem induced by the implicit representation.

notation.meaning: current domain of variable position i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard distinction between explicit tuple tables and succinct predicate-or-oracle representations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint relations represented by predicates, circuits, or oracles rather than enumerated tuples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An implicit representation regime specifies each relation \(R_I\) by an encoding \(I\) together with a membership predicate or oracle deciding whether \(t\in R_I\), without listing all members of \(R_I\). Relative to current domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_r\), a value \(a\in D_i\) has support exactly when there exists \(t\in R_I\cap(D_1\times\cdots\times D_r)\) with \(t_i=a\). Representation size is \(|I|+\sum_i|D_i|\), rather than \(|R_I|\), so propagation complexity is measured in this succinct input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicit constraint encodes a relation by a predicate or oracle; propagation must solve existential support questions without enumerating all tuples.
knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Representation Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition captures existential support under a succinct relation representation, but a source is required and any complexity interpretation must distinguish encoded predicates from unit-cost oracles.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Membership Access Does Not Give Support Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed existential-search boundary for implicitly represented relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when membership \(t\in R_I\) is polynomial-time decidable, designated-value support can be NP-hard because it quantifies existentially over the other coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fast tuple membership need not imply fast support testing.
assumptions_latex: Candidate tuples have polynomial encoding length.
Membership and support use the same encoded cost model.
review_flags: deferred_canonical_home: the computational nonimplication is primarily owned by the Succinctness-Induced Complexity sibling
knowledge_statements.title: Membership Access Does Not Give Support Access

intermediate_metadata.reason: The leaf owns predicate-or-oracle representation, existential support semantics, input-size measurement, and the oracle-cost distinction. The proposed membership-versus-support hardness statement was deferred to Succinctness-Induced Complexity; dedicated global representations were also excluded.

children.title: Global Representation Regime
children.top_down_role: Complexity boundaries arising from dedicated global-constraint representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Semantics Alone Gives No Tractability Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between a global-constraint interface and a family-specific filtering algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial-size semantic description of a global-constraint family does not itself imply polynomial-time support testing or generalized-arc-consistency enforcement. A tractability claim requires exploitable family-specific structure; if designated-value support is NP-hard for the family, polynomial-time complete filtering would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Calling a constraint global does not make complete propagation tractable; tractability depends on family-specific structure.
assumptions_latex: The scope or parameters may grow with the instance.
Complexity is measured in the global representation and current-domain encoding length.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Semantics Alone Gives No Tractability Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dedicated Propagators Need Not Materialize the Relation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic obligations of a propagator using a family-specific global representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a global instance \(C(I,X)\) denote relation \(R_I\). A sound propagator may compute a contracting store \(P_I(D)\subseteq D\) using a family-specific graph, automaton, dynamic program, or other representation. Soundness requires every tuple in \(R_I\cap\prod_xD_x\) to remain represented by \(P_I(D)\); complete filtering additionally requires every retained value to occur in such a tuple. Neither property requires explicit enumeration of \(R_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dedicated global propagator may use compact family-specific structure without enumerating the represented relation.
assumptions_latex: \(P_I\) is a domain-reduction operator for the represented global constraint.
Current domains are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_I\cap\prod_xD_x\subseteq\prod_xP_I(D)_x,\qquad P_I(D)_x=\{a:\exists t\in R_I\cap\prod_yD_y,\ t_x=a\}\text{ under complete filtering}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dedicated Propagators Need Not Materialize the Relation

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a finite-domain constraint whose scope may grow with the instance.
\(R_C\) is the relation defined by the constraint's semantic specification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Generalized arc consistency for \(C\) is exactly retention of values having a tuple in \(R_C\) within the current domains.

notation.meaning: relation defined by the global constraint

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard semantic definition of a global constraint and its generalized-arc-consistency propagator
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic, potentially unbounded-arity constraints equipped with dedicated propagation procedures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A global representation consists of a constraint symbol \(C\), a scope \(S=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\), parameters, and a semantic relation \(R_C\subseteq D_1^0\times\cdots\times D_r^0\), where \(r\) may vary with the instance. Under current domains \(D_i\subseteq D_i^0\), a generalized-arc-consistency propagator returns domains \(D_i'\) satisfying \(a\in D_i'\) exactly when some tuple \(t\in R_C\cap(D_1\times\cdots\times D_r)\) has \(t_i=a\). A propagator may use the global semantics without materializing \(R_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global constraint defines a potentially unbounded-arity relation and supports dedicated propagation without enumerating its complete relation.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Representation Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic definition of a global constraint and exact generalized-arc-consistency filtering is coherent and fits the leaf, but it lacks a specialized source and locator.

children.title: Succinctness-Induced Complexity
children.top_down_role: Effects of compact representation on enforcement cost and attainable propagation strength.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Testing and Complete Filtering Are Polynomially Interreducible
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity equivalence when current-domain literals are explicitly and polynomially represented.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a succinct constraint instance has \(M=\sum_i|D_i|\) explicitly represented variable-value pairs. One complete-filtering call decides support for every pair. Conversely, calling a designated-value support procedure once for each pair constructs the completely filtered domains using at most \(M\) calls. Hence the two tasks are polynomial-time interreducible when \(M\) is polynomially bounded by the input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With explicitly listed finite domains, designated-value support and complete filtering differ by only a polynomial number of calls.
assumptions_latex: Every current-domain value is explicitly represented.
\(M\) is polynomially bounded in the encoded instance length.
knowledge_statements.title: Support Testing and Complete Filtering Are Polynomially Interreducible

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer boundary between succinct and extensional encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an instance of succinct length \(L\) denote a relation whose explicit table has length \(E(L)\). Expansion followed by an algorithm polynomial in \(E(L)\) is polynomial in \(L\) only when \(E(L)\) is polynomially bounded in \(L\). If \(E(L)=2^{\Omega(L)}\), this strategy takes exponential time or output space in the worst case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expanding a compact relation before filtering is polynomial only when the expanded table is polynomially bounded in the compact input.
assumptions_latex: The expansion explicitly enumerates the denoted relation.

notation.meaning: length of the expanded extensional table

knowledge_statements.title: Expansion Can Destroy Polynomial Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hard Complete Filtering Does Not Preclude Weaker Polynomial Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation-strength boundary under succinct encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: NP-hardness of exact designated-value support rules out polynomial-time complete filtering unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\), but it does not rule out polynomial-time sound propagators computing relaxations of the supported-value closure. Such propagators may retain unsupported values but must not delete values occurring in feasible tuples.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When exact filtering is hard, weaker sound propagation may remain polynomial by retaining some unsupported values.
assumptions_latex: The weaker propagator is required to be sound but not complete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Support}\text{ NP-hard}\centernot\implies\text{every sound nontrivial propagator is NP-hard}.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard Complete Filtering Does Not Preclude Weaker Polynomial Propagation
Succinctness-Induced Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hardness boundary created when a polynomial-size encoding denotes an exponentially large relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) succinctly encode a finite relation \(R_I\) and its finite domains. If deciding whether a designated value \(a\) at position \(i\) has a tuple \(t\in R_I\) within those domains with \(t_i=a\) is NP-hard under polynomial-time reductions, then polynomial-time enforcement of generalized arc consistency for this representation family would imply \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\). This hardness is measured in the succinct encoding length, not the size of an expanded tuple table.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If support testing is NP-hard for a succinct relation family, polynomial-time generalized-arc-consistency enforcement for that family would imply P equals NP.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) succinctly represents a finite relation \(R_I\) together with finite current domains.
Deciding whether the designated value \(a\) at position \(i\) has a supporting tuple in \(R_I\) is NP-hard in the encoding length \(|I|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polynomial-time generalized-arc-consistency enforcement for the represented family would imply \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\).
review_flags: complexity classification depends on the representation family

children.title: Tree-Structured Regimes
children.top_down_role: Propagation completeness and tractability within tree-structured constraint networks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional propagation followed by backtrack-free solution construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Root the primal tree. Process every nonroot variable \(x\) after its descendants and delete each \(a\in D_{p(x)}\) having no \(b\in D_x\) with \((a,b)\in R_{p(x)x}\). If a domain becomes empty, report unsatisfiable. Otherwise choose any remaining root value and traverse outward, choosing for every child a retained supporting value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Revise constraints toward a root and then choose supporting values outward to decide and solve the tree CSP without backtracking.
assumptions_latex: The finite binary primal graph is a rooted tree.
Support tests and revisions are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The algorithm reports failure iff the CSP is unsatisfiable, and otherwise returns a solution}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rooted Tree-CSP Propagation and Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost for directly tested binary supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) variables with domains of size at most \(d\), the rooted tree has \(n-1\) edges. Directly testing all parent-child value pairs takes \(O(nd^2)\) time and storing one selected support per directed edge and parent value takes \(O(nd)\) auxiliary space, in addition to the represented constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct extensional tree-CSP procedure runs in O(nd²) time and O(nd) auxiliary space.
assumptions_latex: The primal graph is a tree.
Every domain has cardinality at most \(d\).
Binary supports are tested directly.

notation.meaning: variable count and maximum domain size

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-CSP Propagation Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating primal trees from cyclic binary networks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x,y,z\in\{0,1\}\), the constraints \(x
e y\), \(y
e z\), and \(z
e x\) leave every value arc supported but admit no satisfying assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Boolean odd disequality cycle is arc consistent and nonempty but unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Cycle Failure of Arc-Consistency Completeness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary of the binary tree regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite binary CSP is tree structured when its primal graph \(G=(V,E)\), with \(xy\in E\) exactly when some constraint contains both variables, is a tree. A forest-structured CSP is a disjoint union of tree components and is solved componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary CSP is tree structured when its primal graph is a tree; forests split into independent tree components.
assumptions_latex: All nonunary constraints are binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is a tree, or componentwise a forest}.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Structured Binary Constraint Network

assumptions_latex: A finite binary CSP has a connected primal graph that is a tree.
Every binary constraint is arc consistent and every current domain is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The CSP is satisfiable, and every remaining value extends to a complete solution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical global-completeness theorem for arc consistency on tree-structured binary CSPs
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global completeness of arc consistency for finite binary CSPs with tree primal graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be the primal graph, and let each edge \(xy\in E\) carry relation \(R_{xy}\subseteq D_x\times D_y\). Suppose that for every \(xy\in E\), each \(a\in D_x\) has some \(b\in D_y\) with \((a,b)\in R_{xy}\), and symmetrically each value of \(D_y\) has support in \(D_x\). If \(G\) is a tree and all domains are nonempty, then a satisfying assignment exists. Moreover, for every variable \(x\) and every \(a\in D_x\), there is a satisfying assignment whose value at \(x\) is \(a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a tree-structured binary CSP, nonempty arc-consistent domains guarantee a solution, and every remaining value occurs in some solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Structured Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is the standard global-completeness result for arc consistency on finite tree-structured binary CSPs, and its strengthened value-extension conclusion is coherent, but no source is supplied.

children.title: Acyclic-Network Regimes
children.top_down_role: Propagation completeness across broader acyclic network structures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-free propagation for extensionally represented relations on a supplied join tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Root the join tree. For a directed edge \(i\to j\), revise \(R_j\leftarrow R_j\ltimes R_i=\{t\in R_j:\exists s\in R_i,\ t|_{S_i\cap S_j}=s|_{S_i\cap S_j}\}\). One pass toward the root followed by one pass away from it produces mutually semijoin-consistent adjacent relations. A relation becomes empty exactly when the global join is empty; otherwise each final relation is the projection of the global join onto its scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inward and outward semijoin pass decides emptiness and removes exactly the tuples lacking global extensions.
assumptions_latex: The finite scope hypergraph has a supplied join tree.
Semijoins are computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Pass Join-Tree Semijoin Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-sensitive cost of the two-pass algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\) relations of cardinality at most \(r\), the \(2(m-1)\) directed semijoins take \(O(mr)\) expected time when separator keys are hashable and \(O(mr^2)\) time under direct tuple-pair testing, excluding key-construction costs. Relation storage is \(O(mr)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Indexed semijoins are linear in total bounded relation size, whereas naive pair testing can be quadratic per edge.
assumptions_latex: Every current relation has at most \(r\) tuples.
Hash construction and lookup have expected constant cost per represented separator key.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T=O(mr)\text{ expected with indexes},\qquad T=O(mr^2)\text{ with pair testing},\qquad S=O(mr).
knowledge_statements.title: Join-Tree Semijoin Cost

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pairwise Agreement Fails on a Cycle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of separator agreement without join-tree acyclicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y,z\in\{0,1\}\), impose \(x=y\), \(y=z\), and \(z\ne x\). Every relation is nonempty and the projections of each intersecting pair onto its shared variable are both \(\{0,1\}\), but the natural join is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two equalities and one disequality on a triangle have complete pairwise projection agreement but no global solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Agreement Fails on a Cycle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural definition of the acyclic-network regime for finite constraint hypergraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite scope hypergraph \(H=(X,\mathcal E)\) is join-tree acyclic if there is a tree \(T\) on \(\mathcal E\) such that, for every \(x\in X\), the scopes containing \(x\) induce a connected subtree. Equivalently, every scope on the path between scopes \(e\) and \(f\) contains \(e\cap f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scope hypergraph is join-tree acyclic when its scopes admit a running-intersection tree.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ is join-tree acyclic}\iff H\text{ admits a running-intersection join tree}.
knowledge_statements.title: Join-Tree Acyclicity
Acyclic-Network Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Join-tree form of propagation completeness for finite acyclic constraint hypergraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let finite constraints have nonempty relations \(R_i\) on scopes \(S_i\), and let \(J\) be a join tree satisfying the running-intersection property. If every edge \(ij\) of \(J\) satisfies \(\pi_{S_i\cap S_j}(R_i)=\pi_{S_i\cap S_j}(R_j)\), then the natural join \(R=\mathop{\bigbowtie}_{i}R_i\) is nonempty and satisfies \(\pi_{S_i}(R)=R_i\) for every \(i\). Consequently, every tuple retained in any \(R_i\) extends to a complete solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a finite join-tree network, nonempty relations agreeing on every separator have a nonempty lossless natural join, and every retained tuple extends to a complete solution.
assumptions_latex: The finite constraint hypergraph admits a join tree \(J\) satisfying the running-intersection property.
Each relation \(R_i\) on scope \(S_i\) is nonempty.
Adjacent relations have equal projections on their shared variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The natural join \(R=\mathop{\bigbowtie}_{i}R_i\) is nonempty, and \(\pi_{S_i}(R)=R_i\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: natural join of all constraint relations

review_flags: specialized database or constraint-programming source required

children.title: Tree-to-Acyclic Generalization
children.top_down_role: Structural features preserved or lost when moving beyond tree-shaped networks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-size limitation of the tree-to-acyclic reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a scope \(e\) contains \(|e|\) variables with domains of size at most \(d\), its explicit cluster domain can contain \(d^{|e|}\) tuples. Join-tree acyclicity therefore removes cyclic search but does not by itself make compactly represented, unbounded-arity relations polynomial-time enumerable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduction preserves search-free tree structure but can create exponentially large cluster domains.
assumptions_latex: Cluster relations are materialized extensionally.
knowledge_statements.title: Cluster-Domain Blowup

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency object preserved and changed by the cluster reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the cluster reduction, arc consistency between adjacent cluster variables is exactly mutual semijoin consistency of their relations. The supported objects are relation tuples and separator assignments rather than individual original-variable values, so arc consistency on the original primal graph need not express the required join-tree consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cluster arc consistency is semijoin consistency, replacing original values by relation tuples and primal edges by separators.
assumptions_latex: The cluster-variable reduction is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{AC}(Y_e,Y_f)\iff R_e\text{ and }R_f\text{ are mutually semijoin consistent}.
knowledge_statements.title: Arc-Consistency–Semijoin Correspondence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cluster-Variable Reduction Along a Join Tree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mechanism carrying the binary-tree theorem to acyclic hypergraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given relations \(R_e\) whose scopes form a join tree \(T\), introduce a cluster variable \(Y_e\) with domain \(R_e\). For each tree edge \(ef\), impose \(Y_e|_{e\cap f}=Y_f|_{e\cap f}\). Solutions of this tree-structured binary cluster CSP are in bijection with tuples of \(\bigbowtie_eR_e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treating each constraint tuple as a cluster-variable value converts an acyclic hypergraph network into a binary tree CSP with separator-equality constraints.
assumptions_latex: The finite scopes admit a join tree.
Each cluster domain is the corresponding relation.

notation.meaning: cluster variable associated with scope e

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster-Variable Reduction Along a Join Tree
Tree-to-Acyclic Generalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Join-tree extension of the tree-structured binary-CSP consistency result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N=(X,\{R_e\}_{e\in E})\) be a finite constraint network whose scope hypergraph admits a join tree \(T\): for every variable, the hyperedges containing it induce a connected subtree. If every adjacent pair \(e,f\) in \(T\) is semijoin consistent, meaning that each tuple of \(R_e\) agrees on \(e\cap f\) with some tuple of \(R_f\), and conversely, then every tuple in every \(R_e\) extends to a satisfying assignment of \(\mathcal N\). Consequently, nonemptiness of all relations after join-tree propagation is equivalent to satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an acyclic constraint hypergraph, pairwise consistency along a join tree makes every surviving tuple globally extendible and decides satisfiability without search.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and all constraint relations are finite.
The scope hypergraph of \(\mathcal N\) admits a join tree.
Adjacent relations are mutually semijoin consistent on their intersections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N\text{ is satisfiable}\iff (\forall e\in E)\;R_e\ne\varnothing\), and every surviving tuple has a global extension.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical join-tree global-consistency theorem for acyclic constraint networks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The join-tree theorem is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source or theorem locator supports the stated tuple-extension conclusion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered enforcement through exact bucket elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Process variables in reverse instantiation order. At each variable, join its bucket relations, project the join onto its remaining neighbors, and place the projected relation in the bucket of its latest remaining variable. An empty generated relation reports inconsistency. Retaining the intermediate relations permits backtrack-free forward reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bucket elimination joins each variable's relations and projects onto its earlier neighbors, producing the directional information needed for forward reconstruction.
assumptions_latex: Relations are finite and relational operations are exact.
The ordering is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Elimination either derives emptiness or preserves an equivalent network for ordered reconstruction}.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional Consistency by Elimination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensional cost controlled by the selected ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With maximum domain size \(d\) and induced width \(w(\pi)\), explicit elimination forms relations on at most \(w(\pi)+1\) variables. Under standard table operations it takes \(O(nd^{w(\pi)+1})\) time and stores \(O(nd^{w(\pi)})\) message tuples, up to polynomial representation factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directional elimination is exponential in the induced width of the chosen ordering.
assumptions_latex: Intermediate relations are stored extensionally.
The maximum domain size is \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T=O(nd^{w(\pi)+1}),\qquad S=O(nd^{w(\pi)})\text{ up to representation factors}.
review_flags: Exact exponents and storage depend on table and message conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Induced-Width Elimination Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-sensitive width controlling directional enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Eliminate vertices in reverse instantiation order, connecting all remaining neighbors of each eliminated vertex. The induced width \(w(\pi)\) is the maximum number of remaining neighbors at an elimination step. The primal-graph treewidth satisfies \(\operatorname{tw}(G)=\min_\pi w(\pi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Induced width is the largest remaining-neighbor set created by an ordering; minimizing it gives treewidth.
assumptions_latex: Elimination and instantiation directions are fixed as stated.
knowledge_statements.title: Induced Width of an Ordering

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-relative binary consistency under an explicit convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ordering \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), a binary network is directionally arc consistent when, for every constraint \(R_{ij}\) with \(i<j\), every \(a\in D_{x_i}\) has a support \(b\in D_{x_j}\) satisfying \((a,b)\in R_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directional arc consistency requires each earlier variable value to have support in the later endpoint of every constraint.
assumptions_latex: The relevant constraints are binary.
The earlier-to-later support convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall i<j,\ \forall a\in D_{x_i},\ \exists b\in D_{x_j}:(a,b)\in R_{ij}.
review_flags: Direction conventions vary; this record fixes one explicitly.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional Arc Consistency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of tractability under a poor ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two orderings of the same primal graph can have different induced widths. Consequently, explicit directional enforcement under a poor ordering can create exponentially larger intermediate relations than an ordering attaining treewidth, although the underlying CSP is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poor ordering can create exponentially larger intermediate scopes than a width-minimizing ordering.
assumptions_latex: Intermediate relations are materialized explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w(\pi_1)\ll w(\pi_2)\implies d^{w(\pi_1)+1}\ll d^{w(\pi_2)+1}\text{ may hold}.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Sensitivity
Ordered Directional Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtrack-free search under directional consistency calibrated to induced width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N\) be a finite binary constraint network with variable ordering \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), maximum domain size \(d\), and induced width \(w\) under that ordering. If \(\mathcal N\) is directionally strongly \((w+1)\)-consistent—every consistent assignment to at most \(w\) earlier neighbors of \(x_i\) extends to a value of \(x_i\)—then assigning variables in the stated order never encounters a dead end. Thus, unless consistency enforcement detects failure, any sequence of supported choices extends to a complete solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directional strong consistency one level above the ordering’s induced width makes ordered variable assignment backtrack-free.
assumptions_latex: The network is finite and binary.
The ordering has induced width \(w\).
Directional strong \((w+1)\)-consistency holds.

notation.meaning: induced width of the variable ordering

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: directional consistency and induced-width backtrack-freeness
ordering convention and authoritative theorem locator required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits ordered directional regimes, but the direction of the ordering and the precise induced-width backtrack-freeness hypothesis require an authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision and construction given a decomposition and enumerable bag relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct the bag relations of a supplied width-\(w\) decomposition, perform inward and outward semijoin passes, and report unsatisfiable if a bag relation becomes empty. Otherwise select compatible bag tuples outward from a root and merge them on shared variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Materialize decomposition bags, run join-tree propagation, and merge compatible bag tuples to decide and solve the CSP.
assumptions_latex: A width-\(w\) tree decomposition is supplied.
Bag relations can be enumerated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure decides satisfiability and constructs a solution without backtracking}.
knowledge_statements.title: Width-Bounded Bag Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter dependence with a supplied linear-size decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) variables of maximum domain size \(d\), an \(O(n)\)-bag decomposition of width \(w\) has at most \(d^{w+1}\) assignments per bag. If testing the constraints assigned to a bag assignment is polynomial in \(|I|\), direct construction and propagation take \(O(nd^{w+1}\operatorname{poly}(|I|))\) time and \(O(nd^{w+1})\) space. The decomposition-construction cost is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a linear-size width-w decomposition, direct bag propagation is polynomial for fixed w and exponential in w.
assumptions_latex: The supplied decomposition has \(O(n)\) bags.
Constraint evaluation on a represented bag assignment is polynomial in the input size.
review_flags: The bound excludes finding the decomposition and is representation sensitive.
knowledge_statements.title: Treewidth-Calibrated Bag Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural parameter defining the leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tree decomposition of a primal graph \(G=(V,E)\) is a tree of bags \(B_t\subseteq V\) covering every vertex and edge such that the bags containing any fixed vertex form a connected subtree. Its width is \(\max_t|B_t|-1\), and \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\) is the minimum width. A family is bounded width when \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\le w\) for a fixed constant \(w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treewidth is one less than the largest bag in a smallest-width running-intersection decomposition; a bounded-width family fixes that width.
knowledge_statements.title: Treewidth and the Bounded-Width Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Fixed Consistency Level Covers Unbounded Width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of width-calibrated local consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every fixed \(k\), finite constraint networks exist that are strongly \(k\)-consistent but unsatisfiable. Thus no consistency level fixed independently of the instance decides all unbounded-width CSPs; the consistency level or decomposition width must grow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-level local consistency cannot decide arbitrary-width CSPs.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is fixed independently of the instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\;\exists\mathcal N:\ \mathcal N\text{ is strongly }k\text{-consistent and unsatisfiable}.
review_flags: A standard high-consistency unsatisfiable-family locator is desirable.
knowledge_statements.title: No Fixed Consistency Level Covers Unbounded Width

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acyclic representation underlying bounded-width tractability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a width-\(w\) tree decomposition, assign every original constraint to a bag containing its scope and form the relation of bag assignments satisfying all constraints assigned there. Link adjacent bags by equality on their intersection. The bag scopes form a join tree, have arity at most \(w+1\), and their compatible tuples project exactly to the original solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A width-w decomposition converts the CSP into an acyclic network of bag relations of arity at most w+1.
assumptions_latex: Every constraint scope is contained in a decomposition bag.
The supplied decomposition has width at most \(w\).
knowledge_statements.title: Bag-Relation Join-Tree Representation
Bounded-Width Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong local consistency solves finite CSPs of bounded primal-graph width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N\) be a finite constraint network with primal graph of treewidth at most \(w\). If strong \((w+1)\)-consistency has been established, then every consistent assignment to the variables already chosen along a width-\(w\) elimination ordering extends to the next variable. Hence an empty relation or domain certifies unsatisfiability; otherwise a complete solution can be constructed without backtracking. For every fixed \(w\), the required consistency enforcement and solution construction are polynomial in the network size and maximum domain cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On networks of fixed treewidth, strong consistency at level treewidth plus one decides satisfiability and permits backtrack-free construction.
assumptions_latex: The network and its domains are finite.
The primal graph has treewidth at most \(w\).
Strong \((w+1)\)-consistency is enforced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N\) is decided without search, in polynomial time for fixed \(w\).

notation.meaning: treewidth bound of the primal graph

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded-treewidth CSPs are solved by width-calibrated consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-width claim is standard in broad form, but no source establishes the stated consistency level, elimination-order convention, and polynomial enforcement conclusion together.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial source of explicit higher-consistency overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(n\) variables and maximum domain size \(d\), there are at most \(\binom ni d^i\) assignments to exactly \(i\) distinct variables. A generic method explicitly materializing all partial assignments through level \(k\) may therefore store up to \(\sum_{i=0}^k\binom ni d^i\) states before extension-test costs are counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit higher-consistency enforcement can materialize a binomial number of partial assignments through level k.
assumptions_latex: Partial assignments are represented explicitly.
Every variable domain has size at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_{\le k}\le\sum_{i=0}^k\binom ni d^i=O(n^kd^k)\text{ for fixed }k.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Assignment State-Space Growth

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Overhead with No Additional Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case absence of compensating inference benefit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every constraint relation is universal, the network is strongly \(k\)-consistent for every applicable \(k\). A higher-level explicit procedure can inspect additional collections of partial assignments while deleting none, so its added enforcement work can be positive while its pruning gain is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Universal constraints let higher consistency cost more while pruning nothing.
assumptions_latex: All constraint relations contain every tuple over their scopes.
The higher-level procedure performs additional level-specific checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Overhead with No Additional Pruning

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on the immutable naive complexity estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: No single time bound depending only on \(n,d,k\) describes every strong-consistency implementation. Extensional tables, intensional predicates, support indexes, decomposition methods, and implicit relations assign different costs to consistency and extension tests. The naive enumeration bound is therefore specific to its explicit computational model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher-consistency cost depends on relation representation and support testing, so enumeration bounds are not universally tight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_k\text{ cannot be determined from }(n,d,k)\text{ alone without a computational model}.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Dependence of Enforcement Bounds
Stronger-Consistency Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case combinatorial cost of increasing the local-consistency level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite network on \(n\) variables with domains of size at most \(d\). A direct strong \(k\)-consistency procedure must represent or inspect consistent assignments on up to \(k\) variables and test extension to an additional variable. There are at most \(\binom{n}{k}d^k\) such assignments and at most \(nd\) candidate extensions per assignment. Consequently, a naive enforcement bound is \(O(n^{k+1}d^{k+1})\) time and \(O(n^kd^k)\) stored assignment states; the dependence is polynomial only when \(k\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Naively enforcing consistency level k costs up to order n^(k+1)d^(k+1), so increasing strength can impose exponential dependence on k.
assumptions_latex: There are \(n\) finite-domain variables.
Every domain has cardinality at most \(d\).
Extension tests are performed by explicit enumeration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected duplication of the chapter's foundational consistency hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strong \((k+1)\)-consistency implies strong \(k\)-consistency, while the converse fails in general.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Node Count Is Not a Runtime Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance- and heuristic-dependence of the tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Residual tree size and per-node work depend on the instance, propagation schedule, variable and value ordering, restart policy, and implementation. Therefore a node-count reduction alone cannot certify a runtime improvement unless propagation and per-node costs are also controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fewer search nodes do not guarantee less runtime because propagation and per-node costs may change.
knowledge_statements.title: Node Count Is Not a Runtime Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-level form of the immutable aggregate work equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an optional propagation action at node \(v\) cost \(\Delta P_v\) and eliminate baseline search nodes \(E_v\), whose processing costs are \(c(u)\). Under additive accounting, the action reduces work exactly when \(\Delta P_v<\sum_{u\in E_v}c(u)\), with all downstream costs included consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optional propagation pays when its incremental cost is smaller than the processing cost of the search it prevents.
assumptions_latex: Costs use a common additive resource.
The eliminated baseline nodes and their costs are well defined.

notation.meaning: baseline nodes eliminated by propagation at v

knowledge_statements.title: Amortized Break-Even Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pruning Strength Does Not Imply Runtime Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between logical closure strength and computational performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F_m(s)\subseteq F_\ell(s)\) for every state \(s\), then \(F_m\) leaves no more assignments at the same state. Nevertheless its total runtime may be larger because closure computation, queue maintenance, and repeated execution can outweigh reductions in visited search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger propagator prunes at least as much locally but need not solve faster.
assumptions_latex: Propagator strength is ordered by inclusion of resulting states.
Both propagators are sound.
knowledge_statements.title: Pruning Strength Does Not Imply Runtime Dominance
Propagation–Search Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal work decomposition for choosing a propagation strength before or during search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each available propagation level \(\ell\), let \(P_\ell\) be its total enforcement cost, let \(N_\ell\) be the number of search nodes remaining after its pruning, and let \(C_\ell\) be the mean nonpropagation cost per such node. Under an additive cost model, total work is \(W_\ell=P_\ell+N_\ell C_\ell\). Moving from level \(\ell\) to a stronger level \(m\) improves this model exactly when \(P_m-P_\ell<C_\ell N_\ell-C_mN_m\); extra propagation is justified only when its overhead is smaller than the search work it removes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stronger propagation pays off precisely when its additional enforcement cost is less than the search work eliminated.
assumptions_latex: Propagation and residual search costs are measured in a common additive resource.
\(P_\ell,N_\ell,C_\ell\) are finite nonnegative quantities.

notation.meaning: mean residual cost per search node

review_flags: empirical quantities are solver and instance dependent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebra is correct under the stated additive model and the principle fits the leaf, but the proposed formalization has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected local duplication of the stronger-consistency overhead boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A higher-level propagator may perform \(M\) redundant sound checks while producing the same closure and search tree as a baseline, giving arbitrarily larger work as \(M\) grows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant higher-level checks can make stronger propagation arbitrarily slower without additional pruning.
assumptions_latex: Both procedures terminate and use the same branching choices.
review_flags: The zero-pruning overhead family is canonically owned by Stronger-Consistency Overhead; the local no-dominance conclusion is already covered without duplicating it.
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrarily Bad Stronger Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General semantics independent of a particular estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive consistency policy is a state-dependent map \(\sigma(s)\) selecting at state or search node \(s\) a member of a finite family of sound terminating propagators \(\{F_0,\ldots,F_q\}\), possibly subject to a resource budget. Selection may change inference effort but must preserve the represented solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive consistency chooses a sound propagator from the observed search state without changing the solution set.
assumptions_latex: Every selectable propagator is sound and terminating.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Consistency Policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-dominance boundary of adaptive selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If policy evaluation costs \(A>0\) and all candidate propagators produce the same closures on every encountered state, adaptation removes no additional search node and incurs at least \(A\) extra work relative to retaining the baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all candidate closures coincide, probing and switching are pure overhead.
assumptions_latex: Candidate closures coincide on every encountered state.
Adaptive evaluation incurs positive work.
knowledge_statements.title: Probe and Switching Overhead

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for online switching among propagators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every selected propagator is solution preserving, every speculative trial is restored or soundly committed, and finite branching remains exhaustive, then any history-dependent sequence of propagation choices preserves completeness. Predictor accuracy affects work but not correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary online switching among sound propagators remains complete under exhaustive finite branching.
assumptions_latex: All selected propagation is solution preserving.
Speculative trials are restored or committed soundly.
Branching is finite and exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Adaptive search reports failure only if the original finite CSP is unsatisfiable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Independent Correctness Invariant
Adaptive Consistency Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online selection among sound propagation levels within complete backtracking search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite CSP, an ordered family of sound propagators \(F_0,\ldots,F_q\), an evaluation interval \(h\), and a threshold \(\tau\ge 0\). Run complete backtracking search, initially with \(j=0\). At each search node, apply \(F_j\) to a fixed point; on domain wipeout, backtrack, and on a complete assignment, return that assignment. After each block of \(h\) visited nodes, estimate the marginal pruning gain \(\widehat G_{j+1}\) and marginal cost \(\widehat C_{j+1}\) using restorable trial applications of \(F_{j+1}\). Set \(j\leftarrow j+1\) when \(j<q\) and \(\widehat G_{j+1}/\max\{\widehat C_{j+1},\varepsilon\}>\tau\); otherwise retain \(j\). Return unsatisfiable only after the complete search tree has been exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: During complete backtracking search, periodically activate a stronger sound propagator when its estimated pruning gain per unit cost exceeds a threshold; a failed node causes backtracking, and unsatisfiability is returned only after exhaustive search.
assumptions_latex: Every \(F_j\) is contracting, monotone, terminating, and solution preserving.
The underlying branching procedure is complete.
Trial propagation state can be restored or committed without losing solutions.
\(h>0\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(\tau\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns either a satisfying assignment or, after exhaustive search, a sound unsatisfiability report.
review_flags: algorithmic template rather than a uniquely canonical method
gain estimator and threshold policy require specification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected arbitrary scoring template proposed as a canonical adaptive variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a decision point, estimate \(U_j=\widehat G_j-\lambda\widehat C_j\), discard choices exceeding a budget, and apply a maximizing propagator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probe propagators and choose the eligible one with the largest estimated gain-minus-cost score.
assumptions_latex: Probes are restorable.
The selected propagator is sound.
review_flags: The score, budget, and reevaluation events are arbitrary design choices rather than a standard locally necessary algorithm.
knowledge_statements.title: Budgeted Portfolio Selection

The proposed budgeted gain-minus-cost portfolio is deferred because it is an arbitrary unsourced design, not a canonical required variant. Generic enforcement cost and aggregate propagation–search accounting remain in the sibling leaves.
